Job Title: Procurement AI & Automation Analyst                
Location:  Remote US only
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Ready to build AI solutions that move beyond experimentation and deliver real business impact?  Ingersoll Rand is seeking a hands-on Procurement AI & Automation Analyst to join its Procurement Excellence team, developing and deploying AI-powered applications, intelligent agents, and automated workflows that simplify processes, improve efficiency, and transform how work gets done. In this highly visible role, you'll turn business challenges into practical, working solutions using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, alongside technologies including Snowflake and GitHub.

You'll help expand an existing portfolio of internally developed applications supporting cost-savings tracking and tariff exposure, while exploring new opportunities across supplier scorecards, portals, workflow automation, and broader Procurement and Supply Chain operations. Working across Direct and Indirect Procurement, Logistics, and other business functions, you'll collaborate with stakeholders to identify opportunities, translate business needs into solutions, and help take applications from concept through development, testing, deployment, and adoption. You'll also assume increasing ownership of existing tools, supporting their performance, continuous improvement, and long-term business value. 

This is not a machine-learning research or a traditional software-engineering role. Specific programming languages and deep Procurement expertise are not required. The strongest candidates bring proven hands-on experience using AI-powered development tools to build working applications, agents, or automated workflows that solve real business problems. Equally important are strong communication and problem-solving skills, curiosity, adaptability, and the ability to connect technology with business needs.

If you're excited about building practical AI solutions, seeing your work make a measurable difference, and expanding your experience across AI, automation, business analysis, and solution ownership, we invite you to help shape Ingersoll Rand's growing portfolio of AI-enabled Procurement solutions.

Responsibilities:
Identify and Prioritize AI Opportunities

  • Partner with Strategic Sourcing, Category Management, Procurement Operations, Supply Chain, and Procurement Excellence teams to identify pain points and repeatable work that can be improved with AI or automation.

  • Map end-to-end processes, decisions, data inputs, handoffs, exceptions, and approval points; distinguish what can be automated from what requires human judgment.

  • Maintain a transparent use-case backlog and help prioritize high-volume, repetitive, lower-complexity opportunities with clear business outcomes and manageable risk.

  • Translate business needs into user stories, process requirements, acceptance criteria, and an achievable delivery plan.

Build and Deploy AI Agents, Applications, and Automations

  • Prototype and build solutions using approved generative AI tools, Claude Code or comparable AI-assisted development tools, GitHub, APIs, scripting, data platforms, and low-code/no-code automation tools.

  • Develop prompts, structured outputs, retrieval workflows, business rules, interfaces, and integrations that enable agents to complete defined procurement process steps.

  • Design solutions with appropriate human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception handling, approval logic, and guardrails.

  • Test for accuracy, reliability, security, usability, and business fit; coordinate user acceptance testing and incorporate feedback before release.

  • Deploy, document, and support solutions in a controlled manner, using version control and repeatable release practices.

Own Agent Operations and the Solution Lifecycle

  • Maintain an inventory of active agents and applications, including business owner, purpose, process scope, data sources, prompts or logic, access, dependencies, risk level, and current version.

  • Monitor usage, performance, quality, failures, exceptions, cost, and user feedback; quickly troubleshoot issues and coordinate resolution with technical or business partners.

  • Continuously improve prompts, workflows, integrations, and user experience as business requirements and source data change.

  • Establish practical operating routines for intake, prioritization, testing, release, support, change control, and retirement of outdated solutions.

  • Prevent one-time experiments from becoming unsupported tools by ensuring every production solution has clear ownership, documentation, and measurable outcomes.

Support Responsible AI Governance

  • Partner with IT, Cybersecurity, Data Privacy, Legal, Compliance, and Internal Controls to ensure solutions use approved tools and follow company requirements.

  • Apply appropriate controls for data access, confidential information, auditability, validation, records retention, and human review.

  • Document known limitations, acceptable-use boundaries, escalation paths, and situations in which an AI output must not be used without human verification.

  • Help establish reusable standards, templates, and checklists for procurement AI and automation solutions.

Build Adoption and Procurement AI Skills

  • Create and maintain a procurement-specific library of prompts, playbooks, reusable components, examples, and lessons learned.

  • Deliver short training sessions, demonstrations, office hours, and user guides that help employees apply AI safely in real procurement workflows.

  • Collect feedback, share successful use cases, and make time savings and process improvements visible to encourage adoption.

  • Act as a practical connector between business users and technical teams, communicating clearly with both audiences.

Measure and Communicate Business Impact

  • Build and maintain an AI scorecard that tracks adoption and operating results, not just activity.

  • Track measures such as percentage of the team using approved AI tools, number of workflows automated, number of active agents handling real work, cycle-time or hours saved, accuracy, exception rate, user satisfaction, and financial or risk-reduction value.

  • Provide concise updates on the portfolio, delivery status, risks, lessons learned, and realized benefits to Procurement Excellence leadership and business stakeholders.

  • Use data and user feedback to recommend where to scale, redesign, pause, or retire solutions.

Illustrative Use Cases

  • Examples may include contract review against approved playbooks, supplier discovery and qualification screening, RFP content development, supplier response analysis, bid-comparison support, purchase-request triage, approval routing, renewal-deadline monitoring, category intelligence, and recurring procurement reporting. The role will not be limited to these examples.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience in computer science, information systems, analytics, engineering, supply chain, business, finance, or a related field. 

  • 2 – 3+ years of relevant experience, which may include professional experience, internships, co-ops, academic projects, freelance work, or a demonstrated project portfolio. 

  • 1+ year of hands-on experience using Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build applications, platforms, workflows, or automations; general chat-based LLM use alone is not sufficient. 

  • Experience taking at least one AI-assisted solution from business need or concept through working output, including solution development, iteration, testing, and evaluation of results. 

  • Experience analyzing business processes and translating ambiguous needs into defined requirements, workflows, automation opportunities, or acceptance criteria. 

  • Experience collaborating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including gathering requirements, communicating solutions, incorporating feedback, and adapting to changing technologies or business needs.


Core Competencies

  • AI-Enabled Problem Solving – Identifies practical opportunities to apply AI and automation to business problems and improve processes. 

  • Business & Process Analysis – Breaks down ambiguous workflows, identifies gaps or inefficiencies, and translates needs into clear solution requirements. 

  • Learning Agility & Curiosity – Quickly learns emerging AI tools, technologies, and approaches in a rapidly changing environment. 

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Builds effective working relationships across Procurement, Supply Chain, IT, Legal, Cybersecurity, and other business functions. 

  • Communication & Translation – Effectively translates business needs for technical audiences and technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders. 

  • Ownership & Continuous Improvement – Takes accountability for solutions from concept through deployment, support, measurement, and ongoing enhancement


Preferences:

  • Experience using multiple AI-assisted development platforms or advanced AI development capabilities beyond the minimum required experience. 

  • Exposure to Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Supply Chain, Contract Management, Supplier Management, or Spend Analytics. 

  • Experience with Git/GitHub or other version-control practices. 

  • Experience with Snowflake or another cloud-based data platform. 

  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization/reporting tools. 

  • Experience with low-code/no-code automation or application-development platforms, such as Power Automate, n8n, Zapier, Retool, or Streamlit. 

  • Familiarity with APIs, system integrations, scripting, structured data, or data connections. 

  • Familiarity with agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI evaluation methods, monitoring, and human-in-the-loop design. 

  • Experience supporting or maintaining internally developed applications, workflows, or automation solutions. 

  • Experience conducting user acceptance testing (UAT) and incorporating user feedback. 

  • Experience creating technical/process documentation, user guides, playbooks, or reusable templates. 

  • Experience delivering training, demonstrations, office hours, or change-adoption support.


Travel and Work Arrangements 

  • This is a Remote US based role only and not open to international candidates.

  • Minimal travel (<10%), primarily to suppliers as needed.


Pay Range 
The base pay range for this role is $80,000 - $115,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Plant Controller
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Lead Financial Performance. Help Shape What Comes Next. Join LeROI, an Ingersoll Rand Center of Excellence for gas compression technology, manufacturing compressors and packaged solutions for the Oil & Gas and Biogas industries. We’re seeking an experienced Plant Controller to lead all aspects of plant finance at our Sidney facility during a significant period of growth. With revenue expected to more than double, new product lines planned, and a proposed facility expansion, you’ll help guide growth while strengthening the existing operation.

In this highly visible, hands-on role, you’ll develop the finance team and partner directly with plant leadership, Operations, and Materials to strengthen financial discipline and improve manufacturing performance. You’ll go beyond reporting results to understand what drives them—and turn those insights into action. Strong accounting and manufacturing finance expertise, attention to detail, and sound business judgment will help you identify risks, challenge assumptions, and uphold GAAP, internal controls, and reporting standards. You’ll thrive here with intellectual curiosity, an ownership mindset, and the agility to learn quickly and navigate changing priorities. An experienced Finance Leader who previously held the role will provide hands-on transition guidance.

Help shape the financial direction of a growing manufacturing operation—and expand your leadership impact.

Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Business Partnership:
  • Lead, develop, and manage the Sidney finance team.
  • Serve as the primary financial business partner to plant leadership, providing financial insight and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Commercial, and other functions to drive business performance.
  • Provide clear and actionable analysis of financial results, risks, and opportunities.
  • Support and challenge the organization to achieve financial and operational commitments.
Accounting, Reporting & Controls:
  • Lead the monthly financial close and reporting process, ensuring timely and accurate results.
  • Oversee journal entries, account reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP, SOX requirements, company policies, and internal controls.
  • Lead and coordinate site activities related to internal and external audits.
  • Maintain strong financial controls and proactively identify opportunities to strengthen processes and reduce risk.
Planning & Financial Analysis:
  • Lead development of the facility's Annual Operating Plan (AOP), as well as monthly and quarterly forecasting processes.
  • Analyze financial and operational performance against plan, forecast, and prior periods.
  • Identify key drivers of performance, including manufacturing and plant variances, and partner with operational leaders to understand root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Provide financial modeling and analysis to support business decisions and continuous improvement initiatives.
Cost Accounting & Inventory:
  • Provide leadership and oversight of plant cost accounting activities.
  • Lead the annual standard cost process and ensure accurate product costing.
  • Establish standard costs for new parts and review proposed cost changes for existing products.
  • Monitor and analyze material, labor, overhead, purchase price, and other manufacturing variances.
  • Lead quarterly excess and obsolete inventory reviews and work with cross-functional teams to proactively manage inventory exposure.
Capital & Asset Management:
  • Provide financial oversight of capital expenditures, including business case analysis, spending controls, and project tracking.
  • Oversee fixed asset accounting and ensure appropriate capitalization and asset controls.
  • Partner with plant leadership to prioritize investments and evaluate financial returns.
Continuous Improvement:
  • Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, reporting, controls, and business intelligence.
  • Drive standardization, simplification, and automation where appropriate.
  • Support ad-hoc financial analysis and business initiatives as needed.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 7+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including increasing responsibility for month-end close, financial reporting, U.S. GAAP compliance, and internal controls.
  • 3+ years of accounting or finance experience in a plant or manufacturing environment, including direct partnership with Operations, Materials, Production, or Supply Chain.
  • 3+ years of experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and variance analysis, supported by advanced Microsoft Excel skills, such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, complex formulas, financial modeling, and analysis of large financial data sets.
  • 1+ year of practical manufacturing cost-accounting experience, including working knowledge of standard costs and manufacturing, production, inventory, or purchase price variances.
  • 1+ year of demonstrated leadership experience through direct supervision, people management, team leadership, or leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.

Core Competencies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Ability to communicate financial concepts to financial and non-financial audiences
  • Cross-functional relationship building and influence
  • Ability to manage competing priorities
  • Learning agility and comfort with ambiguity
  • Sound business judgment and professional courage
  • Ability to challenge business decisions appropriately when they conflict with U.S. GAAP or internal controls

Preferences:
  • Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Professional certification such as CPA or CMA.
  • Experience with SAP.
  • Experience with Hyperion (Forecasting sys) or similar financial consolidation and reporting systems.

Travel and Work Arrangements:
  • This position is based onsite in Sidney, OH.
The pay range for this role, excluding incentive opportunities, is a base of $120,000 - $140,00 annually. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation. 

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What we Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Job Title: Service Supervisor, Commercial Compressed Air
Location: Northern Indiana (South Bend, Fort Wayne, Goshen)

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor in the compressed air commercial segment is responsible for leading the local service function for the full life cycle of the equipment to achieve exceptional customer satisfaction. This encompasses supporting the sales team to grow the business, collaborating with service coordination, and managing a Service Technician team that installs, repairs and maintains all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating air compressors and compressed air system components. The Service Supervisor also has responsibility for the Service P&L for their Customer Center.

Responsibilities: 
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 5+ years of relevant services experience, ideally in an industrial sales business environment.
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Associate's or Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes 

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybrid from Northern Indiana, IN (South Bend, Fort Wayne, Goshen)
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Base Salary with bonus incentives
  • Regional travel approximately 20% to customer sites 
This position will have some work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms, will include physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Job Title:  Field Service Technician, Electromechanical
Location: Blandon, PA  (Hybrid with travel)

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, a proud Ingersoll Rand brand, has been a powerhouse in engineered air solutions delivering decades of proven performance, reliability, and innovation. Backed by a legacy of excellence, we’re trusted across industries for systems that perform under pressure and consistently exceed expectations.  We’re looking for a hands-on Field Service Technician who thrives in the field and takes pride in keeping critical equipment running at peak performance. In this role, you’ll be the expert customers rely on—installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing Ingersoll Rand positive displacement (PD) blower systems, including controls and VFDs, directly at customer sites. You’ll play a vital role in delivering responsive, high-impact service that supports customers’ operational needs.  
Your work won’t stop in the field. You’ll also install controls and wiring for PD blower systems at our facility, applying your electromechanical expertise across the full equipment lifecycle. If you already bring PD blower experience, you’ll hit the ground running. If not, you bring a strong foundation in rotating equipment, motor and electrical troubleshooting, alignment, system-level diagnostics, and reading schematics and P&IDs—and the drive to master the rest. This is a role for someone who enjoys solving real-world problems, working independently, and making a visible impact every day. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Install, commission, and start up positive displacement (PD) blower packages, vacuum/pressure systems, and associated rotating equipment per OEM specifications and site requirements.

  • Configure, program, and troubleshoot variable frequency drives (VFDs) and soft starters (parameter setup, PID loops, accel/decel profiles, motor protection, fieldbus/communication interfaces such as Modbus/TCP, EtherNet/IP).

  • Diagnose and repair electrical controls including relays, contactors, motor starters, overloads, interlocks, safety circuits, and control transformers.

  • Perform control panel wiring and field terminations (24 VDC control, 120/480 VAC power, grounding/bonding, signal wiring, shielded cable practices); read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Install and integrate instrumentation (pressure, temperature, vibration, flow, differential pressure transmitters, proximity sensors, limit switches) and calibrate as required.

  • Execute mechanical service tasks (coupling alignment—laser or dial, belt tensioning, blower timing, bearing replacement, seal changes, lubrication, fastener torque verification).

  • Conduct vibration and performance checks; identify root cause of abnormal noise, heat, vibration, or amperage draw (airflow restrictions, leaks, misalignment, cavitation, resonance).

  • Troubleshoot system issues end-to-end across electrical, mechanical, and controls, including motor diagnostics (insulation resistance, megger testing, continuity), VFD/motor matching, and load-related faults.

  • Perform field measurements and documentation (voltage/current, phase balance, harmonics, airflow/pressure, vibration readings) and produce detailed service reports with parts lists and recommended follow-up.

Requirements:

  • High School diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant / equivalent technical experience: millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service.
  • 2+ years of electromechanical experience

Core Competencies

  • Strong electromechanical troubleshooting skills, including rotating equipment such as motors, gearboxes, compressors, mixers, blowers, and pumps; electronic power conversion (AC to DC) and related faults/alarms (GF, OC, OV, UV, OL, OH); and PLC troubleshooting, including I/O, hardware, and software checks.
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, employees, and Sales Representatives.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues, resolve conflicts, make sound decisions, and appropriately escalate problems in dynamic environments.
  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Valid driver’s license held for at least 12 months with a satisfactory driving record. No major or frequent violations, including DUI within the past 5 years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple minor violations/preventable collisions within the past 3 years.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is 40% onsite shop repairs and up to 60% travel for field work
  • Possible minimal travel to Canada, Puerto Rico, and/or Mexico
  • Paid travel time at full hourly rate
  • Company vehicle and gas provided

Job Overview
The Service Coordinator supports the Customer Center by coordinating service technicians and delivering responsive customer service to industrial customers with compressed-air equipment. Working closely with Service, Sales, and Operations, the Service Coordinator helps ensure technicians have the parts, information, and scheduling support needed to meet customer needs. This role also supports service inventory, rental equipment, warranty claims, and accurate documentation.

Responsibilities

Job Overview:
At Ingersoll Rand’s Monroe, Louisiana facility, precision-engineered products play a critical role in equipment customers depend on every day. The site manufactures and services THOMAS air compressor and vacuum pump products within an OEM portfolio serving medical, laboratory, environmental, and industrial markets. In this hands-on manufacturing environment, quality is measured not just by what leaves the line, but by how reliably the product performs for the customer—creating a meaningful opportunity to strengthen processes, systems, and overall plant performance.

We’re seeking a Quality Engineer who is a hands-on individual contributor focused on strengthening quality performance across the Monroe facility by turning quality challenges into sustainable process improvements. Rather than simply reacting to defects, this engineer will look at quality through the customer’s eyes—identifying trends, uncovering root causes, and building the processes, standards, controls, and corrective actions that prevent issues from recurring.  Partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Production, Customer Service, and Supply Chain, this role will apply proven manufacturing quality practices—including process controls, quality metrics, and customer-focused problem solving—to improve process capability, reduce cost of poor quality, address customer complaints and returns, and strengthen overall product performance.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on manufacturing quality experience, can quickly understand the operation, and is comfortable taking ownership and driving improvements with a high degree of independence. This is an opportunity for a builder—not simply a maintainer: someone energized by improving what exists, creating what is missing, and helping establish stronger, more sustainable quality practices as the operation continues to grow.

Responsibilities:
  • Lead investigations of customer complaints, warranty issues, and internal concfomromances using structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, 5 Why, Fishbone, and PFMEA, implementing effective corrective and preventative actions. 
  • Support and continuously improve the site's Quality Management System, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001 and applicable company quality standards.
  • Conduct internal process audits, support customer and certification audits, and drive timely resolution of findings.
  • Analyze quality, manufacturing, inspection, and warranty data to identify trends, reduce defects, minimize scrap and rework, and improve operational performance.
  • Develop and maintain quality planning and validation documentation, including PPAPs, Process Flow Diagrams, PFMEAs, Control Plans, Measurement System Analyses (MSA), and Process Capability Studies.
  • Support process validation and qualification activities, including IQ, OQ, and PQ protocols where applicable.
  • Collaborate with Engineering and Manufacturing teams to develop process controls, improve product quality, and ensure customer requirements are met.
  • Provide quality-related training and guidance, promote continuous improvement initiatives, and participate in Kaizen and operational excellence activities.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing quality, quality engineering, or a related technical role within a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of experience applying root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies to investigate and resolve manufacturing or product quality issues.
  • 2+ years of experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including internal audits, corrective actions, or quality-system compliance activities.
  • 3+ years of experience analyzing manufacturing or quality data to identify trends, process issues, or improvement opportunities and communicating findings and recommended actions to manufacturing, engineering, or operations teams.

Core Competencies 
  • Continuous Improvement Mindset – Looks beyond immediate fixes to identify opportunities for sustainable process, product, and quality improvement. 
  • Analytical Problem Solving – Uses data, quality metrics, root cause analysis, and sound judgment to identify issues, evaluate trends, and develop effective solutions. 
  • Customer Focus – Evaluates quality through the customer’s perspective and takes action to improve product performance, reliability, and overall customer satisfaction.
  • Ownership & Follow-Through – Takes personal accountability for commitments, respects deadlines, drives actions to completion, and operates effectively without constant direction.
  • Collaboration & Influence – Builds productive relationships across Engineering, Operations, Production, Supply Chain, and other functions to resolve issues and advance quality initiatives.
  • Quality & Compliance Excellence – Maintains high standards for quality, process discipline, documentation, and compliance while supporting effective quality management systems.

Preferences: 
  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or similar quality certification.
  • Experience with PPAP, PFMEA, MSA, SPC, and Process Capability Studies.
  • Experience supporting ISO 9001 certified manufacturing environments.
  • Working knowledge of GD&T, blueprint reading, and metrology systems.
  • Experience in machining, assembly, pump manufacturing, or other industrial manufacturing environments.

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • This position is fully site-based at the Monroe, Louisiana manufacturing facility. 
  • Occasional travel may be required to support customer audits, supplier visits, training, or other business needs.

What We Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:

The Project Engineer is a key member of the project management team and the primary technical point of contact for customers during execution of complex ETO centrifugal compressors. This role turns contractual and customer requirements into a clear, executable technical plan while coordinating engineering, manufacturing, quality, sourcing, vendors, and project management.

Success in this position requires strong technical judgment, disciplined follow-through, commercial awareness, and the ability to communicate complex information clearly. The Project Engineer maintains visibility to scope, schedule, documentation, risk, change, and project financial health throughout the contract lifecycle.

 

Key Responsibilities:

Lead technical project execution:

· Review purchase orders, customer specifications, clarifications, deviations, and internal order documentation to confirm that contract requirements are complete, accurate, and understood before execution.

· Own the technical handoff from order acceptance through shipment, helping the project team translate scope into deliverables, decisions, actions, and milestones.

· Monitor technical execution against the project schedule, identify risks or slippage early, and coordinate recovery actions with the Project Manager and functional teams.

Serve as the customer technical liaison:

· Act as the primary technical contact for assigned projects and provide clear, timely communication on requirements, submittals, open items, decisions, and status.

· Lead technical discussions to resolve questions, align expectations, and document decisions while maintaining awareness of contractual commitments.

· Issue customer-facing technical documentation and provide regular schedule updates in coordination with the Project Manager.

Manage scope, change, and project risk:

· Monitor scope throughout execution, including customer comments, specification changes, and drawing markups; identify potential scope growth and escalate it promptly.

· Partner with the Project Manager to evaluate the technical, cost, and schedule impacts of customer change requests and support development of change orders.

· Maintain accurate action, risk, and decision records so accountability and due dates remain clear.

Drive documentation, quality, and delivery readiness:

· Coordinate the preparation, review, and transmittal of contract documents, including drawings, data sheets, test reports, manuals, and project-specific technical documentation.

· Create and maintain the Inspection and Test Plan (ITP), coordinate customer witness and hold points, and support inspections and performance testing.

· Partner with Quality on pre-shipment inspection and customer coordination.

· Support revenue-recognition activities by helping confirm completion of applicable technical and contractual milestones.

Provide technical product support:

· Apply working knowledge of centrifugal compressors and associated systems, including gearboxes, lubrication systems, intercoolers, controls, motors or drivers, and auxiliary equipment.

· Review major buyout and supplier documentation for alignment with project requirements.

· Provide technical support for proposals, field questions, troubleshooting, and post-shipment activities when needed.


Required Qualifications:

· Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Chemical Engineering.

· 3-5 years of relevant experience in an industrial, manufacturing, or engineered-to-order environment.

 

Core Competencies:

· Understanding of engineering, manufacturing, inspection, testing, and supplier processes. General knowledge of centrifugal compressor systems is strongly preferred.

· Ability to manage multiple deliverables, priorities, interfaces, and deadlines in a technical project environment.

· Clear written and verbal communication with customers, suppliers, and cross-functional teams; able to build trusted working relationships.

· Accountable, organized, proactive, collaborative, and detail-oriented, with sound judgment and a commitment to quality.

 

Tools and systems:

· Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications. Experience with scheduling, spreadsheet, collaboration, and document-control tools is expected.

· Experience with ERP and business systems such as SAP or Oracle is preferred.

· Experience reading engineering drawings and specifications is required; 3D modeling or drafting experience is a plus.

 

How success is demonstrated:

· Contract requirements are translated into complete, accurate, and actionable technical direction.

  • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.

  • Strong ability to create, maintain, and manage quality-related documentation, including process controls, inspection logs, visual work instructions, ECNs, and corrective action records, while utilizing MS Office, Excel, and ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
•In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. 
•Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
•Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
•Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
•Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.

Requirements:
•2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
•Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
•Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
•This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
•High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Core Competencies:
•Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
•Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
•Basic vibration troubleshooting.
•Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
•Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
•Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner

Preferences:
•Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
•EPA Certification.
•Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
•Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
•A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Location:  Sedalia, MO (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a Quality Engineer role with Gardner Denver – Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, a division of Ingersoll Rand, where your work directly impacts product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia operation. You’ll help ensure products meet exacting quality standards while supporting the transformation of metal castings and raw materials into high-performing products used around the world.  In this highly collaborative role, you’ll serve as a key problem-solving partner across manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, and purchasing. Using the plant Quality Management System, you’ll respond to quality issues, lead root cause analysis, identify risks, and drive corrective and preventive actions that strengthen product reliability, reduce defects, and support continuous improvement across the plant.

Responsibilities: 
  • Process Development and Improvement: Develop, implement, and document process improvements to ensure quality and reliability. Quality project lead representative, as assigned, for new product introductions. Identifies production concerns and take proactive steps to correct problems. 
  • Documentation: Initiates and maintains documentation as needed to support process and manufacturing improvements (i.e. Process Control, Inspection logs, Visual Work Instructions, ECN's) 
  • Quality: Develops and maintains all departmental procedures supporting and maintaining ISO certification. Participate in internal and external periodic plant audits. Support plant internal corrective actions. 
  • Suppliers: Respond/ investigate quality related issues found on the production floor, or at the customer's location. Communicate with suppliers on non-conforming material, and issue/ manage supplier corrective actions as necessary. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or directed. 

Requirements:
  • 5+ years of relevant progressive quality experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.
  • 3+ years of relevant quality experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years experience with MS Office Suite, to include intermediate Excel skills
  • 1+ year of experience working with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Core Competencies:
  • Quality Systems & Compliance
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, maintain, and support quality procedures, documentation, and plant-level quality systems in alignment with ISO certification, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Structured Problem Solving & Root Cause Analysis
  • Ability to respond to quality issues as they occur, investigate non-conformances, apply root cause analysis tools, and drive corrective and preventive actions that improve product reliability and reduce defects.
  • Process Improvement & Manufacturing Support
  • Experience identifying production concerns, developing and documenting process improvements, and partnering with manufacturing teams to strengthen quality, reliability, and operational performance.
  • Cross-Functional & Supplier Collaboration
  • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.
  • Documentation, Data & Systems Proficiency
  • Strong ability to create, maintain, and manage quality-related documentation, including process controls, inspection logs, visual work instructions, ECNs, and corrective action records, while utilizing MS Office, Excel, and ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors Degree or some college with relevant quality engineering experience
  • Experience with Lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives
  • ASQ certification (e.g., CQT, CQE, CQM, or CRE)
  • Six Sigma Green Belt certification

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Travel anticipated is less than 10%

Job Title: Area Service Leader 
Location: City of Industry, CA

About Us:
 Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

Job Overview:
 The Area Service Leader position is responsible for providing the leadership for all service activities from the installation of new equipment to the implementation of a services contract through lifetime connectivity with that customer.  Processes within that oversight include support of sales through contract pricing on parts and service, field service coordination, management of technicians and service supervisors, customer satisfaction, and responsibility for the revenue and margin of the parts and service business within the geography.  Provides strategy for connectivity and services growth within the defined region. This position is responsible for service growth for office locations within the West Region (Southern California, Arizona & Nevada).   

Responsibilities:

  • Accountable for full services portfolio performance. 
  • Ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately balanced to service customers, and leverage resources across the area.  This includes emergency repair (break/fix), regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components (parts), and long-term service agreements (Package Care).  
  • Collaborate with the Operations Leader to ensure service coordination processes/functions are aligned with service objectives. 
  • Collaborate with sales on contract pricing of parts and services to maintain and enhance profitable service operations. 
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, and develop all service employees.
  •  Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available.
  • Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process and technical skills, to the highest degree possible.    
  • Proactively build the technician and service supervisor pipeline (internally and externally) and strategically manage your workforce to prevent resource gaps. 
  •  Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team.  
  • Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure a safe and productive work environment both in the shop and at customer sites.  
  • Visit customers on a regular basis to build relationships and provide solutions.  
Requirements:
  • 5+ years of experience in industrial product space, preferably with a diverse product portfolio including service offerings.   
  • 3+ years’ management experience, preferably in a customer-facing environment.
Core Competencies:
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. 
  • Leadership skills are essential.
  • Must be able to manage an hourly technical workforce, including remote employees, as well as salaried staff.   
  • Work is completed through other employees, so this person must excel at hiring, developing, training, coaching, leading and motivating a diverse workforce for optimal results.  
  • Profit & Loss experience is critical
  • Must have experience in forecasting needs, obtaining resources, and managing budgets.
  • Collaborate and partner with the Regional Director in creation of a strategic business plan for growing the service business through internal process improvements and lean strategies to positively impact our market position.
Preferences:
  • Technical and/or mechanical capabilities are a plus.
  • Bachelor’s Degree  in related discipline; Engineering, Technical, Marketing or Business preferred. 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • This position will be based out of one of the West region area customer centers with regional and overnight, out of town travel required (45-70%). 
     

The Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $130,000 - $170,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicants will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Schedule: Monday - Friday, 7:30 AM - 4:30 PM

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
•In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. 
•Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
•Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
•Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
•Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.

Requirements:
•2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
•Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
•Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
•This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
•High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Core Competencies:
•Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
•Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
•Basic vibration troubleshooting.
•Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
•Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
•Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner

Preferences:
•Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
•EPA Certification.
•Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
•Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
•A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range: 
•The pay range for this role is $25.00 - $40.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond.

Job Title: Mechanical Inside Sales Support Specialist

Location: On-site, Lincolnshire, Illinois 

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Welch Vacuum, a subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand since 1996, is a global leader with over a century of history in high-performance vacuum technologies. We specialize in vacuum pumps, systems, and components for laboratories, life sciences, and industrial manufacturing. Operating within Ingersoll Rand's medical and laboratory division, we combine the engineering strengths of US-based Welch Vacuum Technology and Germany's Ilmvac GmbH.

The Mechanical Inside Sales Support Specialist provides technical, commercial, and operational support for vacuum pump products and systems. This role serves as a trusted advisor to customers, distribution partners, and internal sales teams by delivering application expertise, product recommendations, troubleshooting assistance, and sales enablement activities that drive customer satisfaction, customer retention, and profitable growth. The position combines strong technical knowledge of mechanical systems and vacuum pump technologies with exceptional customer service and commercial acumen.

Responsibilities:

  • The Mechanical Inside Sales Support Specialist will diagnose and resolve product, installation, operational, service, and warranty-related issues, primarily through phone and Microsoft Teams interactions.
  • You will apply strong problem-solving skills, collaborate effectively across internal teams, and deliver a best-in-class customer experience throughout the post-sales lifecycle.
  • Provide technical guidance, application support, and troubleshooting assistance for customers, distribution partners, and internal sales teams, primarily via phone and Microsoft Teams. 
  • Diagnose product and system issues, identify root causes, and coordinate corrective actions to ensure timely and effective resolution. 
  • Support customers with equipment setup, operation, maintenance, service, warranty claims, and other post-sales technical inquiries. 
  • Serve as the primary liaison between customers and internal teams, including Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Product Management, and Customer Service, to ensure prompt resolution of customer concerns. 
  • Prepare accurate quotations, product specifications, technical recommendations. 
  • Identify and develop cross-sell, upsell, replacement, and new application opportunities through customer interactions and technical consultations. 
  • Build and maintain strong customer relationships that enhance customer loyalty and satisfaction. 
  • Partner with distribution channels to provide product training, technical support, and application expertise that drives business growth. 
  • Maintain current knowledge of vacuum technologies, product offerings, competitive solutions, and industry trends. 
  • Document and communicate customer feedback, technical issues, and market intelligence to support continuous product and process improvement to engineering and product management.  
  • Acts as backup to customer Service reps by supporting order management activities, including order tracking, issue resolution, and customer communication. 
  • Demonstrate strategic agility by performing additional duties and responsibilities as assigned to support evolving business priorities. 


Requirements:

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Industrial Technology, Mechanical Technology, or a related technical discipline; equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered. 
  • 2+ years of experience troubleshooting and resolving mechanical equipment issues in an industrial or technical environment; ability to analyze mechanical problems, identify root causes, and implement effective corrective actions.


Core Competencies:
Technical Expertise 

  • Strong mechanical troubleshooting and diagnostic skills. 
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, controls, and industrial equipment. 
  • Ability to evaluate customer applications, interpret technical requirements, perform basic equipment performance calculations, and recommend effective solutions. 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and CRM systems; Salesforce experience preferred. 


Customer & Commercial Acumen 

  • Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills. 
  • Ability to establish credibility and develop strong relationships with customers, channel partners, and internal stakeholders. 
  • Demonstrated business and sales acumen, including opportunity identification, account development, value-based selling, and competitive account conversion. 
  • Customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering exceptional service and support. 


Problem Solving & Collaboration 

  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to resolve complex technical challenges. 
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and organizational levels. 
  • Able to work independently while contributing positively within a team environment. 
  • High level of integrity, professionalism, and accountability. 


Organization & Execution 

  • Exceptional organizational and multitasking skills with strong attention to detail. 
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects and customer requests in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Strong follow-through and commitment to delivering timely, accurate results. 
  • Self-motivated, results-oriented professional with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. 


Preferences:

  • 5+ years of experience troubleshooting and resolving mechanical equipment issues in an industrial or technical environment. 
  • Experience with vacuum pump technologies, vacuum systems, or related industrial equipment preferred. 
  • Electrical troubleshooting experience is a plus. 


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based, approx. 10% domestic travel

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Step into a Quality Engineer role with Gardner Denver – Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, a division of Ingersoll Rand, where your work directly impacts product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia operation. You’ll help ensure products meet exacting quality standards while supporting the transformation of metal castings and raw materials into high-performing products used around the world.  In this highly collaborative role, you’ll serve as a key problem-solving partner across manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, and purchasing. Using the plant Quality Management System, you’ll respond to quality issues, lead root cause analysis, identify risks, and drive corrective and preventive actions that strengthen product reliability, reduce defects, and support continuous improvement across the plant.

Responsibilities: 
  • Process Development and Improvement: Develop, implement, and document process improvements to ensure quality and reliability. Quality project lead representative, as assigned, for new product introductions. Identifies production concerns and take proactive steps to correct problems. 
  • Documentation: Initiates and maintains documentation as needed to support process and manufacturing improvements (i.e. Process Control, Inspection logs, Visual Work Instructions, ECN's) 
  • Quality: Develops and maintains all departmental procedures supporting and maintaining ISO certification. Participate in internal and external periodic plant audits. Support plant internal corrective actions. 
  • Suppliers: Respond/ investigate quality related issues found on the production floor, or at the customer's location. Communicate with suppliers on non-conforming material, and issue/ manage supplier corrective actions as necessary. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or directed. 

Requirements:
  • 5+ years of relevant progressive quality experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.
  • 3+ years of relevant quality experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years experience with MS Office Suite, to include intermediate Excel skills
  • 1+ year of experience working with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Core Competencies:
  • Quality Systems & Compliance
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, maintain, and support quality procedures, documentation, and plant-level quality systems in alignment with ISO certification, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Structured Problem Solving & Root Cause Analysis
  • Ability to respond to quality issues as they occur, investigate non-conformances, apply root cause analysis tools, and drive corrective and preventive actions that improve product reliability and reduce defects.
  • Process Improvement & Manufacturing Support
  • Experience identifying production concerns, developing and documenting process improvements, and partnering with manufacturing teams to strengthen quality, reliability, and operational performance.
  • Cross-Functional & Supplier Collaboration
  • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.
  • Documentation, Data & Systems Proficiency
  • Strong ability to create, maintain, and manage quality-related documentation, including process controls, inspection logs, visual work instructions, ECNs, and corrective action records, while utilizing MS Office, Excel, and ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors Degree or some college with relevant quality engineering experience
  • Experience with Lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives
  • ASQ certification (e.g., CQT, CQE, CQM, or CRE)
  • Six Sigma Green Belt certification

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Travel anticipated is less than 10%
