Job Overview: 

The Material Planner (Buyer) plays a vital role in ensuring timely delivery of materials to support production operations by managing material planning activities from placing purchase orders, follow up with suppliers to deliver product to production assembly lines and/or service parts.  Has a direct impact on ensuring the plant has access to the inputs, materials, goods, and services it needs for its current and future operations.  Plans for engineering change and coordinates into production when appropriate. Provides other support for production and management as required. 

Responsibilities:

  • Perform timely, cost-conscious procurement of production/inventory/MRO items. 
  • Receive and analyze requisitions to determine quantity, specifications, and delivery requirements. 
  • From approved supplier list, recommend and select suppliers to fulfill scheduled plant deliveries. 
  • Responsible for the onboarding of newly selected suppliers related to material planning. 
  • Ensure optimal inventory levels and safety stock are maintained for their parts. 
  • Ensure that Exception Messages (Expedites/De-Expedites/Cancels) are managed regularly and consistently to ensure that the delivery and inventory needs of the business are met. 
  • Ensure that all Procedures relating to PO approvals / LOA / documentation/archiving are followed. 
  • Coordinate with Quality Assurance to resolve quality issues with suppliers. 
  • Maintain proactive shortage identification and management - help flag root causes & corrective actions. 
  • Identify total cost and cash flow opportunities with suppliers. 
  • Analyze and select parts for Kanban and Supplier replenishment.

Job Overview
Serve as the senior Engineering design resource responsible for advanced CAD development, technical drafting leadership, drawing quality, modeling standards, and mentorship of junior designers. Supports engineering teams through development of complex products, design documentation, and implementation of best practices across the organization. 

The Designer III (CAD) is a senior-level design professional with extensive experience in mechanical and electromechanical product development. This role independently develops complex design solutions, establishes drafting standards, mentors junior designers, and serves as a key technical resource for engineers, manufacturing, quality, and sourcing teams. 

The Designer III (CAD) possesses deep expertise in CAD systems, GD&T application, manufacturing processes, tolerance analysis, and design documentation. This role operates with minimal supervision and often acts as the lead designer on major projects. 

Responsibilities
  • Lead CAD development activities for complex pump and electromechanical products. 
  • Create and review sophisticated assemblies, layouts, and manufacturing drawings. 
  • Establish and maintain CAD modeling standards and drafting practices. 
  • Ensure compliance with ISO GPS or ANSI Y14.5 and applicable international drawing standards. 
  • Lead drawing quality audits and documentation improvement initiatives. 
  • Perform tolerance stack-up analysis and manufacturability reviews. 
  • Develop advanced assembly structures and configuration management approaches. 
  • Support new product development, sustaining engineering, and custom engineering projects. 
  • Collaborate closely with engineers during concept development and product architecture activities. 
  • Provide design support for testing, validation, certification, and supplier qualification activities. 
  • Lead design reviews focused on manufacturability, assembly, serviceability, and cost. 
  • Mentor and train Designer I and Designer II personnel. 
  • Support implementation of PDM/PLM best practices. 
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to CAD efficiency, drawing quality, and documentation processes. 
  • Serve as technical reviewer and approver for drawings and models where authorized. 
  • Support supplier technical reviews and manufacturing problem resolution.

  • This position requires access to export-controlled information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Applicants must be a U.S. person as defined by 22 CFR § 120.62, which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees. Applicants who do not meet this requirement cannot be considered for this position. 
  • Associate degree or Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Design, Drafting Technology, Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline. 
  • 8+ years of progressively responsible CAD design and mechanical drafting experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience in electromechanical product design. 
  • 3+ years of experience leading complex design documentation efforts. 
  • 3+ years of experience serving as technical mentor to designers and engineering support personnel. 
  • Solidworks Professional Administrator CPAP, or 5+ years of equivalent experience PDM Admin 

Core Competencies
  • Experience managing Engineering Changes and the Change process 
  • Strong technical and mathematical skills. 
  • Supporting industrial products, pumps, fluid handling equipment 
  • Expert-level SolidWorks or equivalent CAD proficiency. 
  • Advanced GD&T knowledge and application. 
  • Advanced understanding of machining, molding, fabrication, casting, assembly, and manufacturing processes. 
  • Strong understanding of pumps, motors, fluid systems, and industrial products. 
  • Advanced tolerance stack-up knowledge. 
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills. 
  • Ability to mentor others and lead technical initiatives. 
  • Excellent documentation and communication skills. 
  • Strong understanding of PDM and PLM systems. 
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities with minimal supervision. 
  • Continuous learning mindset to keep up with evolving technologies. 
  • Excellent mechanical comprehension with the ability to understand, describe, or discuss problems of a technical nature. 
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively. 
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills 
  • Ability to direct and work effectively through others and be a participative team player 

Preference
  • Experience with global drawing standards and manufacturing environments preferred. 
  • Working knowledge of Syteline 10 ERP

  • Prefer Residency in Midwest near a Major Airport 
  • Fully Remote with some occasional travel - less than 25% - to US facilities

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
•In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. 
•Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
•Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
•Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
•Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.

Requirements:
•2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
•Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
•Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
•This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
•High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Core Competencies:
•Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
•Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
•Basic vibration troubleshooting.
•Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
•Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
•Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner

Preferences:
•Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
•EPA Certification.
•Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
•Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
•A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range: 
•The pay range for this role is $25.00 - $40.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. 

What We Offer:
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Job Overview

Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Electrical Controls Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role designs, develops, tests, and supports PLC-based industrial control systems, including HMI and SCADA applications, for blowers, compressors, and associated equipment.

The Electrical Controls Engineer manages assigned controls software projects from requirements definition and design through programming, testing, and customer-site startup. This position works directly with customers and engineering teams to deliver safe, reliable, and maintainable solutions while independently managing assigned work with minimal oversight.

Responsibilities

  • Translate customer and project requirements into control software solutions, control narratives, and system design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain PLC programs, HMI/SCADA applications, and equipment control strategies.
  • Manage assigned controls software projects from requirements and design through implementation, testing, and optimization.
  • Develop and execute software validation and acceptance testing, including customer-facing Factory Acceptance Testing and Site Acceptance Testing.
  • Support customer-site startup, commissioning, equipment tuning, and troubleshooting.
  • Maintain software revisions, reusable code, change records, and technical documentation.
  • Collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams, communicate progress and risks, and improve control software reliability and maintainability.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.
  • 2+ years of experience in industrial automation, controls engineering, or control system software development.
  • 2+ years of Hands-on experience with one or more PLC platforms, including Rockwell Automation, Siemens, Phoenix Contact, or Schneider Electric.
Core Competencies 
  • Proficiency in Structured Text programming, Ladder Logic and Function Block Diagram programming.
  • Knowledge of control system fundamentals, PLC hardware, industrial instrumentation, analog and digital I/O, actuators, and VFD/motor control.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, P&IDs, control panel drawings, and network architecture documentation.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to gather requirements, develop technical solutions, and work directly with customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to independently manage assigned projects, prioritize work, and meet deadlines.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred experience

  • HMI and SCADA development experience.
  • Customer-facing Factory Acceptance Testing and Site Acceptance Testing.
  • Industrial equipment startup, commissioning, and tuning.
  • Modular programming, reusable code, user-defined data types, and software change management.
  • Electrical control panel design fundamentals.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Willingness and ability to travel to customer sites for startup, commissioning, and technical support.

Job Overview: 
This position involves building multiple new construction models along with the teardown, evaluation and repair of used equipment.  Products consist of various tank mounted systems, priming valves, and commercial pumps.  Product assembly requires the setting of heavy equipment on fabricated metal tanks to exacting tolerances.  Product assembly for some models includes making sub level components / assemblies.

 

Responsibilities: 

  •  Assemble units consisting of pumps, motors, exchangers, separators, and piping from engineering schematics, procedures, and detailed prints.
  • Conduct required acceptance testing for assembled product hydro test, vacuum test, performance test, sound test, others test as requested.
  • Assemble various products as required by the customer including pumps, compressors, exhausters, priming valves, and systems. Receive and inspect returned pumps and systems, complete a tear down and evaluation.
  •  Access computer files containing available assembly instructions follow assembly steps to build final assembly that conforms to Nash and its customers' requirements.
  • Read shop packet, pull and pick parts in SAP Warehouse Management, record required part information per job requirements and quality control documentation.  
  • Provide detailed tear down and evaluation reports; identifying the condition of each component, the recommended disposition of each component submit completed tear down reports with detailed descriptions and pictures to provide a basis for repair cost quotation to the customer.
  • Assist in receiving process as needed; measure components to affirm dimensional compliance.
  • Participate in government inspections and audit, as necessary.
  •  Complete hydro testing on incoming parts using fixtures, develop fixture when one is not available. Operate crane and fork truck in order to move equipment to specific areas. Operate machinery and hand tools per their intended purpose. Conduct Cycle Counts.
  •  Follow all safety rules, environmental regulating procedures and utilize required safety equipment when appropriate.

 

Requirements: 

  •  High School Diploma or GED 
  • Must be US Citizen and be able to obtain US Government Security clearances within 6 months of hire.  
  • 1+ years of experience in Blueprint Reading

 

Core Competencies: 

  •  Knowledge of piping systems such as threaded, flanged, socket weld and butt weld fittings.
  •  Ability to conduct visual inspection of components and systems • Ability to hear very slight noise and differentiate the source of the noise
  • Follow instructions from various sources, resolving conflicts through supervision.
  • Ability to identify when there is a need to report suspicious activity.
  • Experience with parts inspection, measuring, and machining is preferred.
  • Ability to lift and maneuverer 50 pounds.

 

Preferences: 
• US Navy or other military background 
• 3+ years experience in setting of heavy equipment, assembly and pipefitting. • Familiar with and ability to utilize all hand tools including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, and steel banding. 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Bentleyville, PA no travel.

Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $27.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Overview:

The Shipping & Receiving Associate performs a variety of shipping, receiving, inventory control, and material handling functions in support of manufacturing operations. Assignments may include parts picking and packing, inbound receiving, inventory transactions, fork truck operation, painting for shipment, and custom crating for LTL freight, based on operational needs.

This role requires strong attention to detail, accuracy, accountability, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision while supporting inventory accuracy, production flow, and on-time shipment of products.

Responsibilities:

(Assigned based on operational need; employees may be reassigned between functions)

Receiving – Incoming Receiving Clerk

  • Receive incoming materials against purchase orders and packing lists
  • Verify part numbers, quantities, and condition of received materials
  • Perform ERP receiving transactions and assign inventory locations accurately
  • Ensure received materials are delivered to the correct location or personnel
  • Work with Purchasing and other departments to resolve receiving discrepancies
  • Support receipt of outside process parts and finished goods

Receiving – Fork Truck Driver / Inventory Control

  • Operate fork trucks or manually move materials to assigned storage locations
  • Put away materials accurately and efficiently
  • Perform inventory moves, transfers, and adjustments in SAP
  • Maintain accurate inventory location control
  • Support cycle counts and inventory accuracy initiatives

Shipping – Parts Picker / Packer

  • Pick and pack parts accurately for customer and internal shipments
  • Verify part numbers, quantities, and shipment contents prior to packaging
  • Process shipments using UPS, FedEx, and other small-parcel systems
  • Identify and resolve part number, quantity, or documentation discrepancies
  • Ensure shipments are properly packaged, labeled, and staged

Shipping – LTL Crater / Packer

  • Pick large pumps or assemblies from stock for freight shipment
  • Measure products and build custom wooden crates as required
  • Use hand tools, measuring devices, pallet jacks, and fork trucks as needed
  • Secure products properly to prevent damage during transportation
  • Coordinate with shipping personnel to meet LTL and freight schedules

Shipping – Painter

  • Prepare, mask, and paint parts or assemblies for shipment
  • Confirm completion of paint operations in job travelers or systems
  • Ensure painted parts meet appearance and protection requirements
  • Stage painted parts to shipping or back to production as required
  • Maintain cleanliness and safety in paint and prep areas

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting

Core Competencies (All Assignments):

  • Follow standard work instructions, warehouse procedures, and safety requirements
  • Maintain accurate control of part numbers, quantities, and inventory locations
  • Perform SAP transactions accurately and in a timely manner
  • Identify, investigate, and escalate inventory, quantity, or documentation discrepancies
  • Support production and shipping schedules by ensuring materials and shipments are processed correctly
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment
  • Communicate effectively with production, purchasing, shipping, and supervision
  • Actively uphold safety standards and report unsafe conditions or practices
  • Perform other related duties as assigned based on operational needs

Preferences:

(Depending on Assignment) Experience in shipping, receiving, warehouse operations, and inventory control, including use of UPS, FedEx, or similar shipment processing systems.

  • Proficiency with ERP systems and basic computer applications; ability to learn SAP, shipping, and inventory platforms (SAP experience is a plus).
  • Background in manufacturing or industrial environments, with hands-on experience using fork trucks, hand tools, and building custom packaging or crates.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and organizational/timemanagement skills.
  • Ability to work independently, remain productive with minimal supervision, and logically investigate and resolve discrepancies.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills in English.

Physical Demands:

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods
  • Ability to bend, kneel, climb ladders, and work in warehouse and production areas
  • Industrial environment with exposure to noise, temperature variation, moving equipment, fumes, and chemicals

We proudly partner with District No. 8 of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers with a closed shop, which means that all hourly employees are union members.

  • New employees are regarded as probationary for the first 60 working days of their employment.
  • After probation, the employee will join the union with an initiation fee and monthly dues.
  • Full benefits package and company-paid pension?

About Us

Job Overview: 

We are looking for a skilled assembler to perform a variety of tasks as assigned in conjunction with the assembly of our product. You will ensure all parts fit correctly and are suitable for the final product. This position is responsible for safely performing high-level continuous work to quality standards. Assignments may change based on business demands. 

You must have desired technical knowledge and possess great manual dexterity. Ability to interpret instructions represented in manuals, drawings, schematics etc. and follow them with precision.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Read print drawings to determine dimensions, design, and materials for construction.
  • Assemble parts according to standard work / job breakdown sheets of unit being assembled, bill of materials and work order instructions, and assembly drawings 
  • Fastens parts together with bolts, screws, speed clips, rivets, or other fasteners according to torque specifications 
  • Operates pneumatic and manual presses to assist in assembly operation, which includes setting up the presses 
  • Set-up and operate identification equipment (stampers, labelers, etc.) 
  • Test product for compliance to meet specifications using manual and automatic test equipment 
  • Paint, label and pack completed product for shipment 
  • Achieve daily departmental productivity and quality levels 
  • Follow all ISO procedures and safety rules, including wearing personal safety equipment 
  • Keep Team Lead informed of mechanical/machine malfunctions or any supplies/tools needed 
  • Handle product to and from stock 
  • Perform in-process testing and make necessary corrections to meet standard work and Procedures for Qualification (PFQ) 
  • Notify team lead of non-conformance material 
  • Report changes in work orders, bill of materials, and pick lists to team lead. 
  • Contribute to department/cell communication boards 
  • Check off and sign work order cover sheets 
  • Complete daily hour by hour production sheet 
  • Maintain work area in accordance with 5S standards 
  • Identify and report all safety issues to team lead 
  • Participate and/or lead continuous improvement events and training 
  • Suggest ideas for overall improvements to the area processes 
  • Cross-train across multiple product lines 
  • All other duties as assigned by the supervisor/team leader.

 

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting

 

Core Competencies:

  • Knowledge of and willingness to comply with all general work rules, policies and procedures, including safety guidelines and procedures.
  • Able to rely on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals.
  • Ability to learn to operate all equipment associated with the job; including, but not limited to, power hand tools, forklifts, skyjacks, cranes, and measuring devices. 
  • Ability to identify routine problem causation, and correct routine problems, and willingness to learn.

 

Preferences:

  • 2+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting preferred. 
  • Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions in English, short correspondence, and memos, such as supervisory instructions, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, procedure manuals, and work orders 
  • Ability to effectively share information about job duties in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees 
  • Familiar with and ability to utilize all hand tools including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, and steel banding.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude to use equipment and maintain general understanding of business process.
  • Familiar with and can utilize power tools.
  • Forklift certification is required to operate forklift equipment, but is not a required job responsibility for assembly 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position will be based on-site

 

SAFETY REQUIREMENTS While performing the duties of this job, the employee must wear OSHA approved safety glasses, hearing protection and steel toe safety shoes. Gloves are required to be worn when handling or moving parts. OSHA approved hearing protection (ANSI approved ear plugs) is required when on the shop floor. Painters must wear a respirator. 

  • The following is a summary of the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) that was performed for this job: 
  • Hazard communication, fire safety, Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE), & detailed JSA training will be reviewed before any job assignment. The JSA describes identified hazards and what protection the employee must take to protect employees from injury. 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; use hands to finger; handle, or feel; walk; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear 
  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move boxes that weigh up to 50 pounds. The employee may be required to lift and/or move bar stock/baskets that vary in weight above these amounts. The employee must get assistance from other co-workers or by using a material handling device, forklift, or hand truck when lifting items 
  • The employee is frequently required to climb or balance; and to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl 
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to moving mechanical parts, toxic or caustic chemicals, airborne particles and vibration from hammering of parts and using hand tools 
  • Since it is a manufacturing environment, the noise level is usually loud due to the different machinery being operated (i.e. forklifts, hand tools, machines in other departments) and the testing that occurs. Normal noise exposure in the area ranges from 80-90 d BA; hearing protection is required while on the plant floor

Responsibilities:

  • Ability to identify and solve problems.

Location: Quincy, IL (site-based)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview
An Engineering Technician is crucial in running lab tests and technical evaluations in the research department. They are responsible for assisting with product testing and maintaining engineering lab equipment and calibration.

Responsibilities
Technical Support: Provide lab support to engineers and other team members by assisting with running lab tests and technical evaluations in the research department.
Testing and Analysis: Conduct experiments and tests on prototypes or existing systems, collect data, and analyze results to identify issues and propose solutions.
Documentation: Create and maintain accurate test records, test reports, and documentation related to engineering projects, equipment maintenance, and ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulations.
Equipment Maintenance: Perform routine maintenance and calibration of equipment and instruments used in engineering processes.
Prototyping: Assist in building and assembling prototypes or models, including selecting and procuring materials and components.
Quality Control: Conduct quality control checks to ensure products and systems meet specifications and quality standards.
Troubleshooting: Identify and troubleshoot technical issues and collaborate with engineers to develop and implement solutions.
Safety Compliance: Ensure that engineering activities comply with safety regulations and best practices and participate in safety audits and inspections.
Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineers, designers, and project managers, to achieve project objectives.
Technical Research: Stay updated on industry trends, new technologies, and best practices through research and continuous learning.

Requirements

  • High School Graduate/GED
  • 3+ years of experience in industrial maintenance, automotive, or rotary machinery 


Core Competencies

  • Knowledge and experience with basic hand tools
  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings and electrical schematics
  • Ability to build, operate, and test industrial equipment
  • Mechanical aptitude
  • Electrical aptitude
  • Strong communication skills
  • Writing
  • Troubleshooting/Problem Solving

Job Overview
Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Controls Proposal Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role is responsible for reviewing customer inquiries, specifications, and project requirements and developing accurate technical and commercial proposals for industrial control panel systems for blowers, compressors, and related equipment.

This position is ideal for a recent engineering graduate or early-career professional interested in industrial automation, control systems, and customer-focused engineering solutions. The role provides hands on exposure to industrial control panels, PLCs, HMIs, instrumentation, and proposal development processes while working alongside experienced engineering professionals.

The Controls Proposal Engineer serves as the technical lead during the quotation phase, working closely with customers, sales, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing to define project scope, develop cost estimates, select major equipment and control panel components, and deliver competitive proposals. This position requires the ability to interpret customer requirements and industry standards while balancing technical solutions, project risks, manufacturability, and commercial objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Review customer RFQs, specifications, datasheets, drawings, and commercial requirements.
  • Interpret customer requirements and develop technical solutions for industrial control panels and automation systems.
  • Define scope of supply, system architecture, and major equipment requirements.
  • Develop detailed cost estimates including material, labor, engineering, testing, and subcontracted services.
  • Select and specify major control panel components including PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control, networking equipment, and power distribution devices.
  • Prepare technical and commercial proposals, quotations, and bid documentation.
  • Identify project risks, technical exceptions, clarifications, and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate with engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and suppliers to obtain accurate pricing and technical information.
  • Participate in customer meetings, team kickoffs, bid reviews, and technical clarification discussions.
  • Ensure proposals comply with customer specifications and applicable industry standards including NEC, UL 508A, and other project-specific requirements.
  • Maintain proposal documentation, estimating tools, pricing databases, and historical project records.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in estimating processes, proposal quality, and competitiveness.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline.
  • Internship, co-op, or senior design project in industrial automation, controls, or electrical systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, electrical schematics, and P&IDs.

Core Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Eagerness to learn industrial control panel design, proposal development, estimating, and customer specifications.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple proposals and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

Preferred experience

  • Internship or coursework related to automation, controls, electrical design, or industrial systems.
  • Exposure to PLC platforms such as Rockwell Automation, Phoenix Contact, Siemens, Schneider Electric, or other industrial automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with AutoCAD or similar engineering software.
  • Knowledge of industrial networking, instrumentation, or SCADA systems.
  • Experience working on team-based engineering projects.

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Job Title: Supervisor, Shipping & Receiving 
Location:  Alsip, IL (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a world where precision engineering drives scientific innovation. Within our Precision and Science Technologies division, you’ll help power mission-critical applications through cutting-edge pumps, fluid management systems, and aftermarket solutions trusted across the globe. We’re looking for a dynamic Shipping & Receiving Supervisor to join our Ingersoll Rand Pump (IRP), MP Pump, and Oberdorfer Pump (MPOB) Business Unit in Alsip, IL — a high-impact leadership role at the center of our manufacturing operation.  In this role, you won’t just oversee shipping and receiving — you’ll lead the pace of the operation. From driving daily execution and setting clear performance goals to coaching and developing a high-performing team, you’ll play a critical role in keeping production moving safely, efficiently, and on schedule. 

We’re seeking a hands-on leader, with proven SAP skills, who thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, knows how to motivate and mentor teams, and brings strong operational discipline to workflow planning, scheduling, and problem-solving. If you’re energized by continuous improvement, team development, and making an impact in a precision-driven operation, this is your opportunity to lead from the front.

Responsibilities:
  • Analyze and track operational data, maintain daily management boards, and drive departmental performance through reporting, communication, and continuous process improvement initiatives. 
  • Lead daily shipping, receiving, packing, tagging, and export operations to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and on-time delivery performance that meets customer demand and company objectives.
  • Manage receiving and inventory flow processes, including put-away completion within 24 hours, cycle count support, shortage resolution, and coordination of shipments between internal company locations.
  • Direct and support material handlers in delivering materials to manufacturing cells while ensuring workflow priorities and production needs are consistently met.
  • Coach, develop, and monitor employee performance through cross-training, skill development, project assignments, and ongoing team collaboration initiatives that strengthen operational capability.
  • Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external customers by responding to operational inquiries, resolving equipment or parts-related issues, and ensuring clear communication across teams.
  • Maintain adequate inventory of indirect shipping and packaging supplies to support uninterrupted warehouse and shipping operations.
  • Champion a safe, clean, and organized work environment by enforcing safety protocols, PPE compliance, hazard reporting, and adherence to 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain).

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in Shipping & Receiving operations with strong knowledge of warehouse, inventory, shipping, and receiving processes within an industrial manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of experience using SAP for shipping and warehouse management functions.
  • 2+ years of supervisory experience in shipping and receiving or warehouse operations within a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel to analyze and manipulate order and delivery data.

Core Competencies:
  • Customer Focus: Prioritizes customer needs and continuously improves the customer experience.
  • Analytical Problem Solving: Uses data, critical thinking, and sound judgment to solve problems and drive decisions.
  • Communication & Influence: Communicates clearly and professionally while building strong cross-functional relationships.
  • Leadership: Coaches, develops, and motivates teams to achieve operational and customer service excellence.
  • Adaptability: Thrives in fast-paced environments and responds quickly to changing business needs and priorities.
  • Technical Aptitude: Quickly learns systems, processes, and product functionality in complex environments.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Based onsite at our Alsip, IL location
  • Minimal anticipated travel, less than 5%
  • Must be able to lift up to 35 lbs individually and up to 70 lbs as part of a team lift.

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $75,000-$90,000. The pay considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate's skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications, and geographic location.

Job Title: Systems Engineering Technologist
Location: Frederica, DE


About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
This position sits within the engineering organization supporting the development, qualification, production, and sustainment of space flight hardware. The Systems Technologist supports verification activities and technical documentation throughout the product life cycle.  In addition, there is a secondary role serving as a test conductor and/or test technician for verification activities.

The role works within established engineering processes while exercising independent technical judgment appropriate to experience. The Systems Technologist collaborates closely with design engineering, materials and processes, manufacturing and quality to perform verification test activities at the development, acceptance and qualification levels. This position is well suited for an individual seeking broad technical ownership, cross-functional leadership experience, and long-term growth in requirements-driven development of mission-critical products. The test conductor performs testing activities under established Quality processes and procedures, using sound judgment to ensure the safe and compliant handling of flight hardware. Successful candidates will have opportunities to develop into systems engineering, integration and testing, or technical leadership roles.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and support verification and validation activities, including definition of verification methods, test objectives, acceptance criteria, compliance matrices, and closure evidence.
  • Participate in technical reviews such as test readiness reviews, configuration reviews, and certification or customer reviews.
  • Generate and maintain test plans, test procedures, verification documents, engineering reports, change packages, and other product-definition records.
  • Communicate technical information clearly to team members, cross-functional partners, leadership, suppliers, and external customers.
  • Conduct suit testing activities including manned and unmanned operations.  Support other ILC product testing on an as needed/availability basis
  • Perform suit hardware assembly and disassembly activities as part of testing.


Requirements

  • Must be able to access shared databases supporting U.S. Government programs. Due to U.S. export control regulations, applicants must qualify as a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder), refugee, asylee, or otherwise be eligible to obtain any required U.S. Government authorizations.
  • 5+ years of experience in product development, integration, test, manufacturing, or engineering support. Co-op, internship, capstone, or military technical experience may be considered.


Core Competencies

  • Foundational understanding of treatment of mission critical hardware, and ability to follow work instructions and test procedures.
  • Proficiency with standard engineering tools, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentation software, and document collaboration systems. Experience with a requirements-management tool is desirable.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, with engineers, technicians, program teams, suppliers, and customers.
  • Willingness and ability to follow laboratory, test, and production safety practices, including wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Ability to read, understand, and execute work instructions, drawings, specifications, and technical documentation written in English.
  • Willingness to travel occasionally to local worksites, suppliers, customer facilities, or test locations as needed.


Preferences

  • Academic project work or early professional experience with complex, regulated, or safety-critical products in aerospace, defense, medical devices, energy systems, or advanced manufacturing.
  • Exposure to NASA, Department of Defense, commercial space, or equivalent aerospace development standards and customer requirements.
  • Experience supporting environmental, qualification, acceptance, or integrated system testing, including anomaly resolution and verification closure.
  • Familiarity with configuration management, change control, product lifecycle management, and formal technical review processes.
  • Demonstrated technical curiosity, sound judgment, and ownership appropriate for work supporting mission-critical hardware.
  • CPR trained.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position will be based at our office in Frederica, DE
  • Wllingness to travel occasionally to local worksites, suppliers, customer facilities, or test locations as needed.



What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership - taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Job Summary
Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Controls Proposal Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role is responsible for reviewing customer inquiries, specifications, and project requirements and developing accurate technical and commercial proposals for industrial control panel systems for blowers, compressors, and related equipment.

The Controls Proposal Engineer serves as the technical lead during the quotation phase, working closely with customers, sales, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing to define project scope, develop cost estimates, select major equipment and control panel components, and deliver competitive proposals. This position requires the ability to interpret customer requirements and industry standards while balancing technical solutions, project risks, manufacturability, and commercial objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Review customer RFQs, specifications, datasheets, drawings, and commercial requirements.
  • Interpret customer requirements and develop technical solutions for industrial control panels and automation systems.
  • Define scope of supply, system architecture, and major equipment requirements.
  • Develop detailed cost estimates including material, labor, engineering, testing, and subcontracted services.
  • Select and specify major control panel components including PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control, networking equipment, and power distribution devices.
  • Prepare technical and commercial proposals, quotations, and bid documentation.
  • Identify project risks, technical exceptions, clarifications, and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate with engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and suppliers to obtain accurate pricing and technical information.
  • Participate in customer meetings, team kickoffs, bid reviews, and technical clarification discussions.
  • Ensure proposals comply with customer specifications and applicable industry standards including NEC, UL 508A, and other project-specific requirements.
  • Maintain proposal documentation, estimating tools, pricing databases, and historical project records.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in estimating processes, proposal quality, and competitiveness.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline. Equivalent industry experience may be considered.
  • 2+ years of experience reviewing customer specifications and developing technical proposals for industrial equipment, control systems, or engineered products.
  • 2+ years ability to interpret electrical, mechanical, process, and instrumentation documentation.
  • 2+ years of industrial control panels, PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control systems, and automation equipment.

Key Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of NEC, UL 508A, and applicable industrial control panel standards.
  • Experience preparing cost estimates and evaluating project scope, risk, and schedule requirements.
  • Ability to read and understand electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and engineering drawings.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple proposals and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

Preferred experience

  • Experience preparing proposals for industrial control panels, compressor systems, blower packages, turbomachinery, or process equipment.
  • Experience with Rockwell Automation, Phoenix Contact, Siemens, Schneider Electric, or other industrial automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with UL 508A panel design practices and industrial control panel manufacturing.
  • Experience using estimating, ERP, CRM, or configuration management software.
  • Knowledge of process instrumentation, industrial networking, and SCADA systems.
  • Understanding of project execution, commissioning, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), and field service activities.
  • Prior experience in applications engineering, sales engineering, or proposal engineering environments.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Job Overview: 
The Material Handler is responsible for ensuring materials are supplied where and when they are needed. The Material Handler is responsible for keeping workstations fully stocked with materials, ultimately contributing to higher overall productivity of other workers. 

Responsibilities:

  • Receives, ships, loads, and unloads materials/parts from suppliers or carriers.  Material may be unloaded from trucks, pallets, trays, racks, and shelves by hand, with forklift, or other material handling device.
  • Visually inspects incoming pieces/parts for compliance and obvious damage; informing Quality if necessary.
  • Moves material/parts from warehouse or receiving area, to designated line or stock locations. (Ex: to proper stock location, to inspection area, to machine cell) while using barcode scanner and/or computers.
  • Uses computer and/or barcode scanner to properly identify stock locations to retrieve parts.
  • Moving stock to release, consolidate, or change part locations.
  • Reads work order or follows oral instructions to determine materials to be transferred; informs inventory control to update computer system when necessary (Ex: quantity mismatch, mixed parts, wrong labels)
  • Counts, weighs, and records number of units of materials received, moved, or shipped and reports inconsistencies to inventory control.
  • Operates forklift, hand truck, and/or other material handling equipment to assist in loading or moving any material.
  • Receives work orders from planners; picks parts to jobs for machine shop, assembly areas, staging for kits, and spare part sales orders using barcode scanner and/or computer.
  • Follows all ISO procedures and safety rules, including wearing personal safety equipment.
  • Remove any debris found on shelves throughout the warehouse.
  • Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned


Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 1+ years’ experience in manufacturing or distribution industry  


Key Competencies:

  • Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 40 pounds occasionally with hoist to be used on objects over 40 pounds.
  • Standing: Standing is required in periods of up to three hours at a time.
  • Stooping: Would be required to lift objects off pallets
  • Hand Dexterity: Must be able to work with hand tools, screws and gauges, as well as operating buttons on controls.
  • Verbal Communication: Must be capable of clear communication between co-workers and supervisor.
  • Carrying: Capable of carrying 40 pounds for a distance of up to 25 feet.


Preferences:

  • Knowledge of inventory processes.
  • Process driven and systematic in their approach to completing their work
  • Ability to identify and solve problems.
  • Ability to pass certification for Powered Industrial Vehicle license.

 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: This position will be based at our site in Mocksville, NC, with no anticipated travel.

Ingersoll Rand has an exciting opportunity for a Project Manager at our Bentleyville, PA location. This position directly supports the Marine Division to ensure timely and effective project execution for new equipment and rebuilds per contract requirements.  


Responsibilities: 
    
Planning and Strategy Development:  Support sales on new project requests, align schedules & provide preliminary review of contract specifics prior to award.  Upon receipt of contracts, review to determine/finalize scope and related requirements, obtain necessary clarifications, communicate new orders to cross-functional team, monitor schedules to guide the team and stakeholders effectively, drive on-time delivery of documentation & equipment.  
Team Leadership and Coordination:  Guide cross-functional team through project execution from contract award to final acceptance, assign & drive completion of tasks, develop new processes & tools for improved management of contracts, clarify roles & responsibilities of team members including setting priorities, and ensure collaboration among team members, customers, and suppliers.

Risk Identification and Mitigation:  Identify & manage risks to cost, schedule, and revenue, develop & implement contingency, corrective action, and preventative action plans while driving process improvement & efficiency.

Quality Assurance and Documentation:  Identify contract requirements & communicate to team, support quality team to ensure quality requirements are being met internally & at suppliers, work to implement corrective actions when quality deficiencies arise, and review/certify final quality documentation prior to submittal to ensure timely acceptance.

  • 3+ years of project management experience required.  Project Management training, PMP certification or similar, is desirable.

  • Prepare and maintain detailed documentation of processes, improvements, and best practices.
  • Train and support production staff on new and revised manufacturing processes to ensure smooth implementation.
  • Monitor and evaluate production performance metrics to drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for any process deviations or quality issues.
  • Support the development and implementation of Lean Manufacturing principles to optimize workflows.

Requirements

Preferences

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing engineering, Industrial or Mechanical engineering.
  • Working knowledge of Six Sigma
  • Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt
  • Demonstrated ability to continuously improve manufacturing processes
  • Understanding & application of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerance
  • Effective oral & written communications skills. Listens fully to others giving full attention to what is being said, seeking to understand others perspective, being curious & asking questions.
  • Problem-solving skills. Using logic & reasoning to identify the strengths & weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems. Seeking input from others when making decisions
  • Proficient in the use of the personal computer, Microsoft Office software applications, Mastercam, AutoCAD and SolidWorks

Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.
 

Responsibilities: 

Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements
 
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts
 
Core Competencies
 
  • Power generation equipment packaging
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Structural and mechanical design
  • Thermal management systems
  • Airflow and ventilation engineering
  • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
  • Fuel system integration
  • Vibration isolation
  • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
  • Reliability and maintainability engineering
  • Data center infrastructure requirements
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 
Preferences:
  • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
  • Experience designing:
    • Generator enclosures
    • Containerized equipment packages
    • Cooling systems
    • Fuel systems
    • Acoustic attenuation solutions
  • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
  • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
  • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.


Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH 
  • Relocation assistance available
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

Pay Range
The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

job.description:
