Job Title: Maintenance Parts & Materials Coordinator                    
Location:  Alsip, IL
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Bring order to the parts, systems, and processes that keep maintenance moving. Ingersoll Rand’s Alsip facility supports the IRP, MP Pump and Oberdorfer Pump businesses, trusted brands known worldwide for reliable, innovative and durable fluid-handling solutions.  

As the Maintenance Parts & Materials Coordinator, you will create the control, accuracy, and visibility needed to support 159 assets across Ingersoll Rand’s 100,000-square-foot Alsip facility. You will ensure technicians have the right parts, outside services, and reliable system information to complete critical preventive and corrective maintenance. Owning the process from request through completion, you will source vendors, obtain quotes, manage purchase orders, track deliveries, record received materials, maintain inventory accuracy, and coordinate activity across the CMMS, ERP, procurement, and payment processes. You will also become the site’s CMMS subject-matter expert, strengthening parts and asset data, inventory accuracy, and the connection between purchased materials and completed maintenance work. MaintainX experience is not required, but familiarity with a CMMS or comparable operational system—and the ability to learn technology quickly—is essential.

This is a non-supervisory systems-focused position requiring strong ownership, follow through and organization—not a hands-on mechanic, inventory-counting, or administrative support role. Working closely with Maintenance, Purchasing, Finance, Accounts Payable, Operations, Engineering, EHS, and external vendors, you will identify gaps, solve problems, and drive work to completion.Because the site’s maintenance materials and purchasing processes are continuing to evolve, you will have the opportunity to help build and improve them. 

The strongest candidate will bring experience in maintenance coordination, parts or inventory management, logistics, industrial materials, a tool crib or storeroom, automotive service operations, or a similar environment—along with urgency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. For someone eager to grow within industrial maintenance, this role offers broad exposure to plant operations, equipment, purchasing, inspections, and vendors, with opportunities to expand into regulatory support, deeper maintenance expertise, and future leadership.

Responsibilities:

CMMS Administration & Data Management  
  • Maintain accurate asset, equipment, preventive maintenance, work-order, labor, parts, and service records within the CMMS. 
  • Review newly submitted maintenance requests for completeness and route them to the appropriate supervisor or technician. 
  • Create and update work orders based on maintenance findings, approved requests, inspections, and scheduled preventive maintenance activities. 
  • Support the development and maintenance of equipment hierarchies, asset records, PM frequencies, task lists, and equipment documentation. 
  • Monitor open, overdue, incomplete, and waiting-for-parts work orders. 
  • Follow up with supervisors and technicians to obtain missing work-order information, labor hours, parts usage, failure codes, and completion details. 
  • Verify that completed work orders contain sufficient documentation before administrative closure. 
  • Maintain consistent naming conventions and data-entry standards within the CMMS. 
  • Assist with CMMS reports covering PM compliance, work-order backlog, equipment history, parts usage, recurring failures, and maintenance spending. 
  • Support the onboarding of new equipment into the CMMS, including asset information, manuals, parts lists, and initial PM requirements. 
 
Parts Room & Inventory Control 
  • Maintain an organized, labeled, secure, and accurate maintenance parts room. 
  • Receive, identify, label, store, issue, and document maintenance repair parts, consumables, and critical spares. 
  • Maintain accurate inventory quantities, storage locations, part descriptions, manufacturer information, and equipment associations. 
  • Establish and maintain minimum and maximum stocking levels for frequently used and critical spare parts. 
  • Perform cycle counts and periodic physical inventories. 
  • Research and correct discrepancies between physical inventory and system quantities. 
  • Identify obsolete, duplicate, damaged, slow-moving, or unidentified inventory for review. 
  • Coordinate parts reservations and staging for planned PMs, repairs, shutdown work, and contractor activities. 
  • Notify Maintenance Supervisors when critical spares are below established stocking levels or unavailable. 
  • Maintain appropriate parts-room housekeeping, access controls, and storage practices. 
  • Coordinate the proper storage and documentation of lubricants, chemicals, batteries, and other maintenance materials with EHS requirements. 

Purchasing, Service POs & Orders 
  • Prepare maintenance purchase requisitions and supporting documentation for repair parts, supplies, tools, rentals, and outside services. 
  • Coordinate the creation, tracking, and administrative management of maintenance service purchase orders. 
  • Confirm that requests contain the correct vendor, scope, asset, department, quote, cost information, and approval documentation. 
  • Submit approved parts and service orders through established company purchasing processes. 
  • Track order acknowledgements, delivery dates, backorders, cancellations, and expedited requests. 
  • Communicate order and delivery status to Maintenance Supervisors and affected stakeholders. 
  • Match received products and completed services to the applicable purchase order and supporting documentation. 
  • Assist with resolving quantity, pricing, receipt, invoice, and purchase-order discrepancies. 
  • Maintain organized records of vendor quotes, purchase orders, service reports, packing slips, invoices, warranties, and approvals. 
  • Escalate urgent parts or service needs that could affect equipment uptime, safety, environmental compliance, or production. 
  • Support emergency purchasing documentation when immediate repairs require expedited vendor service or materials. 

Vendor & Service Coordination 
  • Maintain current maintenance vendor and service-provider contact information. 
  • Coordinate service-call documentation, site access information, schedules, purchase-order references, and required service reports. 
  • Confirm that contractor service documentation is received and associated with the appropriate asset and work order. 
  • Obtain repair reports, inspection results, recommendations, warranty information, and follow-up quotations from vendors. 
  • Track open vendor recommendations and communicate required follow-up actions to Maintenance Supervisors. 
  • Support contractor onboarding and required documentation in coordination with Maintenance and EHS. 
  • Maintain equipment warranty information and assist in identifying repairs or parts that may qualify for warranty coverage. 

Maintenance Planning Support 
  • Review upcoming PMs and identify required parts, materials, documentation, vendor support, and equipment access requirements. 
  • Assemble work-order packets, manuals, drawings, procedures, service history, and parts information for planned work. 
  • Stage or reserve parts for upcoming PMs and corrective repairs. 
  • Support development of weekly maintenance schedules under the direction of the Maintenance Supervisor. 
  • Identify work orders delayed because of parts, purchasing, vendor availability, approvals, or missing information. 
  • Maintain a visible list of maintenance work that is ready to schedule. 
  • Support cross-shift continuity by keeping work-order, parts, and service-status information current and accessible. 
  • Assist with maintenance shutdown preparation, contractor scheduling, and material readiness. 

Reporting & Continuous Improvement 
  • Prepare routine reports on inventory accuracy, stockouts, purchase-order status, parts usage, PM support, work-order backlog, and maintenance costs. 
  • Identify recurring purchases that should be converted into stocked items, blanket orders, or preferred-vendor arrangements. 
  • Identify frequently used or long-lead-time components that may require revised stocking levels. 
  • Help improve maintenance workflows, purchasing controls, storeroom organization, and CMMS data quality. 
  • Support root cause analysis by providing equipment history, prior work orders, parts usage, vendor reports, and repair-cost information. 
  • Participate in maintenance planning meetings and provide updates on parts, orders, vendor services, and work-order readiness. 
  • Support standard work and documented procedures for parts issuance, inventory counts, purchase requests, CMMS entries, and work-order closure. 

Safety, Environmental & Compliance Support 
  • Follow all applicable site safety, environmental, purchasing, financial, and document-retention requirements. 
  • Maintain the parts room and maintenance administrative areas in a safe and orderly condition. 
  • Coordinate with EHS regarding storage, labeling, documentation, and disposal requirements for maintenance chemicals and controlled materials. 
  • Report damaged shelving, unsafe storage, spills, blocked access, missing labels, and other hazards. 
  • Maintain required records for contractor services, inspections, repairs, and compliance-related maintenance activities. 
  • Ensure that safety-critical parts and services are clearly identified and appropriately prioritized. 
 
Requirements
  • High School Diploma or GED. 
  • 2+ years of progressive experience supporting maintenance operations, such as maintenance data, service purchase orders, and inventory, with exposure to CMMS coordination, inventory control, purchasing, parts management, manufacturing support, or a related function.
  • 2+ years experience reading and understand equipment descriptions, part numbers, bills of material, manuals, quotations, and service reports. 
  • 2+ years experience working with a CMMS, inventory-management system, ERP system, or purchasing platform
  • 2+ years of professional experience using Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and other Microsoft Office applications to support operational workflows. 
  • 1+ years working knowledge of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, inventory transactions, and vendor documentation.
  • Ability to lift and handle maintenance parts within established site material-handling requirements. 
 
Core Competencies
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple open orders, work requests, and changing priorities. 
  • Demonstrates strong ownership, urgency, and consistent follow-through.
  • Collaborates effectively with technicians, supervisors, vendors, Purchasing, Finance, Engineering, Operations, and EHS.
  • Maintains accurate records and closes items only when supporting information is complete and properly documented.
  • Communicates delays, shortages, discrepancies, and potential risks promptly and proactively.
  • Uses data to identify opportunities for improving inventory control and maintenance processes.
  • Exercises sound judgment when coordinating urgent equipment, parts, and service needs.
  • Protects confidential pricing, purchasing, vendor, and business information.
  • Contributes to a collaborative, responsive, and service-oriented maintenance culture.

Preferences: 
Associate degree, technical certification, or coursework in maintenance, supply chain, business administration, industrial technology, or a related field
Manufacturing or industrial maintenance experience
Familiarity with mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and / or CNC equipment parts 

Travel Work Arrangement
  • Onsite role at the Alsip, IL manufacturing facility.
 
The pay range for this role is an annual base of $65,000 - $75,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting.

  • Apply statistical tools to establish/monitor capability and verify effectiveness of improvements.

Core Competencies
  • Proven experience leading IQ/OQ/PQ and working to ISO 13485 / FDA 21 CFR 820. 
  • Practical experience using DOE, SPC, and Gage R&R; familiarity with control plans and PFMEA.

  • Motivated and creative; operates effectively under pressure in a fast?paced team environment.

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

About Us  

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview

  • The Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Industrial Technologies and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 
     

Responsibilities

  • Ensure the correct installation, maintenance, and field repair of the equipment manufactured and sold by Ingersoll Rand at the purchaser's location. 

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the field installation and repair requirements of this equipment. 

  • Provide technical advice and be able to train customers, potential customers, field salesmen, and field service trainees.

  • Diagnose problems, recommend corrective action in this unsupervised environment and submit clear, accurate records and/or oral reports to the manufacturing facility. 

  • Maintain a high degree of integrity in handling business affairs.

  • Maintain proper written and oral communication skills to transfer information related to service work in a concise and logical manner. 

  • Submit detailed technical reports on each service call in a legible fashion, suitable for billing customers. 

  • Submit accurate, detailed & timely expense account records along with timecards on a weekly basis. Maintain good financial records and practices to manage company business matters, credit cards, and if required, a company car.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. Experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus. While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. .

Core Competencies 

  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; specialty tools will be provided. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

  • This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Customer service skills such as conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner. 
  • Mechanical competency to be able to learn, diagnose, and troubleshoot compressor systems and machinery. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Preferences

  • Desired degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification. Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus. Candidates who possess this knowledge or skills but have not completed a formal program may be considered. 

  • EPA 608 /F-GAS 303/2008/CE/ISHRAE Certification Preferred (Refrigeration experience/certification a plus).

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require occasional travel for training. 1-2 times per year for one week at a time. (5-10%). 

  • This position is included in an on-call rotation with other service technicians in the local area to service customer emergencies in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during scheduled on-call weeks.

Location: Buena Park, CA

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Summary 

The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 

  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.

  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range

Starting Pay will range between Min - 50,000.00 - Max - 104,000.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Location: Sedalia, MO
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

Job Title: Chiller Test Engineer
Location: Junction City, OR

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.
 

 Job Overview

The Chiller Test Engineer is responsible for planning, executing, monitoring, and documenting performance, reliability, safety, and validation testing of commercial and industrial chiller systems. This role supports product development, product validation, regulatory compliance, quality improvement, and continuous innovation by ensuring chillers meet customer requirements, industry standards, and company performance specifications. The engineer collaborates closely with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Controls, and Laboratory teams to deliver accurate and timely test results.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute test plans, procedures, and protocols for air-cooled and water-cooled chiller products.
  • Conduct performance, functional, reliability, endurance, acoustic, and environmental testing of HVAC equipment.
  • Configure and operate laboratory equipment, instrumentation, data acquisition systems, and controls used for chiller testing.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret test data to verify compliance with design specifications and industry standards.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, refrigeration, electrical, and controls-related issues identified during testing.
  • Identify root causes of product performance issues and provide engineering recommendations for corrective actions.
  • Prepare detailed technical reports summarizing test conditions, results, conclusions, and recommendations.
  • Coordinate laboratory schedules, test setup activities, and resource requirements to support product development timelines.
  • Support certification and compliance testing to applicable standards such as AHRI, ASHRAE, UL, CE, and other regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with design engineers to validate new product designs, design modifications, and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Monitor laboratory equipment calibration and ensure test procedures comply with quality and safety requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to testing processes, laboratory operations, and product performance.
  • Support manufacturing and field issue investigations through testing and data analysis.
  • Maintain accurate technical documentation and test records.

 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, HVAC Engineering, or related engineering discipline is preferred
  • 3+ years of engineering experience in HVAC, refrigeration, thermal systems, product testing, or laboratory environments.

Core competencies
  • Experience with test instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition systems, and performance measurement techniques.
  • Knowledge of vapor compression refrigeration cycles, heat transfer principles, and HVAC systems.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, and wiring diagrams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel for data analysis.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and testing priorities simultaneously.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience testing commercial HVAC equipment, chillers, heat pumps, or refrigeration systems.
  • Familiarity with AHRI, ASHRAE, UL, ISO, and related industry standards.
  • Experience with LabVIEW, MATLAB, Python, Minitab, or similar data analysis tools.
  • Knowledge of PLCs, building automation systems, or embedded controls.
  • Understanding of refrigeration components including compressors, heat exchangers, expansion devices, and controls.
  • Experience with Design Verification Testing (DVT), Product Validation Testing (PVT), and reliability testing.

 

Technical Competencies

  • Refrigeration and HVAC systems
  • Chiller performance testing
  • Data acquisition and analysis
  • Root cause analysis
  • Test method development
  • Product validation
  • Controls and instrumentation
  • Thermal systems engineering
  • Regulatory compliance testing
  • Problem-solving and continuous improvement

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 
  • Fully onsite in Junction City, OR
  • Minimal travel expected.

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview: 
Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Cybersecurity Compliance & Regulatory Lead to support and mature our cybersecurity compliance program. This role will serve as the primary subject matter expert for cybersecurity regulations and compliance requirements, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), NIS2 Directive, EU Machinery Regulation, CMMC, UK Cyber Essentials other emerging regulatory obligations. 

The successful candidate will partner with business units, product teams, engineering, procurement, legal, quality, IT, and cybersecurity stakeholders to establish governance processes, compliance frameworks, guidance, training, assessments, and reporting capabilities. This role will help the organization understand, implement, and maintain compliance with applicable cybersecurity regulations while proactively monitoring regulatory developments and supporting readiness across the enterprise. 


Responsibilities: 

Cybersecurity Compliance Program 

  • Serve as the primary subject matter expert for the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), NIS2 Directive, EU Machinery Regulation, CMMC2, UK Cyber Essentials and other emerging cybersecurity regulations. 

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks, guidance documents, assessment methodologies, templates, and tools to support cybersecurity compliance efforts. 

  • Provide consistent interpretation of regulatory requirements and cybersecurity best practices to business stakeholders and compliance owners. 

  • Support the development and maintenance of cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, and governance processes necessary to meet cybersecurity obligations. 

  • Create repeatable compliance processes that enable business functions and product teams to achieve and maintain regulatory compliance. 

Business Support & Enablement 

  • Partner with business units, engineering teams, IT teams, procurement, legal, quality, and cybersecurity stakeholders to help them understand and meet cybersecurity compliance obligations. 

  • Provide guidance, consultation, and support on implementing regulatory and compliance requirements. 

  • Develop and deliver training, awareness materials, workshops, and educational content related to cybersecurity regulations. 

  • Assist stakeholders with identifying compliance gaps and developing remediation plans. 

  • Facilitate the sharing of best practices and lessons learned across the organization. 

Regulatory Monitoring & Compliance Intelligence 

  • Monitor emerging and evolving cybersecurity, privacy, digital resilience, and technology regulations. 

  • Evaluate regulatory changes and communicate potential impacts to business stakeholders and cybersecurity leadership. 

  • Maintain awareness of applicable regulations, standards, and guidance documents to ensure Ingersoll Rand remains prepared for future compliance obligations. 

  • Develop compliance readiness plans for new and upcoming regulatory requirements. 

  • Serve as a trusted advisor on regulatory developments impacting Ingersoll Rand products, services, operations, and third-party relationships. 

Third-Party & Supply Chain Compliance 

  • Support third-party cybersecurity review activities required to meet EU cybersecurity compliance requirements. 

  • Work with procurement, legal, engineering, and cybersecurity teams to assess supplier cybersecurity capabilities and compliance posture. 

  • Assist in evaluating third-party providers, software suppliers, and cybersecurity-related supplier risks. 

  • Support the collection and maintenance of compliance evidence associated with third-party and supply chain requirements. 

  • Contribute to the development of processes supporting cybersecurity compliance and third-party risk management objectives. 

Program Governance & Reporting 

  • Develop and maintain compliance metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting. 

  • Track compliance status, risks, remediation activities, and readiness efforts across business units. 

  • Prepare recurring status reports for cybersecurity leadership and business stakeholders. 

  • Support audits, assessments, customer inquiries, and regulatory reviews related to cybersecurity requirements. 

  • Maintain visibility into compliance risks, issues, and remediation priorities. 

 

Requirements: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Compliance, Risk Management, or a related discipline. 

  • 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, compliance, governance, risk management, regulatory compliance, product security, or a related field. 
     

Core Competencies: 

  • Product cybersecurity compliance and regulatory interpretation 

  • Governance process development and stakeholder enablement 

  • Risk assessment, issue tracking, and remediation coordination 

  • Executive reporting, metrics, and compliance readiness communication 

  • Collaboration across engineering, legal, procurement, quality, cybersecurity, and business teams 

 

Preferences: 

  • Experience with cybersecurity regulations and frameworks, such as EU CRA, NIS2, EU Machinery Regulation, CMMC Level 2, UK Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 27001, or NIST CSF.

  • Knowledge of cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and control frameworks.

  • Experience developing governance processes, regulatory guidance, training, and compliance reporting.

  • Experience conducting compliance assessments, gap analyses, audits, and supplier or third-party cybersecurity reviews.

  • Experience collaborating with global engineering, IT, cybersecurity, legal, procurement, and compliance teams.

  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, Security+, or ISA/IEC 62443.

  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, organizational, and analytical skills.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and cross-functional stakeholders in a global environment
     

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Ability to work effectively across global teams and time zones. 

  • Limited travel may be required based on business, project, stakeholder, or assessment needs.

Job title: Production Coordinator

Location: Southern Pines, NC (onsite)

 

About Us 

Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company with a passion for making lives better.  We do this by living our values, and through a relentless focus on the success of our customers and partnering with our employees to think and act like owners. We believe in sustainability through the development and distribution of a broad range of global brands designed to meet the needs of our customers in both efficient and responsible ways. Ingersoll Rand is a diverse and inclusive environment.  For more information visit: www.irco.com.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a driven and organized Production Coordinator to support our manufacturing operations. In this role, you will coordinate daily workflow, communicate production goals, assign responsibilities, manage schedules, and provide coaching and mentorship to team members. You will help ensure a safe working environment, maintain quality standards, achieve production targets, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment, effectively manages multiple priorities, and consistently delivers results.

Responsibilities:

  • Train, develop, and support assemblers to ensure a thorough understanding of departmental procedures, work instructions, and quality requirements.
  • Maintain production scheduling systems and productivity tracking tools while collaborating with cross-functional departments to meet operational objectives.
  • Monitor and evaluate team member performance, recommend development opportunities, assign projects that build skills and capabilities, and conduct annual performance evaluations.
  • Identify, track, communicate, and help resolve material shortages, equipment issues, and other production-related concerns that may impact operations.
  • Communicate production goals and delivery expectations to ensure on-time performance targets are understood and achieved.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in responding to changing business needs, priorities, and responsibilities.
  • Conduct quality inspections and audits in accordance with established quality procedures, customer requirements, and ISO standards.
  • Participate in Material Review Board (MRB) activities and contribute to quality improvement initiatives and problem-solving discussions.
  • Promote and maintain a safe work environment by adhering to all safety policies and ensuring proper use of required personal protective equipment (PPE).

 

 

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills are a must
  • 1-2 years of assembly experience with 3 years supervisory experience
  • Understanding of KPI (key performance indicators)
  • Understanding of Lean principles and responsibilities
  • Proficient computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs

 

Core Competencies:

  • Advanced operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Advanced verbal/written communication skills 
  • Advanced customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 

 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required

 

What we Offer 

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Title: Assembler
Location: Mocksville, NC (Onsite) (338 Valley Rd. Mocksville, NC 27028) 
Shift: 2nd shift (Monday - Friday -2pm - 10pm) Full Time, Direct Hire

 

Job Overview: 
This is a Rotary Test Technician role supporting the build and functional test of rotary screw and centrifugal air compressor packages. This is more than just a job; it’s an opportunity to be part of a company that values creativity, excellence, and collaboration



Responsibilities: 

  • Use computer software programs for controlling tests and analyze test data per acceptance criteria.
  • Layout, assemble, and install required electrical supply cabling, instrumentation, hose connections to water cooling systems, and compressed air outlet piping.
  • Troubleshoot and repair or replace instrumentation and/or product hardware due to test failures and read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, assembly instructions, bills of material, and quality control documents.
  • Ensures that all tools used in performing job duties are within calibration, as stated on calibration sticker. Where discrepancies arise, immediate notification of supervisor occurs and performs job duties with limited supervision. 
  • Uses problem solving skills (identify problems and respond correctly).  Shall be capable of performing disassembly and rebuild of air ends, or sensitive rotating assemblies.
  • Exhibits a high degree of manual dexterity with great attention to detail and workmanship and demonstrate use of calipers, dial, indicators, precision measuring devices.  


Requirements: 

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate and 2 years of testing experience in a manufacturing, aerospace, or similar environment
  • Repetitive assembly operations, grasping, standing, lifting, bending, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.
  • Able to stand for extended periods – 8 hours minimum and able to stoop, bend, crawl, and being able to maneuver in tight spaces.
  • Ability to read blueprints, schematics, and electrical wiring diagrams.
  • Ability to use correct tooling, fixturing and equipment to perform work tasks to engineering specifications. 



Core Competencies:  

  • Strong problem-solving skills (identify problems and respond correctly).



Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 

  • This position will be fully site based at our facility in Mocksville, NC.

job.description:

Job Title: Procurement Supervisor            
Location: Sedalia, MO
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Field Service Technician

Location: Northern Indiana or Ohio preferred - Remote
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

Requirements:

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

job.title: Quality Control Lead
job.description:
POSITION:                Quality Control Lead

DEPARTMENT:         Quality

REPORTS TO:          Site Quality Manager

FLSA STATUS:         Non-exempt

 

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Quality Lead is responsible for overseeing inspection activities to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, internal quality standards, and customer specifications. The Quality Lead demonstrates a strong knowledge of the ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 requirements. The Quality Lead interacts professionally with company management, internal departments, and customers on Quality related tasks. This position also manages and maintains day-to-day scheduling and workflow of the Quality Inspectors. They also support the management team by conducting training, performing troubleshooting, managing the daily shipment schedule, and generally supporting the QC department and Quality functions to ensure compliance with the company’s QMS requirements and established processes.

  

 

KEY ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Partner with departmental peers in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, purchasing, maintenance, and QC to monitor and ensure compliance with the quality assurance program established by the company.
  • Coordinate and manage daily schedules and work assignments of Quality Inspector personnel.
  • Lead the QC department in daily activities, such as visual and dimensional inspection, quality testing, Device History Record (DHR) review, and others as assigned.
  • Review and approve inspection records, nonconformance reports, and related documentation.
  • Cooperate with and act professionally with coworkers and managers.
  • Meet Flexan standards for quality, cleanliness, and productivity.
  • Follow all procedures for cleanroom operation, cleanroom attire, and contamination control.
  • Follow all Flexan procedures for traceability, line clearance, process control, safety, and housekeeping.
  • Accurately input data into ERP system daily (including clock in time, work orders worked on, operation worked on, indirect work performed, quantities of parts produced and quantities of parts that are deviated).
  • Participate in 5S activities and follow 5S procedures.
  • Conduct on-boarding and on-the-job training for new employees as needed.
  • Participate in interviewing candidates for inspection roles, assessing technical skills, and cultural fit.
  • Work closely with the Quality Manager to provide objective feedback and recommendations for development plans, training needs, and performance evaluations for inspection personnel.
  • Manage and maintain Flexan’s quarantine locations and ensure proper disposition of parts/materials.
  • Assist with root cause investigations driven through nonconformance reports (NCs) and CAPAs. 
  • Assist with internal and external audits, providing inspection-related documentation and evidence of compliance.
  • Assist in risk management activities including preventive actions, pFMEA and Control Plans.
  • Assist in the development of Dimensional, Quality Control, and other process sheets or work instructions.
  • Work with Engineering to develop vision system measurement teaching files for dimensional inspection.
  • Lead the execution of Gage R&Rs and other validation activities within the QC department.
  • Perform dimensional and visual inspections.
  • Identify opportunities to improve inspection processes, methods, and reduce defects.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, and presents well at all levels of the organization.
  • Works well independently and in a team environment, can lead people that are not direct reports, strong goal setting, follow up, organization and prioritization skills, and excellent attention to detail.
  • Strong computer skills and familiar with Microsoft Windows applications.
  • Medical Device Manufacturing environment experience preferred.
  • Demonstrable ability to analyze a wide variety of information and data to assist management decisions regarding potential risks that may impact product or compliance status.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to multitask.
  • Good work ethic (comes to work and returns from lunch and breaks on time, works hard to reach work standards, tries to minimize waste)
  • Team player that gets along well with others (respectful of supervisors and co-workers, helps others by offering assistance and ideas when appropriate)
  • Able to recognize and address both good and sub-standard performance (praise excellent performance and cooperation, recognize and immediately discuss any safety issues, identify and report interpersonal and attitude problems, recognize and either immediately stop or report any incidences of misuse of tools and equipment)
  • Is proactive in identifying potential problems or opportunities to increase productivity and quality, decrease waste and improve morale.
  • Follows through on tasks and projects as assigned.
  • Demonstrates all corporate values: 
    • We think and act like owners. 
    • We are bold in our aspirations while moving forward with humility and integrity. 
    • We are committed to making our customers successful. 
    • We foster inspired teams.  

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • The employee is required to work in a cleanroom environment and is expected to follow the guidelines and rules for working in the cleanroom. This includes following the gowning procedures, covering hair in a hairnet, and wearing personal protective equipment as appropriate.
  • While performing the duties of this position, the employee is frequently/occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts.
  • The employee is occasionally required to sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
  • The employee is frequently required to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

job.description:

Job Title:  Sustaining Engineer Manager

Location: Remote
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  
 
 
Job Overview:
The Sustaining Engineering Manager oversees all activities related to legacy product support, including production troubleshooting, supplier obsolescence management, cost-reduction initiatives, and design improvements (I2V). This role is responsible for setting team priorities, developing engineering talent, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals. The manager serves as the primary interface between engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and external partners to drive operational excellence and continuous improvement for legacy products. Lead and manage the Sustaining Engineering team responsible for supporting and improving legacy pump products, ensuring production continuity, supply chain resilience, and ongoing product quality through strategic leadership and cross-functional collaboration.
 
Responsibilities: 
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of sustaining engineers to support legacy pump production lines.
  • Oversee and prioritize the resolution of complex production and supplier issues to minimize downtime and ensure supply continuity.
  • Direct the identification and qualification of alternative components and suppliers to address obsolescence and mitigate supply risks.
  • Guide and approve I2V (Innovation to Value), cost-reduction, and design simplification projects to improve product performance and reduce costs.
  • Ensure all engineering changes and documentation updates comply with regulatory, quality, and company standards.
  • Drive root cause analysis and corrective action for recurring or high-impact production and field issues.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and R&D leadership to align on priorities and resource allocation.
  • Monitor and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to sustaining engineering activities, such as uptime, cost savings, and issue resolution.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and operational excellence within the team.
  • Manage team workload, performance, and professional development, including recruiting, training, and performance reviews.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for legacy product support with internal and external stakeholders.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline from an accredited institution (Master’s degree or MBA preferred).
  • 8+ years of relevant engineering experience 
  • 3+ years in a technical leadership or management role within pump solutions, fluid handling, or related industries.
 
Preferences:
  • Proactive, self-organized leader with strong organizational skills, strategic planning experience, and the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities effectively.
  • Strong customer-facing communicator with excellent verbal and written communication skills, active listening abilities, and the capability to uncover customer needs and articulate value propositions.
  • Technical and analytical problem solver with strong engineering principles, mechanical comprehension, and expertise in Fluid Power (Hydraulics, Pneumatics, and Electromechanical Systems).
  • Experienced cross-functional leader skilled at influencing teams, managing stakeholders, and driving business results through collaboration and effective team management.
  • Product and project execution expert with experience delivering impactful presentations, optimizing processes, and applying project management methodologies (PMP/Six Sigma certifications a plus).
  • Continuous learner and team mentor with experience developing junior engineers, adapting to evolving technologies, and supporting growth in Life Science market applications.
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements
  • Remote position
  • Availability to travel up to 15% of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is 120,000 - $150,000, excluding incentive opportunities. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Title: Assembler (First shift)
Location: Southern Pines, NC (Onsite)

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

 

Job Overview: 

We are looking for a skilled assembler to perform a variety of tasks as assigned in conjunction with the assembly of our product. You will ensure all parts fit correctly and are suitable for the final product. This position is responsible for safely performing high-level continuous work to quality standards. Assignments may change based on business demands. 

You must have desired technical knowledge and possess great manual dexterity. Ability to interpret instructions represented in manuals, drawings, schematics etc. and follow them with precision.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Read print drawings to determine dimensions, design, and materials for construction.
  • Assemble parts according to standard work / job breakdown sheets of unit being assembled, bill of materials and work order instructions, and assembly drawings 
  • Fastens parts together with bolts, screws, speed clips, rivets, or other fasteners according to torque specifications 
  • Operates pneumatic and manual presses to assist in assembly operation, which includes setting up the presses 
  • Set-up and operate identification equipment (stampers, labelers, etc.) 
  • Test product for compliance to meet specifications using manual and automatic test equipment 
  • Paint, label and pack completed product for shipment 
  • Achieve daily departmental productivity and quality levels 
  • Follow all ISO procedures and safety rules, including wearing personal safety equipment 
  • Keep Team Lead informed of mechanical/machine malfunctions or any supplies/tools needed 
  • Handle product to and from stock 
  • Perform in-process testing and make necessary corrections to meet standard work and Procedures for Qualification (PFQ) 
  • Notify team lead of non-conformance material

inventory replenishment planning and purchasing from multiple vendors (Domestic and International). A Buyer’s primary goal is to ensure the highest level of customer service while achieving high inventory turnover at the lowest total cost. This position will work closely and collaborate with the Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, Production, Customer Service, Distribution/Operations, Product Management, Accounting and Vendors.

  • 1+ years of purchasing experience in manufacturing
  • 2 + years relevant experience in inventory management, purchasing, production planning can be substituted for degree

  • Proven ability to understand best practices:
  • Demand & forecasting experience
  • Purchasing & inventory planning
  • MRP, safety stock, reorder-point, ABC analysis
  • Ability source data from multiple sources and analyze large amounts of data
  • Self- directed, flexible with a positive attitude
