Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

Job Overview: 
The Site Supply Chain Lead is an individual contributor role accountable for end-to-end supply chain planning across demand, supply, and production execution. This role owns production scheduling, capacity planning, and NPI readiness to ensure alignment with customer demand, operational constraints, and business objectives. This position serves as a central integrator across Sales, Operations, Engineering, and Procurement, driving data-based decisions, improving planning processes, and ensuring optimal service, cost, and inventory performance across multi-line manufacturing operations.

 

Responsibilities:  

  • Develop and manage the master production schedule (MPS) aligned to demand plans and capacity constraints
  • Ensure finite scheduling and sequence optimization to maximize throughput and minimize changeover and delays. Influence cross-functional stakeholders to align on priorities, resolve constraints, and drive execution against the plan.
  • Manage production work orders and maintain ERP/MRP accuracy for inventory, BOMs, planning parameters, and product lifecycle updates.
  • Review new customer orders to confirm capacity (labor, machines), materials, and design availability to meet customer dates. Monitor and manage past due orders, backlog, and service risk.
  • Lead and execute the monthly Supply Agreement process, including demand/supply balancing, scenario modeling, and risk identification
  • Develop and evaluate supply-demand scenarios resulting in actionable supply plans clearly articulating trade-offs across service, cost, and inventory to support decision-making.
  • Lead capacity planning for labor, machines, and materials across product lines; provide future capacity reports highlighting risks.
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to align raw material supply plans with inventory strategies and policies (e.g., safety stock, segmentation, reorder parameters) aligned to business objectives.
  • Support NPIs by integrating launch timelines into production planning and coordinating with cross-functional teams.
  

Qualifications:  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management or related field of study; comparable combination of education and years of experience will be considered 
  • 7+ years of work experience in Supply Chain or Production Planning/ Scheduling 
  • 3+ years of experience with ERP/MRP systems, such as SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • 1+ years of experience and extensive knowledge of the flow of data through entire manufacturing process – from design conception to shipment of product
  • Must be able to work on government contracts directly or access shared data resources (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident of the U.S.) 

Preferences:
  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred   
  • Proficiency in Excel and other data analysis tools. 
  • Experience in a regulated, lot-controlled manufacturing environment or clean room environment preferred    
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively work in cross-functional teams in a lead capacity or as a participant 
  • Experience or training with Lean and Visual Factory manufacturing tools  
  • Demonstrated strong, analytical skills, problem solving and learning ability 
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with all levels of team membership 
  • Ability to work within defined process and identify process improvements, drive improvements and sustain improvements; Ability to get results through process 
  • Demonstrated comprehension and experience with various business models and their effect on supply chain structure, planning and execution 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site base in Chicago, IL

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is Min - $103,000 -$120,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

À propos de nous

Ingersoll Rand est une entreprise Fortune 500 passionnée par l'amélioration de la vie. Nous y parvenons en incarnant nos valeurs, en nous concentrant sans relâche sur la réussite de nos clients et en collaborant avec nos employés pour penser et agir comme des propriétaires. Ingersoll Rand valorise un environnement diversifié et inclusif. Pour plus d'informations, visitez : www.irco.com.

Aperçu du poste
Le préposé à la manutention / journalier général soutient les activités de production et de logistique de l’entrepôt. Ce rôle consiste principalement à conduire des chariots élévateurs, recevoir les marchandises entrantes, préparer avec précision les pièces requises pour les ordres de production, effectuer des comptages cycliques d’inventaire et saisir des données exactes dans le système ERP afin de maintenir un environnement de travail efficace et performant.

Responsabilités:

• Réception des marchandises

  • Recevoir les expéditions entrantes.
  • Vérifier les quantités livrées par rapport aux bordereaux d’expédition.
  • Inspecter les marchandises afin de détecter tout dommage.
  • Enregistrer toutes les réceptions dans le système ERP.
  •  

• Gestion et maintien de l’inventaire

  • Assurer le maintien des niveaux d’inventaire en identifiant, étiquetant et entreposant adéquatement les matériaux et fournitures.
  • Consigner l’emplacement exact des articles en stock.
  • Signaler rapidement toute pénurie ou variation d’inventaire.

 

• Conduite de chariot élévateur

  • Utiliser les chariots élévateurs motorisés de façon sécuritaire pour charger, décharger, déplacer et empiler les matières premières, les marchandises reçues et les produits finis.

 

• Préparation des commandes de production

  • Sélectionner avec exactitude les articles, pièces et matériaux requis dans l’aire d’entreposage.
  • Approvisionner les lignes d’assemblage et soutenir les calendriers de production dans les délais prévus.

• Comptage cyclique

  • Effectuer des inventaires physiques réguliers.
  • Comparer les quantités physiques aux données du système afin d’identifier et de corriger les écarts.

• Travaux généraux et entretien

  • Balayer les planchers.
  • Débarrasser les allées des débris et obstacles.
  • Éliminer les déchets de fabrication conformément aux procédures établies.
  • Maintenir les rayonnages à palettes propres et organisés.

Compétences et exigences:

• Certification

  • Certification valide de conducteur de chariot élévateur obligatoire.

• Compétences techniques

  • Connaissances de base en informatique.
  • Expérience avec un système ERP (p. ex. SAP, Oracle, NetSuite) ou un logiciel de gestion d’entrepôt (WMS).

• Souci du détail

  • Grande précision dans la vérification des numéros de série, des codes d’articles (SKU) et des quantités physiques lors des réceptions et de la préparation des commandes.

• Endurance physique

  • Capacité à demeurer debout pendant de longues périodes.
  • Aptitude à soulever des charges de 50 à 70 lb (23 à 32 kg).

• Santé et sécurité

  • Bonne connaissance des règles de sécurité au travail.
  • Compréhension et utilisation appropriée de l’équipement de protection individuelle (EPI).
  • Connaissance des procédures de communication des risques et des normes de santé et sécurité.

Location: 190 Av. du Voyageur #100, Pointe-Claire, Québec H9R 6A

Job Overview:

The Material Handler / General Labourer supports production and warehouse logistics. This role focuses on operating forklifts, receiving incoming goods, picking accurate parts for production orders, performing routine cycle counts, and logging accurate data into the ERP system to maintain a highly efficient facility.

Responsibilities:

  • Material Receiving: Receive incoming shipments, verify delivery quantities against packing slips, inspect goods for damage, and log all receipts into the ERP system.
  • Inventory Maintenance: Maintain inventory by identifying, labeling, and keeping materials and supplies in stock, recording the exact location of inventory, and promptly reporting shortages.
  • Forklift Operation: Drive motorized forklifts safely to load, unload, transfer, and stack raw materials, received goods, and finished products.
  • Production Order Picking: Accurately retrieve specific items, parts, and materials from storage to feed assembly lines and satisfy production schedules on time.
  • Cycle Counting: Perform regular physical inventory counts and cross-reference physical quantities with system records to identify gaps.
  • General Labour & Cleanup: Sweep floors, clear debris from walkways, dispose of manufacturing waste, and organize pallet racking.

Skills/Requirements:

  • Certification: Active and valid Forklift Operator Certification is mandatory.
  • Technical Skills: Basic computer literacy with previous experience using an ERP system (e.g., SAP, Oracle, NetSuite) or warehouse management software.
  • Detail-Oriented: Exceptional accuracy in matching serial numbers, SKUs, and physical counts during receiving and production picks.
  • Physical Stamina: Competency to stand for long intervals and lift heavy items weighing 50 to 70 lbs.
  • Safety Awareness: Solid knowledge of workplace safety rules, personal protective equipment (PPE), and hazard communication standards.

Job Overview

As a Welder at Fruitland Manufacturing, you will be responsible for fitting, assembling, and welding metal components used in the manufacturing of our products. Working from fabrication drawings and specifications, you will use various welding processes to produce high-quality components that meet customer and company standards.

This hands-on role requires strong welding and fitting skills, attention to detail, and the ability to read and interpret fabrication drawings. You will work both independently and as part of the production team while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, and productivity. You may also operate various metalworking equipment, including press brakes, shears, saws, roll-forming machines, forklifts, and cranes, with company training provided where required.

Responsibilities

  • Read and understand fabrication blueprints and drawings.
  • Fit metal components according to specifications and fabrication drawings while ensuring all tolerances are met.
  • Perform welding using GMAW (MIG), GTAW (TIG), and FCAW processes.
  • Operate welding equipment (manual and semi-automatic) and various metal shaping machines.
  • Complete all assigned work within established timelines while complying with health and safety regulations and company procedures.
  • Perform basic maintenance of welding equipment.
  • Operate metalworking equipment such as shears, press brakes, roll-forming machines, and saws as required.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Collaborate with production team members to ensure quality and productivity goals are achieved.

Requirements

  • Technical trade school certification in Welding.
  • Minimum 1-2 years of welding experience.
  • Minimum 1-2 years of fitting experience.
  • Basic computer skills.
  • Ability to read and interpret fabrication drawings and prints.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to read and understand drawings in English.
  • Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
  • Excellent manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs.

Core Competencies

  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Commitment to workplace safety and quality standards.
  • Excellent teamwork and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.


This position will be based at our facility in Stoney Creek, Ontario, with no anticipated travel.

Job Overview: 
The Site Supply Chain Lead is an individual contributor role accountable for end-to-end supply chain planning across demand, supply, and production execution. This role owns production scheduling, capacity planning, and NPI readiness to ensure alignment with customer demand, operational constraints, and business objectives. This position serves as a central integrator across Sales, Operations, Engineering, and Procurement, driving data-based decisions, improving planning processes, and ensuring optimal service, cost, and inventory performance across multi-line manufacturing operations.

 

Responsibilities:  

  • Develop and manage the master production schedule (MPS) aligned to demand plans and capacity constraints
  • Ensure finite scheduling and sequence optimization to maximize throughput and minimize changeover and delays. Influence cross-functional stakeholders to align on priorities, resolve constraints, and drive execution against the plan.
  • Manage production work orders and maintain ERP/MRP accuracy for inventory, BOMs, planning parameters, and product lifecycle updates.
  • Review new customer orders to confirm capacity (labor, machines), materials, and design availability to meet customer dates. Monitor and manage past due orders, backlog, and service risk.
  • Lead and execute the monthly Supply Agreement process, including demand/supply balancing, scenario modeling, and risk identification
  • Develop and evaluate supply-demand scenarios resulting in actionable supply plans clearly articulating trade-offs across service, cost, and inventory to support decision-making.
  • Lead capacity planning for labor, machines, and materials across product lines; provide future capacity reports highlighting risks.
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to align raw material supply plans with inventory strategies and policies (e.g., safety stock, segmentation, reorder parameters) aligned to business objectives.
  • Support NPIs by integrating launch timelines into production planning and coordinating with cross-functional teams.
  

Qualifications:  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management or related field of study; comparable combination of education and years of experience will be considered 
  • 7+ years of work experience in Supply Chain or Production Planning/ Scheduling 
  • 3+ years of experience with ERP/MRP systems, such as SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • 1+ years of experience and extensive knowledge of the flow of data through entire manufacturing process – from design conception to shipment of product
  • Must be able to work on government contracts directly or access shared data resources (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident of the U.S.) 

Preferences:
  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred   
  • Proficiency in Excel and other data analysis tools. 
  • Experience in a regulated, lot-controlled manufacturing environment or clean room environment preferred    
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively work in cross-functional teams in a lead capacity or as a participant 
  • Experience or training with Lean and Visual Factory manufacturing tools  
  • Demonstrated strong, analytical skills, problem solving and learning ability 
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with all levels of team membership 
  • Ability to work within defined process and identify process improvements, drive improvements and sustain improvements; Ability to get results through process 
  • Demonstrated comprehension and experience with various business models and their effect on supply chain structure, planning and execution 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site base in Chicago, IL

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is Min - $103,000 -$120,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, an Ingersoll Rand Company, is looking for a Mechanical Engineer / CAD Designer who is looking for a role where no two designs are the same. Bring your expertise, and preferable electromechanical, PLC skills and work on rotating equipment skid design.  Join a dynamic team where every project brings something new—whether it's custom-engineered blower packaging or adapting standard product lines to fit unique spaces. This is true Engineer-to-Order (ETO) work that keeps things fresh and challenging.

Our core market? Wastewater treatment. It’s an industry that never slows down, which means you’ll enjoy long-term stability and job security while making a meaningful impact on essential infrastructure. You’ll wear multiple hats, work hard, and thrive in a fast-paced environment—but you won’t do it alone. Our team collaborates closely, supports one another, and knows how to have fun along the way.  If you’re energized by variety, enjoy problem-solving, and want to be part of a team that delivers real solutions while having a good time doing it, this is the opportunity for you.

Responsibilities:

  • Design structural steel skids using SolidWorks 3D software
  • Create engineering submittal documents per project specifications
  • Communicate with customers regarding product design and specifications
  • Generate bills of material, cut lists and fabrication drawings
  • Create and interpret mechanical engineering drawings
  • Participate in finished equipment run testing
  • Inspect completed assembled equipment skids
  • Support the sales department with technical information
  • Interact with shop fabrication & assembly personnel

  • 3+ years equivalent work experience
  • 3+ years of experience with 3D CAD software
  • 2+ years working with and understanding of structural steel metal fabrication and pipe weldments

Core Competencies:

  • Ability to communicate with customers’ engineering departments
  • Ability to multi-task and work with multiple projects
  • Strong problem solving and project management skills
  • Strong English communication skills, oral and written
  • Ability to work in a small office environment and collaborate with peers

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree concentration in: Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Technology, or Electro-mechanical Engineering Technology.
  • A Computer Aided Drafting degree or certificate will be considered.
  • Proficiency in SolidWorks
  • Experience in sheet metal forming
  • Knowledge of electrical controls and wiring
  • Experience with FEA tools and design validation methods

Travel and Work Arrangements

Job Overview:

Fruitland Manufacturing is seeking an experienced CNC Machinist to join our growing team in Stoney Creek, Ontario. Due to increased production demands and additional work being brought into the facility, we are adding two Machinists to support our operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for a skilled machinist with strong CNC setup, troubleshooting, and programming experience. We are looking for professionals who can independently set up tooling, make programming adjustments, perform inspections, and ensure high-quality production while maintaining a safe and productive work environment.
The successful candidate will work primarily on CNC machining centers utilizing Fanuc controls and will play a key role in producing precision components that support mission-critical applications across multiple industries.
Please note: This position currently operates on a day shift schedule; however, candidates must be willing and able to transition to a future second-shift operation if business needs require it. A $2.00 per hour shift premium applies to second-shift assignments.

Responsibilities
  • Operate CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Perform machine setups, including tooling changes, fixture setup, program loading, and first-piece inspections.
  • Perform basic CNC programming and make adjustments directly at the machine controller.
  • Organize tooling requirements and verify fixture readiness for production jobs.
  • Troubleshoot CNC programming issues and machine fault codes.
  • Maintain precise tolerances and quality standards during production.
  • Follow all plant safety requirements and ISO procedures.
  • Log and track production activities using the GSS ERP system.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Collaborate with team members to achieve production and quality objectives.
Requirements
 
  • Operating CNC horizontal, vertical and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Performing basic CNC programming.
  • Setting up CNC machine including changing tools, fixtures, running programs, completing first off inspections
  • Identifying and resolving programming issues and CNC fault codes.
  • Maintaining sharp focus and attention to detail to ensure precision and quality in all operations.
  • Following all plant safety rules, ISO procedures
  • Logging and tracking time using GSS ERP system


Requirements:

  • Minimum 5+ years of CNC machining experience.
  • Strong CNC machine setup experience.
  • Experience operating CNC machining centers with Fanuc controls preferred.
  • Ability to perform basic CNC programming and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with tooling selection, fixture setup, and process optimization.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.

Qualifications:

  • Experience operating CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis machining centers.
  • Strong understanding of CNC setup and production processes.
  • Ability to identify and resolve programming and machine issues.
  • Knowledge of precision measurement tools and inspection techniques.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers, fractions, and decimals.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational abilities.

 Preferred Qualifications: Red Seal certification in 429A General Machinist or 430A Tool and Die Maker.

Job Overview: 
The Site Supply Chain Lead is an individual contributor role accountable for end-to-end supply chain planning across demand, supply, and production execution. This role owns production scheduling, capacity planning, and NPI readiness to ensure alignment with customer demand, operational constraints, and business objectives. This position serves as a central integrator across Sales, Operations, Engineering, and Procurement, driving data-based decisions, improving planning processes, and ensuring optimal service, cost, and inventory performance across multi-line manufacturing operations.

 

Responsibilities:  

  • Develop and manage the master production schedule (MPS) aligned to demand plans and capacity constraints
  • Ensure finite scheduling and sequence optimization to maximize throughput and minimize changeover and delays. Influence cross-functional stakeholders to align on priorities, resolve constraints, and drive execution against the plan.
  • Manage production work orders and maintain ERP/MRP accuracy for inventory, BOMs, planning parameters, and product lifecycle updates.
  • Review new customer orders to confirm capacity (labor, machines), materials, and design availability to meet customer dates. Monitor and manage past due orders, backlog, and service risk.
  • Lead and execute the monthly Supply Agreement process, including demand/supply balancing, scenario modeling, and risk identification
  • Develop and evaluate supply-demand scenarios resulting in actionable supply plans clearly articulating trade-offs across service, cost, and inventory to support decision-making.
  • Lead capacity planning for labor, machines, and materials across product lines; provide future capacity reports highlighting risks.
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to align raw material supply plans with inventory strategies and policies (e.g., safety stock, segmentation, reorder parameters) aligned to business objectives.
  • Support NPIs by integrating launch timelines into production planning and coordinating with cross-functional teams.
  

Qualifications:  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management or related field of study; comparable combination of education and years of experience will be considered 
  • 7+ years of work experience in Supply Chain or Production Planning/ Scheduling 
  • 3+ years of experience with ERP/MRP systems, such as SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • 1+ years of experience and extensive knowledge of the flow of data through entire manufacturing process – from design conception to shipment of product
  • Must be able to work on government contracts directly or access shared data resources (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident of the U.S.) 

Preferences:
  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred   
  • Proficiency in Excel and other data analysis tools. 
  • Experience in a regulated, lot-controlled manufacturing environment or clean room environment preferred    
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively work in cross-functional teams in a lead capacity or as a participant 
  • Experience or training with Lean and Visual Factory manufacturing tools  
  • Demonstrated strong, analytical skills, problem solving and learning ability 
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with all levels of team membership 
  • Ability to work within defined process and identify process improvements, drive improvements and sustain improvements; Ability to get results through process 
  • Demonstrated comprehension and experience with various business models and their effect on supply chain structure, planning and execution 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site base in Chicago, IL

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is Min - $103,000 -$120,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company with a passion for making lives better.  We do this by living our values, and through a relentless focus on the success of our customers and partnering with our employees to think and act like owners. Job Overview:

Fruitland Manufacturing is seeking an experienced CNC Machinist to join our growing team in Stoney Creek, Ontario. Due to increased production demands and additional work being brought into the facility, we are adding two Machinists to support our operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for a skilled machinist with strong CNC setup, troubleshooting, and programming experience. We are looking for professionals who can independently set up tooling, make programming adjustments, perform inspections, and ensure high-quality production while maintaining a safe and productive work environment.
The successful candidate will work primarily on CNC machining centers utilizing Fanuc controls and will play a key role in producing precision components that support mission-critical applications across multiple industries.
Please note: This position currently operates on a day shift schedule; however, candidates must be willing and able to transition to a future second-shift operation if business needs require it. A $2.00 per hour shift premium applies to second-shift assignments.

Responsibilities
  • Operate CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Perform machine setups, including tooling changes, fixture setup, program loading, and first-piece inspections.
  • Perform basic CNC programming and make adjustments directly at the machine controller.
  • Organize tooling requirements and verify fixture readiness for production jobs.
  • Troubleshoot CNC programming issues and machine fault codes.
  • Maintain precise tolerances and quality standards during production.
  • Follow all plant safety requirements and ISO procedures.
  • Log and track production activities using the GSS ERP system.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Collaborate with team members to achieve production and quality objectives.
Requirements
 
  • Operating CNC horizontal, vertical and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Performing basic CNC programming.
  • Setting up CNC machine including changing tools, fixtures, running programs, completing first off inspections
  • Identifying and resolving programming issues and CNC fault codes.
  • Maintaining sharp focus and attention to detail to ensure precision and quality in all operations.
  • Following all plant safety rules, ISO procedures
  • Logging and tracking time using GSS ERP system


Requirements:

  • Minimum 5+ years of CNC machining experience.
  • Strong CNC machine setup experience.
  • Experience operating CNC machining centers with Fanuc controls preferred.
  • Ability to perform basic CNC programming and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with tooling selection, fixture setup, and process optimization.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.

Qualifications:

  • Experience operating CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis machining centers.
  • Strong understanding of CNC setup and production processes.
  • Ability to identify and resolve programming and machine issues.
  • Knowledge of precision measurement tools and inspection techniques.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers, fractions, and decimals.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational abilities.

 Preferred Qualifications: Red Seal certification in 429A General Machinist or 430A Tool and Die Maker.

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly motivated Cooling System Design Engineer to support the design, development, and delivery of cooling infrastructure for hyperscale, enterprise, and colocation data center projects. This role is responsible for designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable thermal management solutions that support mission-critical environments.

The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams, equipment vendors, construction partners, and project stakeholders to develop cooling system designs that meet performance, energy efficiency, scalability, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Responsibilities:

Cooling System Design

  • Develop conceptual, preliminary, and detailed designs for data center cooling systems.
  • Design and optimize chilled water, direct expansion (DX), liquid cooling, air-side and water-side economization systems.
  • Perform cooling load calculations and thermal analyses for white space, support spaces, and critical infrastructure areas.
  • Develop HVAC system layouts, piping schematics, flow diagrams, and equipment specifications.
  • Evaluate emerging cooling technologies, including direct-to-chip and immersion cooling solutions.
Engineering & Technical Analysis

  • Conduct system sizing calculations for chillers, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, pumps, heat exchangers, and associated equipment.
  • Perform computational modeling and simulations to validate cooling performance and energy efficiency.
  • Support CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) analyses for airflow management and thermal optimization.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, and industry best practices.
Project Delivery

  • Support project planning, design reviews, and technical coordination throughout all project phases.
  • Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, structural, controls, and commissioning teams.
  • Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Provide engineering support during procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Resolve design and field issues while maintaining schedule and budget commitments.
Sustainability & Energy Efficiency

  • Design solutions that achieve high levels of energy efficiency and operational resiliency.
  • Support PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) optimization initiatives.
  • Evaluate energy consumption and lifecycle cost impacts of cooling system alternatives.
  • Contribute to corporate sustainability and carbon reduction goals.
Documentation & Standards

  • Prepare engineering reports, calculations, technical specifications, and design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain design standards and best practices for data center cooling infrastructure.
  • Ensure complete and accurate project documentation is maintained throughout the project lifecycle.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in HVAC, mission-critical facilities, or data center infrastructure design.
    • 1+ years of experience performing HVAC load calculations and system sizing  
    Core Competencies

    • Data Center Thermal Management
    • HVAC Design Engineering
    • Mission-Critical Infrastructure
    • Cooling System Optimization
    • Energy Efficiency & Sustainability
    • CFD Analysis
    • Technical Documentation
    • Vendor & Stakeholder Management
    • Risk Assessment & Problem Solving
    • Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
      
    Preferred Qualifications
    • Experience supporting hyperscale or large-scale data center projects.
    • Familiarity with ASHRAE Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments.
    • Experience with CFD modeling tools such as 6SigmaDCX, Future Facilities, or equivalent.
    • Knowledge of liquid cooling technologies for AI/HPC workloads.
    • Experience with Uptime Institute Tier standards and TIA-942 requirements.
    • LEED Accreditation or experience with sustainable design initiatives.
    • Project management experience in multi-disciplinary engineering environments.
    • Proficiency with engineering design software such as:
      • AutoCAD
      • Revit
      • BIM platforms
      • HVAC modeling tools
    • Strong knowledge of:
      • Air-cooled and water-cooled chillers
      • Chilled water systems
      • Cooling towers
      • CRAH and CRAC systems
      • Pumping systems
      • Heat exchangers
      • Building Management Systems (BMS)

Job Tittle: Cooling System Design Engineer

Location: Junction City, OR

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly motivated Cooling System Design Engineer to support the design, development, and delivery of cooling infrastructure for hyperscale, enterprise, and colocation data center projects. This role is responsible for designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable thermal management solutions that support mission-critical environments.

The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams, equipment vendors, construction partners, and project stakeholders to develop cooling system designs that meet performance, energy efficiency, scalability, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Responsibilities:

Cooling System Design

  • Develop conceptual, preliminary, and detailed designs for data center cooling systems.
  • Design and optimize chilled water, direct expansion (DX), liquid cooling, air-side and water-side economization systems.
  • Perform cooling load calculations and thermal analyses for white space, support spaces, and critical infrastructure areas.
  • Develop HVAC system layouts, piping schematics, flow diagrams, and equipment specifications.
  • Evaluate emerging cooling technologies, including direct-to-chip and immersion cooling solutions.
Engineering & Technical Analysis

  • Conduct system sizing calculations for chillers, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, pumps, heat exchangers, and associated equipment.
  • Perform computational modeling and simulations to validate cooling performance and energy efficiency.
  • Support CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) analyses for airflow management and thermal optimization.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, and industry best practices.
Project Delivery

  • Support project planning, design reviews, and technical coordination throughout all project phases.
  • Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, structural, controls, and commissioning teams.
  • Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Provide engineering support during procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Resolve design and field issues while maintaining schedule and budget commitments.
Sustainability & Energy Efficiency

  • Design solutions that achieve high levels of energy efficiency and operational resiliency.
  • Support PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) optimization initiatives.
  • Evaluate energy consumption and lifecycle cost impacts of cooling system alternatives.
  • Contribute to corporate sustainability and carbon reduction goals.
Documentation & Standards

  • Prepare engineering reports, calculations, technical specifications, and design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain design standards and best practices for data center cooling infrastructure.
  • Ensure complete and accurate project documentation is maintained throughout the project lifecycle.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in HVAC, mission-critical facilities, or data center infrastructure design.
    • 1+ years of experience performing HVAC load calculations and system sizing  
    Core Competencies

    • Data Center Thermal Management
    • HVAC Design Engineering
    • Mission-Critical Infrastructure
    • Cooling System Optimization
    • Energy Efficiency & Sustainability
    • CFD Analysis
    • Technical Documentation
    • Vendor & Stakeholder Management
    • Risk Assessment & Problem Solving
    • Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
      
    Preferred Qualifications
    • Experience supporting hyperscale or large-scale data center projects.
    • Familiarity with ASHRAE Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments.
    • Experience with CFD modeling tools such as 6SigmaDCX, Future Facilities, or equivalent.
    • Knowledge of liquid cooling technologies for AI/HPC workloads.
    • Experience with Uptime Institute Tier standards and TIA-942 requirements.
    • LEED Accreditation or experience with sustainable design initiatives.
    • Project management experience in multi-disciplinary engineering environments.
    • Proficiency with engineering design software such as:
      • AutoCAD
      • Revit
      • BIM platforms
      • HVAC modeling tools
    • Strong knowledge of:
      • Air-cooled and water-cooled chillers
      • Chilled water systems
      • Cooling towers
      • CRAH and CRAC systems
      • Pumping systems
      • Heat exchangers
      • Building Management Systems (BMS)
    Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

    • Fully site based

Location:  Remote, USA 
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview:
Early in your career in corporate insurance risk and workers’ compensation claims and ready to step into a role with real visibility into enterprise risk and insurance programs? This is where it happens.

As our Enterprise Risk Analyst, Corp Insurance & Worker's Comp Claims you’ll partner closely with the Enterprise Insurance Manager to support Ingersoll Rand’s global risk management, workers; comp and insurance programs. This hands-on, highly collaborative role involves working across internal teams, insurance brokers, and third-party administrators to manage insurance processes, claims activity, and compliance requirements. You will play a key role in the annual insurance renewal process, coordinating exposure data and supporting broker submissions and policy updates.

Your attention to detail will be critical as you manage Certificates of Insurance requests, reviewing contract requirements and endorsements to ensure accuracy. This position also supports monopolistic state workers’ compensation renewals and quarterly filings, assists with excise tax reporting, and helps monitor workers’ compensation and motor vehicle claims through third-party administrator systems—keeping the business protected and compliant.

This role is ideal for an early–mid career professional with a background in corporate risk, insurance, claims, or workers’ compensation (including legal or paralegal experience) who enjoys detail-oriented work, cross-functional coordination, and making a meaningful impact on the business.

Responsibilities:

  • Assist with data collection for the insurance renewal process, including exposure gathering (statement of values, payroll, revenues, headcount, miles driven), completion of applications, coordination of insurer/broker meetings, receipt and filing of binders and policies.

  • Primary point of contact for requests from the field, vendors, commercial teams or landlords for new or updated certificates of insurance (based on contractual requirements).

  • Assist with the process to review insurance provisions in contracts, leases and other agreements and request documentation required from insurance brokers.

  • Administer and monitor for compliance insurance filings required for monopolistic state workers compensation programs, and excise tax reporting.

  • Assist in identifying, assessing, and controlling the company's risks by running reports to analyze loss and exposure information. 

  • Manage the accurate and timely payment of insurance premiums, assessments, and fees.

  • Assist in day-to-day claims management, including reporting, information gathering, and follow-up, and active communication with the third-party adjusters to secure positive outcome of claim investigations, settlements and closures.

  • Interface with internal departments (Finance, Safety, Legal, Human Resources, Compliance and IR Business Units) and insurance broker, carriers, third-party administrators, and state insurance commissions.


Requirements

  • High School Diploma or GED with equivalent related work experience.

  • 2+ years of experience in state workers compensation claims, insurance claims management, and/or a related finance function.

  • 3+ years of experience building and maintaining effective cross-functional partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

  • 3+ years of demonstrated ability communicating effectively and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.

  • 3+ years of demonstrated experience managing work independently, taking initiative, and driving tasks to completion.

  • 3+ years proven experience working with Windows applications and Microsoft Office Suite.


Core Competencies

  • Insurance & Risk Program Support:  Ability to support enterprise insurance and risk management programs, including renewals, exposure data coordination, policy documentation, and compliance filings.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership: Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal teams, insurance brokers, carriers, and third-party administrators to ensure risk management activities move forward smoothly.

  • Claims Coordination & Insurance Operations: Support day-to-day claims activity, including reporting, information gathering, tracking through third-party administrator systems, and communication with adjusters and partners to advance claims resolution.

  • Analytical & Data Interpretation: Ability to analyze exposure and loss data from multiple sources, identify trends, and provide clear, accurate interpretations to support risk and insurance decision-making.

  • Detail Orientation & Process Accuracy: Maintain high accuracy when managing certificates of insurance, policy documentation, compliance filings, and financial transactions such as premiums, taxes, and assessments.


Preferences

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or related field

  • Experience as a paralegal supporting workers’ compensation legal matters

  • Direct claims experience or experience serving within a major insurance brokerage

  • Ability to quickly learn new software and systems


Travel and Work Arrangements 

  • This role is USA Remotely based

  • Anticipated travel is less than 5 percent

  • Must be a US Citizen or a legal Permanent Resident


Pay Range: The base salary range for this role is $45,000 - $65,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.



Summary of Position

 

This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned

Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

 

Education Requirements / Certifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

 

Experience / Skill Requirements         

  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred

 

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

Job Title: Plant Controller                    
Location: Junction City, OR
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Help shape the finances behind a growing manufacturing operation. Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Plant Controller for its Junction City, Oregon site. As a trusted partner to plant leadership and the production team, you’ll turn financial insight and firsthand operational knowledge into greater cost efficiency, revenue growth, stronger margins, and improved net working capital. With demand from the data center market driving plans for increased production and workforce growth, Junction City is entering an exciting new chapter. You’ll help set its financial direction, give leaders clearer visibility into performance, and build the financial discipline needed to scale.

Work alongside production leaders on the plant floor to connect daily decisions with financial results. You’ll investigate production and purchase price variances, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns while bringing clarity to cost rollups, inventory valuation, reserves, and the metrics that matter most to the plant. Bring your accounting and finance expertise, curiosity, and business judgment to a role where the numbers lead to action. You’ll identify trends, solve root causes, strengthen analytics, and manage plant accounting while helping leaders improve performance and plan for growth.

Ready for your next step? You’ll lead a small site-based team, with a planned transition and direct knowledge transfer to help you take ownership of daily and weekly responsibilities within approximately three to six months. Prior Plant Controller experience is not required. An Assistant Controller, Senior Cost Accountant, Cost Accounting Manager, or similar professional with hands-on manufacturing experience and leadership potential could thrive here. If you can point to the KPIs you’ve improved and the measurable impact of your work, this is your chance to influence a growing plant’s performance and build your future with Ingersoll Rand.

Responsibilities:
  • Management Reporting: Deliver month-end analysis that explains financial results, trends, risks, opportunities, and their implications. Prepare the monthly operating review and report on weekly shipping trends, order rates, backlog, and net working capital metrics, including inventory performance.
  • Controls and Compliance: Maintain a strong control environment through adherence to SOX requirements and proactive partnership with internal and external auditors. Identify and resolve control gaps, and build a culture of compliance across the team. Key processes include revenue cutoff, warranty and obsolescence reserves, other valuation reserves, and account reconciliations.
  • ERP Process Improvement: Improve Epicor configurations and automation by strengthening internal processes and establishing standard work.
  • Forecasting and Budgeting: Partner with finance and business stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate forecasts and assess P&L and balance sheet risks and opportunities. Forecast bookings, revenue growth, production variances, overhead spending, and capital investments.
  • CSS and Corporate Partnership: Respond promptly to requests from shared financial services, corporate FP&A, and CSS leadership to support business performance.
  • Operational Business Partnership: Partner with plant and cross-functional leaders to provide analysis and decision support that advances annual operating plan targets. Participate in and lead IRX (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) processes that support tactical and strategic objectives.
  • Team Leadership and Development: Align the team around corporate objectives, develop talent, and build the coverage needed for business continuity. Coach and mentor direct and indirect reports through succession planning, development plans, and the removal of barriers to engagement and progress.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related business concentration. 
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, controllership, or cost-accounting 
  • 3+ years experience with Excel using complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and / or financial modeling.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated ability analyzing financial performance, identifying root causes, and translating findings into actionable recommendations. 
  • 2+ years experience with ERP systems such as Epicor or something similar 

Core Competencies
  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting: Working knowledge of manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costs and cost rollups, inventory reserves and valuation, production variances, purchase price variance, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns.
  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to interpret complex financial data, derive actionable insights, and communicate key findings clearly and concisely to team members at all levels.
  • Problem-Solving and Continuous Improvement: Proactively identifies issues, evaluates root causes, and implements effective solutions with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Manufacturing Accounting Acumen: Strong numerical and analytical skills, with a careful, structured approach to applying accounting principles within a manufacturing environment.
  • Collaboration and Influence: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to support cross-functional initiatives, build productive working relationships, and influence stakeholders across the organization.
  • Leadership: Ability to drive performance through others, support colleagues in pursuit of shared team goals, and maintain accountability for deliverables.
  • Communication and Coaching: Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain financial concepts clearly and influence and coach teams toward financial and operational objectives.
  • Time and Priority Management: Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and manage multiple projects efficiently while meeting established deadlines and deliverables.

Preferences:
  • MBA or professional certification such as CMA, CFA, or CPA.
  • Experience in SOX compliance requirements, financial or operational audits, and audit engagements.
  • Demonstrated project-management experience
  • Experience using Epicor 

Travel and Work Arrangements: 
  • This position is onsite
  • Anticipated travel approximately 10%

job.title: Quality Technician
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

Summary of Position

This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned

Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

Education Requirements / Certifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

 

Experience / Skill Requirements         

  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred

 

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

job.title: Cybersecurity Engineer
job.description:
Cyber Security Engineer

About the Role

At Ingersoll Rand, we're committed to protecting our global operations through innovative and effective cybersecurity solutions. We are seeking a highly skilled Cyber Security Engineer to join our Security Operations team. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and enhancing security technologies that safeguard both traditional enterprise IT systems and industrial OT/ICS environments across our global manufacturing footprint.

This is a hands-on technical position that works closely with infrastructure, application, cloud, and manufacturing teams to develop scalable security controls, improve threat detection capabilities, automate operational processes, and strengthen the organization's overall security posture.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and support security technologies across endpoint, network, cloud, identity, email, and data protection environments.
  • Develop and optimize threat detection use cases, correlation rules, and alerting capabilities within SIEM and MDR platforms.
  • Build and maintain security automation solutions that improve operational efficiency and accelerate incident response.
  • Act as a senior technical resource during cybersecurity incidents, assisting with investigation, containment, forensic analysis, and root cause determination.
  • Conduct security architecture reviews for applications, cloud environments, integrations, and newly acquired businesses.
  • Lead vulnerability management and security hardening initiatives, including configuration baselines, risk assessments, and remediation planning.
  • Develop scripts, API integrations, dashboards, and reporting solutions to enhance operational visibility and monitoring.
  • Create and maintain technical documentation, standards, procedures, and security runbooks while providing guidance and mentorship to security team members.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity engineering, security operations, or infrastructure security within a complex enterprise environment.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise security technologies such as EDR/XDR, SIEM, IAM, email security, secure web gateways, or SASE solutions.
  • Experience developing automation using Python and/or PowerShell, including integrations through REST APIs.
  • Strong understanding of the MITRE ATT&CK Framework and its application to threat detection, threat hunting, and security validation.
  • Solid knowledge of networking, operating systems, cloud security (Azure and/or AWS), and identity security concepts.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting cybersecurity programs within manufacturing, industrial, or OT/ICS environments.
  • Hands-on experience with technologies such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Security (Defender, Entra ID, Purview), Zscaler, or modern SOAR platforms.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity initiatives related to mergers and acquisitions.
  • Industry certifications such as CISSP, GCIH, GCIA, GDAT, GCED, GICSP, or cloud security certifications.
  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Key Success Factors
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to independently lead projects from design through implementation.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality solutions.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while maintaining a high level of professionalism and integrity.


Work Arrangement & Travel 

  • This is a remote position.
  • Occasional travel of approximately 10-15% is required.
  • Travel may include visits to manufacturing facilities, corporate offices, and acquisition sites to support security projects, assessments, and integration activities.


About Ingersoll Rand

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE: IR) is a global provider of mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions, serving customers through more than 40 trusted brands worldwide. Driven by an ownership mindset and entrepreneurial culture, we are dedicated to delivering innovative solutions that improve productivity, efficiency, and sustainability while creating lasting value for our customers, employees, and communities.

Ingersoll Rand is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

As our Enterprise Risk Analyst, Corp Insurance & Worker's Comp Claims you’ll partner closely with the Enterprise Insurance Manager to support Ingersoll Rand’s global risk management, workers; comp and insurance programs. This hands-on, highly collaborative role involves working across internal teams, insurance brokers, and third-party administrators to manage insurance processes, claims activity, and compliance requirements. You will play a key role in the annual insurance renewal process, coordinating exposure data and supporting broker submissions and policy updates.

Your attention to detail will be critical as you manage Certificates of Insurance requests, reviewing contract requirements and endorsements to ensure accuracy. This position also supports monopolistic state workers’ compensation renewals and quarterly filings, assists with excise tax reporting, and helps monitor workers’ compensation and motor vehicle claims through third-party administrator systems—keeping the business protected and compliant.

This role is ideal for an early–mid career professional with a background in corporate risk, insurance, claims, or workers’ compensation (including legal or paralegal experience) who enjoys detail-oriented work, cross-functional coordination, and making a meaningful impact on the business.

Job Title: Plant Controller                    
Location: Junction City, OR
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability.
