Job Overview:
Help shape the finances behind a growing manufacturing operation. Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Plant Controller for its Junction City, Oregon site. As a trusted partner to plant leadership and the production team, you’ll turn financial insight and firsthand operational knowledge into greater cost efficiency, revenue growth, stronger margins, and improved net working capital. With demand from the data center market driving plans for increased production and workforce growth, Junction City is entering an exciting new chapter. You’ll help set its financial direction, give leaders clearer visibility into performance, and build the financial discipline needed to scale.

Work alongside production leaders on the plant floor to connect daily decisions with financial results. You’ll investigate production and purchase price variances, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns while bringing clarity to cost rollups, inventory valuation, reserves, and the metrics that matter most to the plant. Bring your accounting and finance expertise, curiosity, and business judgment to a role where the numbers lead to action. You’ll identify trends, solve root causes, strengthen analytics, and manage plant accounting while helping leaders improve performance and plan for growth.

Ready for your next step? You’ll lead a small site-based team, with a planned transition and direct knowledge transfer to help you take ownership of daily and weekly responsibilities within approximately three to six months. Prior Plant Controller experience is not required. An Assistant Controller, Senior Cost Accountant, Cost Accounting Manager, or similar professional with hands-on manufacturing experience and leadership potential could thrive here. If you can point to the KPIs you’ve improved and the measurable impact of your work, this is your chance to influence a growing plant’s performance and build your future with Ingersoll Rand.

Responsibilities:
  • Management Reporting: Deliver month-end analysis that explains financial results, trends, risks, opportunities, and their implications. Prepare the monthly operating review and report on weekly shipping trends, order rates, backlog, and net working capital metrics, including inventory performance.
  • Controls and Compliance: Maintain a strong control environment through adherence to SOX requirements and proactive partnership with internal and external auditors. Identify and resolve control gaps, and build a culture of compliance across the team. Key processes include revenue cutoff, warranty and obsolescence reserves, other valuation reserves, and account reconciliations.
  • ERP Process Improvement: Improve Epicor configurations and automation by strengthening internal processes and establishing standard work.
  • Forecasting and Budgeting: Partner with finance and business stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate forecasts and assess P&L and balance sheet risks and opportunities. Forecast bookings, revenue growth, production variances, overhead spending, and capital investments.
  • CSS and Corporate Partnership: Respond promptly to requests from shared financial services, corporate FP&A, and CSS leadership to support business performance.
  • Operational Business Partnership: Partner with plant and cross-functional leaders to provide analysis and decision support that advances annual operating plan targets. Participate in and lead IRX (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) processes that support tactical and strategic objectives.
  • Team Leadership and Development: Align the team around corporate objectives, develop talent, and build the coverage needed for business continuity. Coach and mentor direct and indirect reports through succession planning, development plans, and the removal of barriers to engagement and progress.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related business concentration. 
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, controllership, or cost-accounting 
  • 3+ years experience with Excel using complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and / or financial modeling.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated ability analyzing financial performance, identifying root causes, and translating findings into actionable recommendations. 
  • 2+ years experience with ERP systems such as Epicor or something similar 

Core Competencies
  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting: Working knowledge of manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costs and cost rollups, inventory reserves and valuation, production variances, purchase price variance, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns.
  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to interpret complex financial data, derive actionable insights, and communicate key findings clearly and concisely to team members at all levels.
  • Problem-Solving and Continuous Improvement: Proactively identifies issues, evaluates root causes, and implements effective solutions with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Manufacturing Accounting Acumen: Strong numerical and analytical skills, with a careful, structured approach to applying accounting principles within a manufacturing environment.
  • Collaboration and Influence: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to support cross-functional initiatives, build productive working relationships, and influence stakeholders across the organization.
  • Leadership: Ability to drive performance through others, support colleagues in pursuit of shared team goals, and maintain accountability for deliverables.
  • Communication and Coaching: Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain financial concepts clearly and influence and coach teams toward financial and operational objectives.
  • Time and Priority Management: Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and manage multiple projects efficiently while meeting established deadlines and deliverables.

Preferences:
  • MBA or professional certification such as CMA, CFA, or CPA.
  • Experience in SOX compliance requirements, financial or operational audits, and audit engagements.
  • Demonstrated project-management experience
  • Experience using Epicor 

Travel and Work Arrangements: 
  • This position is onsite
  • Anticipated travel approximately 10%

Job Title:  Product Support Engineer II – Technical Support and Enablement

Position Location: Hampton, NJ

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Position Summary
Business: Power Tools and Lifting

The Product Support Engineer II helps customers, channel partners, service technicians, sales teams, and internal stakeholders successfully select, apply, install, operate, troubleshoot, maintain, and repair Power Tools and Lifting products. The role owns complex technical inquiries from initial diagnosis through documented resolution, minimizes customer downtime, and converts field experience into reusable knowledge and training assets that improve self-service, launch readiness, and the capability of others.

This is not solely a case-resolution role, and it is not an instructional-design position. It is a technical support and enablement role. The engineer is expected to solve the immediate problem, capture what was learned, and help turn that learning into clear articles, service guidance, job aids, demonstrations, and training content in partnership with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, Warranty, Sales, Marketing, and training resources.

Core Responsibilities

Technical Support and Customer Problem Resolution

  • Own technical inquiries and escalations across phone, email, chat, remote-assist, and case-management channels.

  • Diagnose mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, pneumatic, cordless, connected, controls, software, and communications issues using structured troubleshooting and available test tools.

  • Provide product-selection, application, installation, configuration, maintenance, repair, conversion, and competitive-crossover guidance.

  • Coordinate repair, replacement, return, warranty, field-service, or engineering escalation when needed, with clear ownership and proactive customer updates.

  • Reproduce problems, document evidence, isolate likely causes, and provide complete technical handoffs when an issue requires another team.

Knowledge Development and Self-Service Enablement

  • Create and maintain customer-facing and internal knowledge articles, FAQs, troubleshooting guides, service procedures, technical bulletins, quick-reference job aids, and reusable response templates.

  • Convert recurring cases and field observations into durable content that reduces repeat contacts and improves first-contact resolution.

  • Write in clear, plain language while preserving technical accuracy, safety requirements, revision control, and appropriate review and approval.

  • Help govern product knowledge in the Help Center and related repositories, including identifying obsolete, duplicate, missing, or hard-to-find content.

  • Use approved AI and digital tools to accelerate research, drafting, case summarization, and content maintenance while validating technical accuracy.

Training and Commercial Enablement

  • Provide technical authorship and subject-matter expertise for sales, customer-support, distributor, and service-technician training.

  • Develop technical outlines, demonstrations, lab exercises, knowledge checks, job aids, and source content that instructional-design or media partners can convert into polished learning experiences.

  • Deliver or co-deliver live, virtual, recorded, and hands-on training when product expertise is required.

  • Prepare products, tooling, test equipment, configurations, and realistic troubleshooting scenarios for training and demonstrations.

  • Capture learner questions and feedback, then update supporting knowledge and training content.

Launch Readiness and Continuous Improvement

  • Participate early in new-product and product-change activities to evaluate serviceability, support readiness, diagnostic needs, parts and warranty implications, and required knowledge or training.

  • Validate manuals, service information, troubleshooting guidance, release notes, and support content before or immediately following launch.

  • Identify trends across cases, warranty activity, training feedback, and field observations; communicate actionable insights to Product Management, Engineering, Quality, and Warranty.

  • Initiate or support CAPA and other formal quality escalations when issues require cross-functional investigation.

  • Contribute to support analytics, backlog reduction, process improvement, and automation that make the support system more scalable.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, mechatronics, automation, industrial technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant technical experience.

  • 1+ years of experience in product support, field service, applications engineering, manufacturing engineering, technical training, controls, automation, or a related customer-facing technical role. Would consider new graduate with strong Engineering foundation with applicable internships, co-ops or capstone projects.


Core Competencies

  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex mechanical and electromechanical systems and to learn software-connected or networked products.

  • Ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly in writing, conversation, demonstrations, and structured learning materials.

  • Experience documenting technical problems, resolutions, procedures, or customer guidance in a case, knowledge, quality, or document-management system.

  • Ability to manage multiple issues and projects, set expectations, follow through on commitments, and communicate risks early.

  • Comfort working hands-on with products, tools, test equipment, returned material, and training equipment.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and willingness to learn support, knowledge, learning, warranty, quality, and analytics platforms used by the business.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with industrial power tools, precision fastening, pneumatic systems, lifting equipment, PLCs, industrial networks, manufacturing execution systems, or connected products.

  • 3+ years' experience in product support, field service or Applications Engineering in a related customer-facing technical role.

  • Experience creating knowledge-based content, technical service bulletins, training materials, lab exercises, or short instructional videos.

  • Experience supporting product launches, serviceability reviews, warranty analysis, root-cause investigations, CAPA, or ISO 9001 quality processes.

  • Basic data-analysis and visualization capability using Excel, Power BI, or similar tools.

  • Experience with Zendesk or comparable support and knowledge platforms, LMS platforms, and remote-support tools.

  • Bilingual capability in Spanish, French, Portuguese, or another language relevant to global customers and partners.

Travel Requirements

Up to 15%, primarily for customer or distributor support, application assessment, launch support, and training. Onsite based with some hybrid flexibility, regular on-site work for products, labs, content capture, and training

The pay range for this role is Min - 65,000 - Max - 85,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly motivated Cooling System Design Engineer to support the design, development, and delivery of cooling infrastructure for hyperscale, enterprise, and colocation data center projects. This role is responsible for designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable thermal management solutions that support mission-critical environments.

The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams, equipment vendors, construction partners, and project stakeholders to develop cooling system designs that meet performance, energy efficiency, scalability, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Responsibilities:

Cooling System Design

  • Develop conceptual, preliminary, and detailed designs for data center cooling systems.
  • Design and optimize chilled water, direct expansion (DX), liquid cooling, air-side and water-side economization systems.
  • Perform cooling load calculations and thermal analyses for white space, support spaces, and critical infrastructure areas.
  • Develop HVAC system layouts, piping schematics, flow diagrams, and equipment specifications.
  • Evaluate emerging cooling technologies, including direct-to-chip and immersion cooling solutions.
Engineering & Technical Analysis

  • Conduct system sizing calculations for chillers, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, pumps, heat exchangers, and associated equipment.
  • Perform computational modeling and simulations to validate cooling performance and energy efficiency.
  • Support CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) analyses for airflow management and thermal optimization.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, and industry best practices.
Project Delivery

  • Support project planning, design reviews, and technical coordination throughout all project phases.
  • Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, structural, controls, and commissioning teams.
  • Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Provide engineering support during procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Resolve design and field issues while maintaining schedule and budget commitments.
Sustainability & Energy Efficiency

  • Design solutions that achieve high levels of energy efficiency and operational resiliency.
  • Support PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) optimization initiatives.
  • Evaluate energy consumption and lifecycle cost impacts of cooling system alternatives.
  • Contribute to corporate sustainability and carbon reduction goals.
Documentation & Standards

  • Prepare engineering reports, calculations, technical specifications, and design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain design standards and best practices for data center cooling infrastructure.
  • Ensure complete and accurate project documentation is maintained throughout the project lifecycle.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in HVAC, mission-critical facilities, or data center infrastructure design.
    • 1+ years of experience performing HVAC load calculations and system sizing  
    Core Competencies

    • Data Center Thermal Management
    • HVAC Design Engineering
    • Mission-Critical Infrastructure
    • Cooling System Optimization
    • Energy Efficiency & Sustainability

Job Overview:
Early in your career in corporate insurance risk and workers’ compensation claims and ready to step into a role with real visibility into enterprise risk and insurance programs? This is where it happens.

As our Enterprise Risk Analyst, Corp Insurance & Worker's Comp Claims you’ll partner closely with the Enterprise Insurance Manager to support Ingersoll Rand’s global risk management, workers; comp and insurance programs. This hands-on, highly collaborative role involves working across internal teams, insurance brokers, and third-party administrators to manage insurance processes, claims activity, and compliance requirements. You will play a key role in the annual insurance renewal process, coordinating exposure data and supporting broker submissions and policy updates.

Your attention to detail will be critical as you manage Certificates of Insurance requests, reviewing contract requirements and endorsements to ensure accuracy. This position also supports monopolistic state workers’ compensation renewals and quarterly filings, assists with excise tax reporting, and helps monitor workers’ compensation and motor vehicle claims through third-party administrator systems—keeping the business protected and compliant.

This role is ideal for an early–mid career professional with a background in corporate risk, insurance, claims, or workers’ compensation (including legal or paralegal experience) who enjoys detail-oriented work, cross-functional coordination, and making a meaningful impact on the business.

Responsibilities: 
  • Assist with data collection for the insurance renewal process, including exposure gathering (statement of values, payroll, revenues, headcount, miles driven), completion of applications, coordination of insurer/broker meetings, receipt and filing of binders and policies.
    Primary point of contact for requests from the field, vendors, commercial teams or landlords for new or updated certificates of insurance (based on contractual requirements).

  • Assist with the process to review insurance provisions in contracts, leases and other agreements and request documentation required from insurance brokers.

  • Administer and monitor for compliance insurance filings required for monopolistic state workers compensation programs, and excise tax reporting.

  • Assist in identifying, assessing, and controlling the company's risks by running reports to analyze loss and exposure information. 

  • Manage the accurate and timely payment of insurance premiums, assessments, and fees.

  • Assist in day-to-day claims management, including reporting, information gathering, and follow-up, and active communication with the third-party adjusters to secure positive outcome of claim investigations, settlements and closures.

  • Interface with internal departments (Finance, Safety, Legal, Human Resources, Compliance and IR Business Units) and insurance broker, carriers, third-party administrators, and state insurance commissions.

Requirements 
  • High School Diploma or GED with equivalent related work experience.

  • 2+ years of experience in state workers compensation claims, insurance claims management, and/or a related finance function.

  • 3+ years of experience building and maintaining effective cross-functional partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

  • 3+ years of demonstrated ability communicating effectively and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.

  • 3+ years of demonstrated experience managing work independently, taking initiative, and driving tasks to completion.

  • 3+ years proven experience working with Windows applications and Microsoft Office Suite.

Core Competencies 
  • Insurance & Risk Program Support:  Ability to support enterprise insurance and risk management programs, including renewals, exposure data coordination, policy documentation, and compliance filings.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership: Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal teams, insurance brokers, carriers, and third-party administrators to ensure risk management activities move forward smoothly.

  • Claims Coordination & Insurance Operations: Support day-to-day claims activity, including reporting, information gathering, tracking through third-party administrator systems, and communication with adjusters and partners to advance claims resolution.

  • Analytical & Data Interpretation: Ability to analyze exposure and loss data from multiple sources, identify trends, and provide clear, accurate interpretations to support risk and insurance decision-making.

  • Detail Orientation & Process Accuracy: Maintain high accuracy when managing certificates of insurance, policy documentation, compliance filings, and financial transactions such as premiums, taxes, and assessments.

Preferences 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or related field

  • Experience as a paralegal supporting workers’ compensation legal matters

  • Direct claims experience or experience serving within a major insurance brokerage

  • Ability to quickly learn new software and systems

Travel and Work Arrangements  
  • This role is USA Remotely based

  • Anticipated travel is less than 5 percent

  • Must be a US Citizen or a legal Permanent Resident

Pay Range: The base salary range for this role is $45,000 - $65,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

About Us

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly motivated Cooling System Design Engineer to support the design, development, and delivery of cooling infrastructure for hyperscale, enterprise, and colocation data center projects. This role is responsible for designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable thermal management solutions that support mission-critical environments.

The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams, equipment vendors, construction partners, and project stakeholders to develop cooling system designs that meet performance, energy efficiency, scalability, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Responsibilities:

Cooling System Design

  • Develop conceptual, preliminary, and detailed designs for data center cooling systems.
  • Design and optimize chilled water, direct expansion (DX), liquid cooling, air-side and water-side economization systems.
  • Perform cooling load calculations and thermal analyses for white space, support spaces, and critical infrastructure areas.
  • Develop HVAC system layouts, piping schematics, flow diagrams, and equipment specifications.
  • Evaluate emerging cooling technologies, including direct-to-chip and immersion cooling solutions.

Engineering & Technical Analysis

  • Conduct system sizing calculations for chillers, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, pumps, heat exchangers, and associated equipment.
  • Perform computational modeling and simulations to validate cooling performance and energy efficiency.
  • Support CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) analyses for airflow management and thermal optimization.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, and industry best practices.

Project Delivery

  • Support project planning, design reviews, and technical coordination throughout all project phases.
  • Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, structural, controls, and commissioning teams.
  • Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Provide engineering support during procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Resolve design and field issues while maintaining schedule and budget commitments.

Sustainability & Energy Efficiency

  • Design solutions that achieve high levels of energy efficiency and operational resiliency.
  • Support PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) optimization initiatives.
  • Evaluate energy consumption and lifecycle cost impacts of cooling system alternatives.
  • Contribute to corporate sustainability and carbon reduction goals.

Documentation & Standards

  • Prepare engineering reports, calculations, technical specifications, and design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain design standards and best practices for data center cooling infrastructure.
  • Ensure complete and accurate project documentation is maintained throughout the project lifecycle.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in HVAC, mission-critical facilities, or data center infrastructure design.
  • 1+ years of experience performing HVAC load calculations and system sizing  

Core Competencies

  • Data Center Thermal Management
  • HVAC Design Engineering
  • Mission-Critical Infrastructure
  • Cooling System Optimization
  • Energy Efficiency & Sustainability
  • CFD Analysis
  • Technical Documentation
  • Vendor & Stakeholder Management
  • Risk Assessment & Problem Solving
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience supporting hyperscale or large-scale data center projects.
  • Familiarity with ASHRAE Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments.
  • Experience with CFD modeling tools such as 6SigmaDCX, Future Facilities, or equivalent.
  • Knowledge of liquid cooling technologies for AI/HPC workloads.
  • Experience with Uptime Institute Tier standards and TIA-942 requirements.
  • LEED Accreditation or experience with sustainable design initiatives.
  • Project management experience in multi-disciplinary engineering environments.
  • Proficiency with engineering design software such as:
    • AutoCAD
    • Revit
    • BIM platforms
    • HVAC modeling tools
  • Strong knowledge of:
    • Air-cooled and water-cooled chillers
    • Chilled water systems
    • Cooling towers
    • CRAH and CRAC systems
    • Pumping systems
    • Heat exchangers
    • Building Management Systems (BMS)

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Fully site based

Location:  Junction City, OR
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Help shape the finances behind a growing manufacturing operation. Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Plant Controller for its Junction City, Oregon site. As a trusted partner to plant leadership and the production team, you’ll turn financial insight and firsthand operational knowledge into greater cost efficiency, revenue growth, stronger margins, and improved net working capital. With demand from the data center market driving plans for increased production and workforce growth, Junction City is entering an exciting new chapter. You’ll help set its financial direction, give leaders clearer visibility into performance, and build the financial discipline needed to scale.

Work alongside production leaders on the plant floor to connect daily decisions with financial results. You’ll investigate production and purchase price variances, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns while bringing clarity to cost rollups, inventory valuation, reserves, and the metrics that matter most to the plant. Bring your accounting and finance expertise, curiosity, and business judgment to a role where the numbers lead to action. You’ll identify trends, solve root causes, strengthen analytics, and manage plant accounting while helping leaders improve performance and plan for growth.

Ready for your next step? You’ll lead a small site-based team, with a planned transition and direct knowledge transfer to help you take ownership of daily and weekly responsibilities within approximately three to six months. Prior Plant Controller experience is not required. An Assistant Controller, Senior Cost Accountant, Cost Accounting Manager, or similar professional with hands-on manufacturing experience and leadership potential could thrive here. If you can point to the KPIs you’ve improved and the measurable impact of your work, this is your chance to influence a growing plant’s performance and build your future with Ingersoll Rand.

Responsibilities:
  • Management Reporting: Deliver month-end analysis that explains financial results, trends, risks, opportunities, and their implications. Prepare the monthly operating review and report on weekly shipping trends, order rates, backlog, and net working capital metrics, including inventory performance.
  • Controls and Compliance: Maintain a strong control environment through adherence to SOX requirements and proactive partnership with internal and external auditors. Identify and resolve control gaps, and build a culture of compliance across the team. Key processes include revenue cutoff, warranty and obsolescence reserves, other valuation reserves, and account reconciliations.
  • ERP Process Improvement: Improve Epicor configurations and automation by strengthening internal processes and establishing standard work.
  • Forecasting and Budgeting: Partner with finance and business stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate forecasts and assess P&L and balance sheet risks and opportunities. Forecast bookings, revenue growth, production variances, overhead spending, and capital investments.
  • CSS and Corporate Partnership: Respond promptly to requests from shared financial services, corporate FP&A, and CSS leadership to support business performance.
  • Operational Business Partnership: Partner with plant and cross-functional leaders to provide analysis and decision support that advances annual operating plan targets. Participate in and lead IRX (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) processes that support tactical and strategic objectives.
  • Team Leadership and Development: Align the team around corporate objectives, develop talent, and build the coverage needed for business continuity. Coach and mentor direct and indirect reports through succession planning, development plans, and the removal of barriers to engagement and progress.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related business concentration. 
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, controllership, or cost-accounting 
  • 3+ years experience with Excel using complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and / or financial modeling.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated ability analyzing financial performance, identifying root causes, and translating findings into actionable recommendations. 
  • 2+ years experience with ERP systems such as Epicor or something similar 

Core Competencies
  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting: Working knowledge of manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costs and cost rollups, inventory reserves and valuation, production variances, purchase price variance, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns.
  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to interpret complex financial data, derive actionable insights, and communicate key findings clearly and concisely to team members at all levels.
  • Problem-Solving and Continuous Improvement: Proactively identifies issues, evaluates root causes, and implements effective solutions with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Manufacturing Accounting Acumen: Strong numerical and analytical skills, with a careful, structured approach to applying accounting principles within a manufacturing environment.
  • Collaboration and Influence: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to support cross-functional initiatives, build productive working relationships, and influence stakeholders across the organization.
  • Leadership: Ability to drive performance through others, support colleagues in pursuit of shared team goals, and maintain accountability for deliverables.
  • Communication and Coaching: Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain financial concepts clearly and influence and coach teams toward financial and operational objectives.
  • Time and Priority Management: Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and manage multiple projects efficiently while meeting established deadlines and deliverables.

Preferences:
  • MBA or professional certification such as CMA, CFA, or CPA.
  • Experience in SOX compliance requirements, financial or operational audits, and audit engagements.
  • Demonstrated project-management experience
  • Experience using Epicor 

Travel and Work Arrangements: 
  • This position is onsite
  • Anticipated travel approximately 10%

Job Overview
The Design for Manufacturing Engineer supports the assembly, integration, testing, and pre-ship performance evaluation of operational EVA and IVA spacesuit systems used in safety- and mission-critical applications. This role operates under moderate supervision within established engineering processes and procedures while providing meaningful opportunities for independent technical judgment, problem solving, and continuous improvement. The position provides hands-on exposure to the full product lifecycle in aerospace engineering, including design, fabrication, manufacturing, assembly, integration, verification, testing, and sustainment activities. Working closely with design engineering, manufacturing, quality, test, supply chain, and program teams, this role is well suited for early-career engineers seeking technical breadth, system-level understanding, and long-term growth within aerospace engineering and manufacturing operations.

Responsibilities
· Provide engineering support for EVA/IVA spacesuit manufacturing operations, including Sewing, Heat Seal, Chemical Processing, Bonding, Cementing, Electronics, and Hardgoods production, to maintain workflow and achieve On-Time-In-Full (OTIF) delivery objectives.
· Collect, analyze, and document environmental, mechanical, electrical, and functional test data to support product verification, validation, qualification, and acceptance activities.
· Evaluate and disposition nonconforming hardware in compliance with engineering requirements, quality standards, configuration management processes, NASA requirements, and customer specifications.
· Drive improvements in manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and production throughput through process optimization, tooling enhancements, equipment upgrades, environmental controls, and work instruction updates.
· Collaborate with design engineering teams to incorporate Design for Manufacturability (DFM) principles into new product development, product requirements, and future spacesuit hardware designs.
· Lead failure investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) initiatives to improve product reliability, manufacturing performance, and operational effectiveness.
· Develop, review, approve, and maintain configuration-controlled engineering documentation, including work instructions, assembly and test procedures, engineering changes, nonconformance reports, and product records.
· Support refurbishment, maintenance, sustainment, qualification, and production implementation activities for existing and new EVA spacesuit, glove, and Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) hardware.
· Lead material replacement, obsolescence mitigation, shelf-life extension, and risk reduction initiatives by assessing manufacturing impacts and implementing engineering controls to address quality, safety, and production concerns.
· Support capital equipment, tooling, and automation investments while leading continuous improvement initiatives focused on manufacturing processes, production workflows, performance metrics, and long-term operational capability.

Requirements
· Must be able to access shared databases supporting U.S. Government programs. Due to U.S. export control regulations, applicants must qualify as a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder), refugee, asylee, or otherwise be eligible to obtain any required U.S. Government authorizations.
· Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Textile Engineering, Materials Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
· 3+ years of engineering experience supporting design, manufacturing, integration, testing, production, or sustainment activities. Internships, co-op, laboratory, Formula SAE, robotics, or senior design experience may be considered.

Core Competencies
· Understanding of mechanical systems, manufacturing processes, product assemblies, engineering testing methods, and systems verification, validation, acceptance testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, and troubleshooting.
· Proficiency in standard engineering software and CAD-based 3D modeling; ability to read, interpret, and apply engineering drawings, schematics, specifications, bills of material, work instructions, test procedures, and configuration-controlled documentation. Familiarity with GD&T is preferred.
· Experience supporting fabrication, assembly, integration, laboratory testing, troubleshooting, or production operations with a proactive, solutions-oriented approach that balances technical, quality, and schedule requirements.
· Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, production, supplier, customer, and cross-functional teams while managing multiple priorities in a schedule-driven environment.
· Demonstrated ownership, accountability, and commitment to quality and safety, including compliance with laboratory, manufacturing, and test safety requirements.

Preferences
· Solid understanding of mechanical systems, manufacturing processes, product assemblies, engineering testing methods, and systems verification, validation, acceptance testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, and troubleshooting.
· Farmiliarity in standard engineering software and CAD-based 3D modeling; ability to read, interpret, and apply engineering drawings, schematics, specifications, bills of material, work instructions, test procedures, and configuration-controlled documentation. Familiarity with GD&T is preferred.
· Demonstrated ownership, accountability, and commitment to quality and safety, including compliance with laboratory, manufacturing, and test safety requirements.
· Professional experience supporting aerospace, defense, automotive, energy, robotics, or other high-reliability engineering products and systems.
· Experience supporting hardware through the design, fabrication, assembly, integration, verification, testing, production, and sustainment lifecycle.
· Experience with system-level testing, environmental testing, functional verification, instrumentation, data acquisition, and performance data analysis.
· Exposure to manufacturing processes such as machining, composites, sheet metal fabrication, additive manufacturing, welding, electronics assembly, or mechanical assembly.
· Experience applying root cause analysis, corrective action methodologies, failure investigations, anomaly resolution, nonconformance management, and hardware disposition processes.
· Understanding of requirements-driven engineering environments, product lifecycle management (PLM), configuration management, and the development or execution of manufacturing, assembly, and test documentation.
· Knowledge of quality management systems, inspection techniques, production controls, and the use of engineering software, data analysis tools, or visualization applications to support troubleshooting and process improvement.
· Demonstrated ability to communicate technical findings and recommendations effectively to diverse audiences, with evidence of technical initiative, sound engineering judgment, and experience in NASA, aerospace, or government contractor environments preferred.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements
· This position will be based at our office in Frederica, DE, with less than 10% travel
· Willingness to travel to local worksites, suppliers, customer locations, and test facilities as required.

Welch Vacuum, a subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand since 1996, is a global leader with over a century of history in high-performance vacuum technologies. We specialize in vacuum pumps, systems, and components for laboratories, life sciences, and industrial manufacturing. Operating within Ingersoll Rand's medical and laboratory division, we combine the engineering strengths of US-based Welch Vacuum Technology and Germany's Ilmvac GmbH.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a dynamic Area Sales Manager to lead our Sales Engineering function across the US West Coast, Mexico, and potentially South America. Requiring up to 75% travel, this role drives the promotion and sale of diverse vacuum technologies and OEM components. You will champion solution-based selling to distributors, manufacturers, system integrators, and end-users across vital sectors—including Life Sciences, Medical, Chemical, and General Manufacturing.

Responsibilities

  • Drive Business Growth: Expand market share using modern prospecting methods, structured toll-gate sales processes, and solution-selling best practices.
  • Manage & Acquire Accounts: Nurture the existing distributor base and partner with dealer reps while aggressively pursuing new distribution, reseller, and OEM/system integrator opportunities.
  • Provide Technical Support: Serve as a trusted technical advisor to OEMs, large end-users, and academic research institutions to guide the pump specification and selection process directly in customer labs.
  • Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Partner closely with Field Sales Support, Application Engineering, Product Management, Operations, Quality, Finance, and Demand Generation to secure new business and drive profitable growth.
  • Lead Commercial Negotiations: Manage major pricing negotiations, define technical specifications, and ensure alignment across complex commercial agreements.
  • Build Multi-Level Relationships: Interface confidently with diverse customer departments on a technical and commercial level, including Engineering, Purchasing, Quality, and decision makers and leadership.
  • Maintain Data Integrity: Manage accurate sales forecasts and maintain up-to-date internal CRM reporting to support strategic growth objectives.
  • Apply Subject Matter Expertise: Leverage technical sales experience and vacuum pump technology knowledge to develop business and promote the Welch brand to new customers.
  • Execute Strategic Agility: Perform other responsibilities as assigned or required to support evolving business needs.
Requirements: 

  • High School Degree or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of customer-facing vacuum sales experience, with a proven track record of growth.
Core Competencies

  • Strategic Selling: Ability to execute sophisticated sales strategies and drive new business development.
  • Problem Solving: Creative problem-solver skilled at resolving technical challenges and open issues.
  • Collaboration: Strong relationship builder with both external clients and internal support teams.
  • Organization: Exceptional multi-tasking abilities with sharp attention to detail, organization, and analysis.
  • Technology: Proficient in Microsoft Office and CRM systems (Salesforce preferred).
  • Languages: Professional fluency in English is required; Spanish proficiency is a strong plus.

Preferences:  
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, Life Sciences, or a related technical field.
  • Industry Expertise: Experience in the Laboratory, Analytical, and Life Sciences markets.
  • Technical Knowledge: Proven sales or application experience with vacuum pump technologies (or closely related industrial systems).
  • Account Management: Demonstrated success in prospecting, securing, and managing enterprise-level accounts.
  • Drive: High-energy self-starter with a goal-oriented mindset.

  • Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the West region.

  • Lead regular project reviews and deliver concise progress reports, executive presentations, technical documentation, and recovery plans when needed.
  • Advise BPS leadership and impacted departments on product or design changes that could affect cost, timing, profitability, and customer commitments.
  • Ensure customer feedback and evolving requirements are evaluated, communicated, and appropriately incorporated into project plans and design decisions.
  • Promote a high-performance, safety-focused culture that maintains compliance with regulatory requirements, quality standards, internal policies, and financial controls.

Job Title: Area Sales Manager 
Location: Remote – Territory - CA, AZ, OR, WA, UT, NV, CO, ID, MT 

About Us:
Welch Vacuum, a subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand since 1996, is a global leader with over a century of history in high-performance vacuum technologies. We specialize in vacuum pumps, systems, and components for laboratories, life sciences, and industrial manufacturing. Operating within Ingersoll Rand's medical and laboratory division, we combine the engineering strengths of US-based Welch Vacuum Technology and Germany's Ilmvac GmbH.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a dynamic Area Sales Manager to lead our Sales Engineering function across the US West Coast, Mexico, and potentially South America. Requiring up to 75% travel, this role drives the promotion and sale of diverse vacuum technologies and OEM components. You will champion solution-based selling to distributors, manufacturers, system integrators, and end-users across vital sectors—including Life Sciences, Medical, Chemical, and General Manufacturing.

Responsibilities

  • Drive Business Growth: Expand market share using modern prospecting methods, structured toll-gate sales processes, and solution-selling best practices.
  • Manage & Acquire Accounts: Nurture the existing distributor base and partner with dealer reps while aggressively pursuing new distribution, reseller, and OEM/system integrator opportunities.
  • Provide Technical Support: Serve as a trusted technical advisor to OEMs, large end-users, and academic research institutions to guide the pump specification and selection process directly in customer labs.
  • Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Partner closely with Field Sales Support, Application Engineering, Product Management, Operations, Quality, Finance, and Demand Generation to secure new business and drive profitable growth.
  • Lead Commercial Negotiations: Manage major pricing negotiations, define technical specifications, and ensure alignment across complex commercial agreements.
  • Build Multi-Level Relationships: Interface confidently with diverse customer departments on a technical and commercial level, including Engineering, Purchasing, Quality, and decision makers and leadership.
  • Maintain Data Integrity: Manage accurate sales forecasts and maintain up-to-date internal CRM reporting to support strategic growth objectives.
  • Apply Subject Matter Expertise: Leverage technical sales experience and vacuum pump technology knowledge to develop business and promote the Welch brand to new customers.
  • Execute Strategic Agility: Perform other responsibilities as assigned or required to support evolving business needs.
Requirements: 

  • High School Degree or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of customer-facing vacuum sales experience, with a proven track record of growth.
Core Competencies

  • Strategic Selling: Ability to execute sophisticated sales strategies and drive new business development.
  • Problem Solving: Creative problem-solver skilled at resolving technical challenges and open issues.
  • Collaboration: Strong relationship builder with both external clients and internal support teams.
  • Organization: Exceptional multi-tasking abilities with sharp attention to detail, organization, and analysis.
  • Technology: Proficient in Microsoft Office and CRM systems (Salesforce preferred).
  • Languages: Professional fluency in English is required; Spanish proficiency is a strong plus.

Preferences:  
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, Life Sciences, or a related technical field.
  • Industry Expertise: Experience in the Laboratory, Analytical, and Life Sciences markets.
  • Technical Knowledge: Proven sales or application experience with vacuum pump technologies (or closely related industrial systems).
  • Account Management: Demonstrated success in prospecting, securing, and managing enterprise-level accounts.
  • Drive: High-energy self-starter with a goal-oriented mindset.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the West region.
Pay Range:

The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $125,000-$145,000.  The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Materials Engineer
Location: Frederica, DE

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 

This position sits within the engineering organization supporting Materials and Processes (M&P) requirements for Aerospace & Defense Solutions including NASA space flight hardware. The Materials Engineer will support the research, development, qualification, and sustainment of materials used in the assembly and component design of space systems products. Responsibilities include supporting M&P testing, verification, and documentation efforts, and assisting with investigations of material non conformances and materials related on orbit issues.

The role operates under moderate supervision, with clearly defined guidelines and procedures, while offering meaningful latitude for independent technical judgment and problem solving. This position provides hands on exposure to real world materials behavior in a regulated, mission critical environment and regular collaboration with manufacturing, quality, and design teams—making it well suited for early career engineers seeking technical depth, accountability, and long-term growth in materials and process engineering.

Responsibilities:

  • Employ established science and engineering principles in the research, design and development of materials and processes for aerospace, defense, and space flight hardware
  • Maintain a detailed knowledge and understanding of softgood materials, their testing, and manufacturing processes, specifically for space flight applications
  • Generate and maintain engineering and material control documents to ensure compliance with space flight hardware requirements including material drawings, Material Identification and Usage Lists, flight or material waivers (including Material Usage Agreements and Material Review Board waivers), and other program documentation related to material/product definition and control
  • Identify, evaluate, and define material requirements and generate specifications
  • Perform materials testing/analysis and generate testing/analysis documentation
  • Effectively present materials engineering information to team members as well as cross-functional partners and external clients/ customers as necessary

Requirements:

  • Must be able to access shared databases with U.S. Government programs (U.S. Citizen or U.S. Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor of Science degree in Materials Engineering, Textile Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Polymer Science, Chemical Engineering or a closely related field
  • 3+ years relevant experience in materials engineering, manufacturing, laboratory, or process support roles (co-op, internship, or senior design experience considered)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with or specialization in metallurgical engineering, including fabrication methods, failure and degradation modes, and shelf/operational life expectancy
  • Familiarity with technical documentation such as material specifications, work instructions, test methods, or M&P requirements (NASA or aerospace exposure a plus, but not required)
  • Proficiency with standard engineering tools, including word processing and spreadsheet software; introductory CAD skills and basic 3D modeling experience desirable
  • Academic focus, project work, or early professional experience related to materials behavior in controlled or safety critical applications, such as aerospace, defense, medical devices, energy systems, or advanced manufacturing
  • Familiarity with materials qualification concepts, including test planning, verification, traceability, and documentation in accordance with defined requirements (formal M&P or equivalent quality systems experience preferred)
  • Exposure to failure analysis or nonconformance investigations, including contributing to root cause analysis, corrective actions, or disposition of material issues
  • Understanding of the importance of material compatibility, outgassing, contamination control, and long-term performance in high reliability hardware
  • Experience working within structured engineering processes, including configuration control, change management, or requirements driven development
  • Ability to clearly document and communicate technical findings in test reports, analyses, or engineering justifications
  • Demonstrated technical curiosity and judgment appropriate for work supporting mission critical hardware, with the ability to recognize when to escalate risk, request testing, or seek peer review

 Core Competencies:

  • Ability to communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, with engineers, technicians, and cross functional stakeholders
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across functions, including manufacturing, quality, and engineering teams
  • Willingness and ability to follow laboratory and production safety practices, including wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Ability to read, understand, and execute work instructions, drawings, and technical documentation written in English
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and tight deadlines
  • Willingness to travel to local worksites as needed

Work Environment:
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals. The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to electricity. The employee is exposed to minor burns and/or cuts. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Physical Demands: Communicate with team members on a regular basis in writing and speech; use of hands to handle, control, or feel objects, tools, or controls; wear common protective or safety equipment; standing for long periods of time. The employee is frequently stooping, crawling, climbing, and performing repetitive motion with arms. The employee occasionally sits. The employee frequently lifts up to 50 Lbs. and occasionally will lift up to 75 lbs.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 
Fully site based in Frederica, DE. Minimal travel expected.

• Read and follow mechanical drawings, piping layouts, and Bills of Material (BOMs).

Job title: Facility Maintenance Technician | REQ 20538

Location: G&D Chillers - Junction City, OR 

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

The Facility Maintenance Technician maintains, troubleshoots, repairs, and improves building facilities, utilities, and supporting equipment to ensure safe, efficient, and uninterrupted operations in a chiller manufacturing and service environment. This role supports facility infrastructure, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, compressed air, and other plant utility systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance; inspect and repair building infrastructure, including walls, floors, roofs, doors, windows, and general facility assets.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot electrical, plumbing, lighting, compressed air, and water systems; support HVAC, ventilation, and industrial cooling systems.
  • Monitor utilities and maintain generators, air compressors, pumps, cooling towers, and related equipment; assist with equipment installation, relocation, and commissioning.
  • Respond promptly to breakdowns and emergency repair requests; coordinate inspections and maintenance schedules to reduce downtime.
  • Follow OSHA, environmental, company safety, and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) requirements; conduct safety inspections and support emergency preparedness programs.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, work orders, and inspection reports.
  • Coordinate contractors and service providers, monitor work quality and compliance, and assist with quotations and maintenance service contracts.
  • Monitor energy consumption and recommend energy-saving improvements, equipment upgrades, and reliability enhancements; support facility projects, cost reduction, Lean Manufacturing, and continuous improvement.

Requirements:

  • High school diploma, technical diploma, associate degree, or equivalent vocational training in facility maintenance, electrical technology, mechanical technology, HVAC/refrigeration, or industrial maintenance.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of facility maintenance experience in a manufacturing, industrial, HVAC, refrigeration, or chiller-related environment, including building systems, utilities, and industrial equipment.
  • Knowledge of electrical systems and understanding of HVAC, refrigeration, and chilled water systems.
  • Ability to troubleshoot mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic equipment; experience with pumps, motors, compressors, cooling towers, and generators.
  • Familiarity with Building Management Systems (BMS) and computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS).
  • Ability to read technical drawings, schematics, and manuals; proficiency with hand and power tools.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, climb ladders, work in confined spaces, and lift up to 50 lbs (23 kg).

Core Competencies:

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills; ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Good communication and teamwork abilities; attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Strong safety mindset; dependable and self-motivated.

Preferences:

  • Experience supporting manufacturing facilities.
  • Knowledge of 120V, 208V, and 480V electrical systems.
  • Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 
  • Work indoors and outdoors in varying temperatures. Occasional after-hours, weekend, or emergency call-in support may be required. Regular shift and travel requirements: Pending information.

What We Offer 

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

job.description:
Senior Salesforce Support Analyst (Remote)

Join Ingersoll Rand and Shape the Future of Service Operations

At Ingersoll Rand, we are driven by an entrepreneurial spirit, a culture of ownership, and a commitment to innovation. As a global leader in mission-critical flow creation and industrial technologies, we empower our teams to solve complex challenges, drive operational excellence, and create exceptional customer experiences.

We are seeking a Senior Salesforce Support Analyst who is passionate about Salesforce technologies and eager to make a significant impact across a global organization. In this highly visible role, you will partner with business leaders, service teams, and technology stakeholders to optimize our Salesforce ecosystem, enhance service operations, and deliver solutions that improve customer success.

If you thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and want to help shape the future of digital service transformation, we'd love to hear from you.

Position Details

Location: Remote
Function: Information Technology
Reports To: Senior Manager, CRM Applications


What You'll Do

As the Senior Salesforce Support Analyst, you will serve as a key contributor to the stability, scalability, and continuous improvement of our Salesforce platform, with a focus on Service Cloud and Salesforce Field Service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary Level 2/3 support resource for Salesforce Service Cloud and Salesforce Field Service.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex application, configuration, data quality, and integration issues.
  • Support critical service processes including scheduling, dispatching, work order management, technician productivity, and mobile workforce operations.
  • Manage and optimize integrations between Salesforce and enterprise platforms including SAP, Oracle ERP, ServiceNow, and other business-critical systems.
  • Lead incident, problem, change, and request management activities through ServiceNow.
  • Partner closely with business stakeholders to gather requirements, document solutions, and drive operational improvements.
  • Support testing, release management, user acceptance testing (UAT), system enhancements, and deployment activities.
  • Develop and maintain end-user documentation, training materials, and knowledge articles.
  • Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable solutions that enhance customer and employee experiences.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Systems, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience supporting Salesforce within a complex enterprise environment.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with Salesforce Service Cloud and/or Salesforce Field Service.
  • Experience supporting integrations between Salesforce and SAP and/or Oracle ERP platforms.
  • Experience working with ServiceNow and ITIL-based support methodologies.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce Administrator Certification.
  • Salesforce Field Service Consultant Certification.
  • Experience with SAP ECC, SAP S/4HANA, Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), or Oracle Fusion.
  • Experience within manufacturing, industrial, or field-service-driven organizations.
  • Familiarity with the enosix integration platform.
  • Experience supporting large-scale Salesforce environments with global user communities.

Technical Environment

Experience with the following technologies is highly valued:

  • Salesforce Service Cloud
  • Salesforce Field Service
  • Salesforce Flow Builder
  • Salesforce Security & Access Model
  • Reporting & Dashboards
  • SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA
  • Oracle EBS / Oracle Fusion
  • ServiceNow
  • APIs and Web Services
  • Middleware & Integration Platforms
  • Data Management & Data Quality
  • Release & Change Management

Why Join Ingersoll Rand?

  • Work remotely with a globally recognized industrial technology leader.
  • Drive meaningful digital transformation initiatives that directly impact customer success.
  • Collaborate with talented teams across IT, Service Operations, and Business Functions.
  • Influence the future direction of Salesforce Service Cloud and Field Service capabilities.
  • Grow your career through continuous learning, leadership exposure, and development opportunities.
  • Join a company that values innovation, ownership, collaboration, and integrity.


About Ingersoll Rand

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE: IR) is committed to helping make life better for our employees, customers, and communities. Through more than 40 trusted brands, we provide mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions that perform in some of the world's most demanding environments. Our global team is united by a passion for innovation, customer success, and continuous improvement.

This position will play a critical role in developing quality processes, inspection standards, documentation systems, corrective action processes, and a culture of continuous improvement throughout the manufacturing operation.
 
Responsibilities:

  • Establish inspection standards, quality control plans, and acceptance criteria for chiller and component production.
  • Lead incoming material inspection activities and ensure supplier compliance with engineering specifications and quality requirements.
  • Conduct production audits and in-process inspections to verify adherence to manufacturing procedures, drawings, and specifications.

  • Support ISO 9001 compliance, quality audits, employee training, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure customer and regulatory requirements are me

  • Experience with quality management systems and ISO 9001 requirements.

  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and bills of materials.
  • Knowledge of mechanical, electrical, piping, refrigeration, or assembly manufacturing processes.
  • Ability to analyze quality issues and perform root cause investigations.
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Service teams.
  • Strong documentation, record-keeping, and communication skills
 
Preferences:
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, or a related field.
  • Experience in HVAC, chiller, refrigeration, industrial equipment, or mechanical/electrical assembly manufacturing.
  • Experience establishing, implementing, or improving quality systems.
  • Prior supervisory, lead, or team leadership experience.
  • Experience developing inspection standards, quality control plans, and quality documentation.
  • Experience managing supplier quality and incoming material inspections.
  • Experience leading corrective and preventive action (CAPA) processes and non-conformance investigations.
  • Experience supporting internal and external quality audits.
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully site based

•Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.

Job title:Oil Free Rotary Product Manager
Location: Charlotte/Davidson, NC (preferred). Nashville, TN
Buffalo, NY

Job Overview: 
Ingersoll Rand’s North America business unit within Industrial Technologies & Services (ITS) is seeking an Oil Free Rotary Product Manager. Reporting to the Product Management Leader for Oil Free Technologies, this role is responsible for driving profitable growth across the Ingersoll Rand oil-free rotary compressor portfolio (3–450 HP).

This position leads product strategy, roadmap development, new product introductions, and lifecycle management for one of the industry’s largest oil-free compressor portfolios. Acting as a business leader for the portfolio, the Product Manager will shape the future of oil-free rotary technologies and support a key growth segment for the company.

Responsibilities: 

  • Own product strategy, roadmaps, business cases, and value propositions for oil-free rotary compressors and related services.
  • Analyze market, technology, and industry trends to identify growth opportunities.
  • Develop and present business cases supporting new products and product enhancements.
  • Conduct customer portfolio reviews to drive sales growth and mitigate business risks.
  • Lead Voice of Customer (VOC) initiatives through customer engagement, interviews, and advisory panels.
  • Advocate for customer satisfaction through continuous improvements in quality and operational performance.
  • Lead cross-functional teams to execute product development, commercialization, and product integration plans.
  • Manage product lifecycle strategies, including existing platforms and aftermarket parts offerings.
  • Develop sales forecasts to support manufacturing plans, inventory management, and product transitions.
  • Travel as needed to strengthen customer and channel relationships.

 
Requirements: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Technical, or Scientific discipline required; MBA preferred.
  • 5+ years of professional experience, preferably in industrial B2B markets.
  • Knowledge of life sciences, food & beverage, electronics, or utility-related industries is a plus.
  • 3+ years of experience working with customers and phase-gate product development processes.
  • Strong presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Proven business acumen, including financial analysis and business case development.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results on schedule.
  • Strong ability to influence without direct authority.


Core Competencies:

  • Strong business acumen with a passion for driving profitable growth.
  • Excellent communicator who builds effective relationships across teams and customers.
  • Experienced in product development, commercialization, and market introduction.

Job Overview:

We are seeking a skilled, safety-focused Industrial Refrigeration Test Technician to inspect, commission, troubleshoot, and functionally test industrial glycol and refrigeration chillers prior to shipment.

This position is responsible for verifying that equipment operates safely, performs according to engineering specifications, and meets company quality standards. The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, comfortable working with refrigeration, electrical, and control systems, and capable of diagnosing and resolving equipment issues in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Perform functional testing, startup, commissioning, and final quality verification of industrial refrigeration systems, chillers, and related equipment prior to shipment.
  • Review engineering documentation including wiring diagrams, piping schematics, bills of material, test procedures, and specifications to ensure equipment is configured and tested correctly.
  • Inspect, operate, and evaluate refrigeration, mechanical, electrical, and control systems while recording operating data and verifying performance against design requirements.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, refrigeration, controls, and system-performance issues; coordinate corrective actions with Production, Engineering, and Quality teams.
  • Perform leak testing, system evacuation, refrigerant charging, refrigerant recovery, and related activities in accordance with company procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Navigate and utilize PLCs, HMIs, controllers, variable frequency drives (VFDs), and other control interfaces to support testing, troubleshooting, and equipment verification.
  • Complete test reports, inspection records, refrigerant documentation, and other required quality records while maintaining accurate testing documentation.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives, maintain testing equipment and work areas, assist with training of team members, and perform other related duties as assigned.

 

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, industrial maintenance, HVAC, refrigeration, electrical, controls, or related technical environments.
  • Ability to read and interpret wiring diagrams, refrigeration schematics, piping drawings, bills of material, and technical documentation.
  • Experience using testing, diagnostic, or measurement equipment and documenting results in computer-based systems or electronic records.

Core Competencies: 
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and regularly bend, kneel, climb, reach, and work around large industrial equipment.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation and safely handle tools, testing equipment, hoses, gauges, and other job-related materials.
  • Follow all company safety policies, PPE requirements, lockout/tagout procedures, electrical safety practices, refrigerant handling requirements, and approved testing procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free work area and promptly report unsafe conditions, equipment concerns, spills, leaks, or near misses.

 

Preferences:

  • Experience testing, servicing, commissioning, or troubleshooting commercial or industrial refrigeration, HVAC, process cooling, or engineered equipment.
  • EPA Section 608 Certification, technical degree, apprenticeship, military technical training, or equivalent hands-on technical experience.
  • Experience working with PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, electrical controls, compressors, pumps, heat exchangers, valves, sensors, and related industrial equipment.
  • Experience performing refrigerant recovery, evacuation, charging, leak testing, brazing, or other refrigeration-related activities; OSHA, electrical safety, or Lockout/Tagout training is a plus.
 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This is a fully onsite position based in a manufacturing environment and requires a strong commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence. The individual must safely work around electrical equipment, refrigeration systems, pressurized components, moving machinery, and active production operations while complying with all company safety policies and required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements.
