job.title: Maintenance Parts & Materials Coordinator
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances. 

Job Title: Maintenance Parts & Materials Coordinator                    
Location:  Alsip, IL
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Bring order to the parts, systems, and processes that keep maintenance moving. Ingersoll Rand’s Alsip facility supports the IRP, MP Pump and Oberdorfer Pump businesses, trusted brands known worldwide for reliable, innovative and durable fluid-handling solutions.  

As the Maintenance Parts & Materials Coordinator, you will create the control, accuracy, and visibility needed to support 159 assets across Ingersoll Rand’s 100,000-square-foot Alsip facility. You will ensure technicians have the right parts, outside services, and reliable system information to complete critical preventive and corrective maintenance. Owning the process from request through completion, you will source vendors, obtain quotes, manage purchase orders, track deliveries, record received materials, maintain inventory accuracy, and coordinate activity across the CMMS, ERP, procurement, and payment processes. You will also become the site’s CMMS subject-matter expert, strengthening parts and asset data, inventory accuracy, and the connection between purchased materials and completed maintenance work. MaintainX experience is not required, but familiarity with a CMMS or comparable operational system—and the ability to learn technology quickly—is essential.

This is a non-supervisory systems-focused position requiring strong ownership, follow through and organization—not a hands-on mechanic, inventory-counting, or administrative support role. Working closely with Maintenance, Purchasing, Finance, Accounts Payable, Operations, Engineering, EHS, and external vendors, you will identify gaps, solve problems, and drive work to completion.Because the site’s maintenance materials and purchasing processes are continuing to evolve, you will have the opportunity to help build and improve them. 

The strongest candidate will bring experience in maintenance coordination, parts or inventory management, logistics, industrial materials, a tool crib or storeroom, automotive service operations, or a similar environment—along with urgency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. For someone eager to grow within industrial maintenance, this role offers broad exposure to plant operations, equipment, purchasing, inspections, and vendors, with opportunities to expand into regulatory support, deeper maintenance expertise, and future leadership.

Responsibilities:

CMMS Administration & Data Management  
  • Maintain accurate asset, equipment, preventive maintenance, work-order, labor, parts, and service records within the CMMS. 
  • Review newly submitted maintenance requests for completeness and route them to the appropriate supervisor or technician. 
  • Create and update work orders based on maintenance findings, approved requests, inspections, and scheduled preventive maintenance activities. 
  • Support the development and maintenance of equipment hierarchies, asset records, PM frequencies, task lists, and equipment documentation. 
  • Monitor open, overdue, incomplete, and waiting-for-parts work orders. 
  • Follow up with supervisors and technicians to obtain missing work-order information, labor hours, parts usage, failure codes, and completion details. 
  • Verify that completed work orders contain sufficient documentation before administrative closure. 
  • Maintain consistent naming conventions and data-entry standards within the CMMS. 
  • Assist with CMMS reports covering PM compliance, work-order backlog, equipment history, parts usage, recurring failures, and maintenance spending. 
  • Support the onboarding of new equipment into the CMMS, including asset information, manuals, parts lists, and initial PM requirements. 
  Parts Room & Inventory Control 
  • Maintain an organized, labeled, secure, and accurate maintenance parts room. 
  • Receive, identify, label, store, issue, and document maintenance repair parts, consumables, and critical spares. 
  • Maintain accurate inventory quantities, storage locations, part descriptions, manufacturer information, and equipment associations. 
  • Establish and maintain minimum and maximum stocking levels for frequently used and critical spare parts. 
  • Perform cycle counts and periodic physical inventories. 
  • Research and correct discrepancies between physical inventory and system quantities. 
  • Identify obsolete, duplicate, damaged, slow-moving, or unidentified inventory for review. 
  • Coordinate parts reservations and staging for planned PMs, repairs, shutdown work, and contractor activities. 
  • Notify Maintenance Supervisors when critical spares are below established stocking levels or unavailable. 
  • Maintain appropriate parts-room housekeeping, access controls, and storage practices. 
  • Coordinate the proper storage and documentation of lubricants, chemicals, batteries, and other maintenance materials with EHS requirements. 

Purchasing, Service POs & Orders 
  • Prepare maintenance purchase requisitions and supporting documentation for repair parts, supplies, tools, rentals, and outside services. 
  • Coordinate the creation, tracking, and administrative management of maintenance service purchase orders. 
  • Confirm that requests contain the correct vendor, scope, asset, department, quote, cost information, and approval documentation. 
  • Submit approved parts and service orders through established company purchasing processes. 
  • Track order acknowledgements, delivery dates, backorders, cancellations, and expedited requests. 
  • Communicate order and delivery status to Maintenance Supervisors and affected stakeholders. 
  • Match received products and completed services to the applicable purchase order and supporting documentation. 
  • Assist with resolving quantity, pricing, receipt, invoice, and purchase-order discrepancies. 
  • Maintain organized records of vendor quotes, purchase orders, service reports, packing slips, invoices, warranties, and approvals. 
  • Escalate urgent parts or service needs that could affect equipment uptime, safety, environmental compliance, or production. 
  • Support emergency purchasing documentation when immediate repairs require expedited vendor service or materials. 

Vendor & Service Coordination 
  • Maintain current maintenance vendor and service-provider contact information. 
  • Coordinate service-call documentation, site access information, schedules, purchase-order references, and required service reports. 
  • Confirm that contractor service documentation is received and associated with the appropriate asset and work order. 
  • Obtain repair reports, inspection results, recommendations, warranty information, and follow-up quotations from vendors. 
  • Track open vendor recommendations and communicate required follow-up actions to Maintenance Supervisors. 
  • Support contractor onboarding and required documentation in coordination with Maintenance and EHS. 
  • Maintain equipment warranty information and assist in identifying repairs or parts that may qualify for warranty coverage. 

Maintenance Planning Support 
  • Review upcoming PMs and identify required parts, materials, documentation, vendor support, and equipment access requirements. 
  • Assemble work-order packets, manuals, drawings, procedures, service history, and parts information for planned work. 
  • Stage or reserve parts for upcoming PMs and corrective repairs. 
  • Support development of weekly maintenance schedules under the direction of the Maintenance Supervisor. 
  • Identify work orders delayed because of parts, purchasing, vendor availability, approvals, or missing information. 
  • Maintain a visible list of maintenance work that is ready to schedule. 
  • Support cross-shift continuity by keeping work-order, parts, and service-status information current and accessible. 
  • Assist with maintenance shutdown preparation, contractor scheduling, and material readiness. 

Reporting & Continuous Improvement 
  • Prepare routine reports on inventory accuracy, stockouts, purchase-order status, parts usage, PM support, work-order backlog, and maintenance costs. 
  • Identify recurring purchases that should be converted into stocked items, blanket orders, or preferred-vendor arrangements. 
  • Identify frequently used or long-lead-time components that may require revised stocking levels. 
  • Help improve maintenance workflows, purchasing controls, storeroom organization, and CMMS data quality. 
  • Support root cause analysis by providing equipment history, prior work orders, parts usage, vendor reports, and repair-cost information. 
  • Participate in maintenance planning meetings and provide updates on parts, orders, vendor services, and work-order readiness. 
  • Support standard work and documented procedures for parts issuance, inventory counts, purchase requests, CMMS entries, and work-order closure. 

Safety, Environmental & Compliance Support 
  • Follow all applicable site safety, environmental, purchasing, financial, and document-retention requirements. 
  • Maintain the parts room and maintenance administrative areas in a safe and orderly condition. 
  • Coordinate with EHS regarding storage, labeling, documentation, and disposal requirements for maintenance chemicals and controlled materials. 
  • Report damaged shelving, unsafe storage, spills, blocked access, missing labels, and other hazards. 
  • Maintain required records for contractor services, inspections, repairs, and compliance-related maintenance activities. 
  • Ensure that safety-critical parts and services are clearly identified and appropriately prioritized. 
  Requirements
  • High School Diploma or GED. 
  • 2+ years of progressive experience supporting maintenance operations, such as maintenance data, service purchase orders, and inventory, with exposure to CMMS coordination, inventory control, purchasing, parts management, manufacturing support, or a related function.
  • 2+ years experience reading and understand equipment descriptions, part numbers, bills of material, manuals, quotations, and service reports. 
  • 2+ years experience working with a CMMS, inventory-management system, ERP system, or purchasing platform
  • 2+ years of professional experience using Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and other Microsoft Office applications to support operational workflows. 
  • 1+ years working knowledge of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, inventory transactions, and vendor documentation.
  • Ability to lift and handle maintenance parts within established site material-handling requirements. 

Core Competencies
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple open orders, work requests, and changing priorities. 
  • Demonstrates strong ownership, urgency, and consistent follow-through.
  • Collaborates effectively with technicians, supervisors, vendors, Purchasing, Finance, Engineering, Operations, and EHS.
  • Maintains accurate records and closes items only when supporting information is complete and properly documented.
  • Communicates delays, shortages, discrepancies, and potential risks promptly and proactively.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 
Locations: Phoenix, AZ

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
The Centrifugal Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems & Services division serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 
  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  
  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 
  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, preventative maintenance (PMs), diagnostics, air audits, and leak detection, can benefit their operations. 
  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components.
  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs.
  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 
  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 
Requirements

  • Minimum 2 years of Centrifugal compressor experience.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
Core Competentcies
  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; speciality tools will be provided.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • Ability to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation). 
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting. 
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment). 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. 
  • Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
Preferences:

  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided. 
Pay Range: Starting pay will range between $35.00 - $50.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position

Title: Processed Lead Assembler

Location: Bentleyville Facility in Charleroi, PA (Gardner Denver Nash - 200 Simko Blvd. Charleroi, PA 15022) 

Pay: $25 - $28 per hour Based on Experience

Shift: 1st Shift (5:00am - 1:30pm)

 

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

 

Job Overview:
Ingersoll Rand has an exciting opportunity for a Process Lead - Assembler/Disassembler at our Bentleyville, PA location. This position is responsible for owning the complete disassembly, inspection, repair, assembly, and testing processes for blowers and rotating equipment. The successful candidate will serve as a subject matter resource for mechanical troubleshooting, equipment evaluation, and continuous improvement efforts while ensuring the highest standards of safety, quality, and productivity.

The Assembler/Disassembler is accountable for the condition, quality, and performance of rotating equipment throughout the disassembly, repair and assembly process. This role requires a strong mechanical background, the ability to diagnose equipment issues, interpret technical documentation, perform precision measurements, and ensure all work is completed according to established procedures and quality standards.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate ownership of assigned jobs from teardown through final assembly while continuously identifying opportunities to improve safety, reliability, efficiency, and workmanship.

 
Responsibilities:
    
Mechanical Equipment Ownership:

  • Own the complete disassembly, inspection, repair, assembly, and reconditioning process for blowers and other rotating equipment.
  • Evaluate mechanical components for wear, damage, corrosion, and operational deficiencies.
  • Identify root causes of equipment failures and communicate findings to supervisors and repair teams.
  • Verify all components meet dimensional and quality requirements before reassembly.
 

Assembly and Disassembly Operations:

  • Disassemble blowers and rotating equipment using approved methods and procedures.
  • Clean, inspect, organize, and document equipment components during teardown.
  • Reassemble equipment according to engineering drawings, repair manuals, specifications, and work instructions.
  • Perform bearing installation, seal replacement, shaft alignment, rotor setup, and other precision mechanical assembly functions.
  • Utilize hand tools, power tools, hydraulic equipment, and specialized assembly tooling safely and effectively.
 

Inspection and Quality Ownership:

  • Perform precision measurements using micrometers, calipers, dial indicators, gauges, and other inspection equipment.
  • Verify critical clearances, tolerances, fits, and alignments.
  • Ensure all work meets company quality standards and customer requirements.
  • Maintain accurate inspection and repair records.
  • Participate in quality investigations and corrective action activities when needed.
 

Process Ownership and Continuous Improvement:

  • Take ownership of repair processes and actively drive improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and efficiency.
  • Recommend process improvements, tooling enhancements, and best practices.
  • Support standard work development and adherence.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce rework and improve shop productivity.
  • Assist in training and mentoring less experienced employees on mechanical repair and assembly practices.
 

Safety and Environmental Responsibility:

  • Maintain a safe, organized, and efficient work area.
  • Operate tools, equipment, cranes, and lifting devices in accordance with safety procedures.
  • Properly use all required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Ensure all chemicals and hazardous materials are properly identified, labeled, stored, and handled.
  • Follow all company safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
 

Teamwork and Communication

  • Effectively communicate equipment conditions, repair findings, and technical concerns.
  • Maintain professional working relationships with supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and production personnel.
  • Support departmental goals while maintaining a positive and team-oriented attitude.

Requirements:

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and demonstrated mechanical troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience working with rotating equipment, industrial machinery, automotive systems, heavy equipment, pumps, compressors, blowers, gearboxes, or related mechanical assemblies.
  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, repair manuals, and work instructions.
  • Experience using precision measuring instruments and inspection equipment.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, and mechanical assembly equipment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
 

Preferred:

  • Experience with blower repair, vacuum equipment, compressors, or other rotating equipment.
  • Overhead crane and forklift operation experience.
  • Knowledge of bearings, seals, shafts, fits, tolerances, and alignment techniques.
  • Hazardous materials training.
 

Core Competencies:

  • A strong mechanical troubleshooter.
  • An owner of equipment quality and repair processes.
  • A champion of safety and continuous improvement.
  • A dependable team member who takes accountability for results.
  • A skilled technician capable of delivering reliable, high-quality repair and assembly work with minimal supervision.
  • Lift up to 25 pounds routinely; utilize approved lifting devices or crane assistance for heavier loads.
  • Stand for extended periods throughout the workday.
  • Frequently bend, stoop, reach, and work in various positions while assembling and disassembling equipment.
  • Possess sufficient hand dexterity to operate tools, controls, and measuring instruments.
  • Communicate effectively with team members, supervisors, and support personnel.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Locations: Phoenix, AZ

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview
The Centrifugal Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems & Services division serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 
  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  
  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 
  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, preventative maintenance (PMs), diagnostics, air audits, and leak detection, can benefit their operations. 
  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components.
  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs.
  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 
  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 
Requirements

  • Minimum 2 years of Centrifugal compressor experience.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
Core Competentcies
  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; speciality tools will be provided.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • Ability to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation). 
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting. 
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment). 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. 
  • Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
Preferences:

  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided. 
Pay Range: Starting pay will range between $35.00 - $50.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position

You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
•In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. 
•Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
•Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.

Requirements:

•Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
•Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
•This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
•High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Core Competencies:
•Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
•Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
•Basic vibration troubleshooting.
•Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
•Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
•Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner

Preferences:
•Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
•EPA Certification.
•Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
•Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.

Job Title: Inside Sales & Service Team Lead  


Location: Greer, SC; Norcross, GA; Moody, AL; New Orleans, LA; Nashville, TN; Knoxville, TN

 

About Us  
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and the planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 


Job Overview:

The Inside Sales & Service Team Leader is responsible for coaching the Inside Sales team to achieve the Area’s key performance indicators while providing an exceptional customer experience. This is a working people leader position that is responsible for developing, training, motivating and leading daily responsibilities of the inside sales team. The role is responsible for all sales support from customer inquiry to delivery. The Inside Sales team is split into three key functions: new equipment order and service contract entry, aftermarket parts, and equipment rentals. 

 

Responsibilities  

  • People Leadership – Effectively recruit, coach, and develop Inside Sales team members through effective performance goals and development plans. Develop and deliver new hire onboarding, and process and systems training. Manage performance of direct reports through 1:1 employee coaching, mid-year, and annual performance reviews. 

  • Achieve business objectives – Create and update standard work, set and track performance targets, analyze variances, and initiate process improvements.  Analyze orders, customer feedback, and market data to effectively solve problems, influence sales growth, and implement solutions to drive growth and achieve results.  

  • Optimize work processes – Identify opportunities to standardize and improve processes using lean methodology.  Utilize problem solving and analytical skills to improve performance, enhance customer satisfaction, and drive efficiency.  Report on metrics and use lean tools to solve problems, drive continuous improvement and manage through change.  

  • Compliance – Ensure environmental, health, and safety compliance, and ensure processes for internal audit compliance controls are met.  Verify all month-end checklists and inventory reconciliations are completed with supporting documentation for the entire Inside Sales team.  Assist with the internal audit process.  

  • Inventory Process Management – Drive process improvements in inventory management and transaction accuracy.  Lead and support site preparations for annual physical inventory. 

  • Cross Function Collaboration – Partner with sales team on order processing to minimize errors, increase accountability, and maximize on time delivery.  Partner with service team to drive optimal customer experience and increase communication to reduce delays in new and rented equipment start-up, installation, and invoicing.  

  • Order Execution – Ensure all paperwork and approval requirements are met with accuracy to reduce errors and disputed invoices. Build an Inside Sales team that will effectively manage communications and orders from initial inquiry through to delivery.   

  • Quote Generation – Support Inside Sales team with quote preparation and submission for customer requests, while looking for opportunities to continue growing our business with each account. 

  • Internal Network – Build strong relationships with key factory resources for expediting, data management for accounts and credit, and account managers for processes and questions.  

 

Requirements:  

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • 5+ years of experience in the sales and service industry required
  • 1+ years of experience in Microsoft Office required; ability to navigate internal software programs will be needed after hire. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling. It requires employees to regularly lift and or move up to 10 lbs. and occasionally lift and or move 40+ lbs.  

 

Core Competencies: 

  • Proven ability to build a team that can form strong customer relationships, deliver exceptional customer service, and provide customer-centric solutions. 

  • Exceptional organization, communication (verbal and written), and follow-up skills with the ability to effectively manage a high volume of priorities and commitments with internal and external customers in a highly visible, fast-paced work environment.? 

  • Proven ability to collaborate, influence and support change with stakeholders across multiple levels of a global organization. Ability to build cross-functional partnerships to meet shared strategic business objectives, and drive employee engagement.  

  • Action-oriented with the ability to think and act strategically to manage complexity, adapt to each unique situation, and remove obstacles for the Inside Sales team to achieve business results. 
      

Preferences:  

  • A minimum of five years’ experience with previous experience in the sales and service industry preferred.

  • Strong knowledge of Salesforce (or other CRM platform) and Oracle/ SAP preferred 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

This position will be based in an office within the Region with travel required to other regional offices for meetings, employee on-boarding and training, and other business needs as they arise (up to 25% travel expected).

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. SEEPEX is a leading global specialist in progressing cavity pump technology, control systems, and digital solutions. Operating as a premier brand within the Compression Flow Technologies segment of Ingersoll Rand Company, we deliver modular, highly engineered fluid-handling infrastructure to municipal wastewater, chemical processing, food & beverage, and energy sectors worldwide. Guided by a shared culture of innovation, operational excellence, and entrepreneurial accountability, we empower our teams to solve complex industrial fluid-handling challenges. 

Job Overview: 

The Project Specialist leads cross-functional teams to execute high-complexity, Engineered-to-Order (ETO) progressing cavity pump systems from contract award through final delivery and site testing. This role serves as the primary commercial and technical nexus between external corporate clients and internal design engineering, procurement, manufacturing, assembly, and quality assurance divisions. The ideal candidate will safeguard project margin, delivery velocity, specification alignment, and standard compliance across every milestone. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Project Lifecycle Management: Direct all execution stages for custom progressive cavity pump assemblies, starting at technical handover through mechanical fabrication, testing, and ultimate customer delivery. 
  • Technical Specifications Review: Audit engineered Bills of Materials (BOM), system schematics, and material selections against demanding application environments and client standards. 
  • Testing & Compliance Validation: Coordinate Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), including hydrostatic, performance, NPSH testing, and material traceability audits, ensuring validation against API 676 or contract provisions. 
  • Financial Oversight: Manage dynamic cost architectures, track scope creeping variations, process precise change orders, and preserve targeted gross margins for every project package. 
  • Risk Mitigation Profiles: Mitigate scheduling gaps, supplier lead-time overruns, and mechanical conflicts through proactive resource forecasting and root-cause analytical strategies. 

Requirements: 

  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or an equivalent technical manufacturing discipline. 
  • Professional Experience: 2+ years of active project management experience directly inside heavy industrial environments, specifically focused on rotating machinery, positive displacement pumps, or complex fluid systems. 
  • Systems Competency: Advanced proficiency deploying enterprise tracking platforms (e.g., SAP, Microsoft Project, or JIRA. 

Preferences: 

 
  • Certifications: Project Management Professional (PMP) preferred but not required. 
  • Industry Standards Literacy: Deep understanding of API 676, Hydraulic Institute standards, elastomer fluid-compatibility mechanics. 
  • Soft Skills: Exceptional command-oriented communication, professional negotiating capabilities, and an ability to navigate matrixed multinational corporate structures successfully

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully site based in Enon, OH with minimal travel expected. 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $87,000-$105,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job title:   Quality Engineer

Location: Alsip, IL

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.

Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location: Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.


Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements 
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts

    Core Competencies 
    • Power generation equipment packaging
    • Containerized power solutions
    • Structural and mechanical design
    • Thermal management systems
    • Airflow and ventilation engineering
    • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
    • Fuel system integration
    • Vibration isolation
    • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
    • Reliability and maintainability engineering
    • Data center infrastructure requirements
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

    Preferences:
    • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
    • Experience designing:
      • Generator enclosures
      • Containerized equipment packages
      • Cooling systems
      • Fuel systems
      • Acoustic attenuation solutions
    • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
    • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
    • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
    • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
    • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

    Travel & Work Arrangements
    • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
    • Relocation assistance available
    • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

    Pay Range
    The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.

  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.

Product Development & Standardization

  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.

  • Medium-voltage distribution systems

5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Help Build What’s Next in Industrial Automation.  ARO Fluid Management, a premier global industrial brand within Ingersoll Rand, is ready to take advanced dispense to the next level—and we’re looking for the product leader who can help define where we go next.

The Global Product Manager, Advanced Dispense and Piston Pumps will lead a proven portfolio while accelerating one of the business’s biggest growth opportunities: two-component (2K) dispensing applications.  This is more than a traditional product-management role. The opportunity is to take ARO’s proven piston-pump technology and help transform it into scalable, repeatable advanced-dispense solutions that move, meter, mix and apply adhesives, sealants, foams, coatings, lubricants and other critical materials with precision. These solutions support automotive assembly, battery production, solar manufacturing, marine, coatings, lubrication and automated manufacturing—including applications that may not even be on the roadmap yet.

As Global Product Manager, you’ll define and execute the full portfolio strategy and lifecycle, with a strong focus on finding new applications, customers, markets, channels and system opportunities. You’ll work closely with customers to understand how they manufacture, uncover unmet needs, translate the voice of the customer and market into clear product requirements, and partner with Engineering to turn opportunities into scalable products, systems and services.  Serving as the global connector across Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, Service, regional teams and customers, you’ll shape product roadmaps, lead new-product development and gate reviews, analyze global market and business data, and develop the application stories and commercial tools that help sales teams win.  You’ll also ensure the portfolio remains competitive, profitable and aligned with evolving customer applications, market needs and industrial standards. As an individual contributor with significant global influence, success will depend on your ability to build alignment across functions, influence without authority and turn strategy into action.

We’re looking for a product leader who is curious, commercially minded, technically credible and growth-oriented—someone willing to step into an unfamiliar application, ask the right questions, engage customers and technical experts, test assumptions, learn quickly and challenge the status quo.  With Advanced Dispense positioned as a significant strategic growth area for ARO, this highly visible role offers the opportunity to partner closely with business leadership and help shape the next generation of industrial fluid handling and automation.

If you share our passion for inspiring progress—for bringing about bold shifts in how people, economies and societies operate—then you belong with Ingersoll Rand. Progress begins with you.

Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap:
  • Develop and maintain strategic product roadmaps for Piston Pumps and Advanced Dispense applicable portfolio in IR.
  • dentify new market and application opportunities.
  • Create an exceptional growth focus by enhancing product portfolio and solution extensions specifically for Advanced Dispense applications.
 
Product Lifecycle Management:
  • Oversee the full lifecycle from ideation through end?of?life decisions.
  • Ensure product quality, reliability, and cost competitiveness.
 
Market, Application, and Competitive Analysis:
  • Conduct market research on Advanced Dispense applications and competitors.
  • Benchmark performance and pricing to guide differentiation.
 
Cross Functional Leadership:
  • Lead cross-functional products, solutions, and service development process.
  • Collaborate with Engineering to define requirements and performance targets.
  • Partner with Operations and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturability and cost efficiency.
 
Commercial & Channel Enablement:
  • Support customers, end-users, distributors, sales teams, internal teams with technical?commercial guidance / expertise.
  • Develop pricing and positioning strategies, structures, sales tools, and product value messaging.
    • Collaborate with marketing on product launches and technical content.
    • Enable sales teams with technical training and competitive messaging.
 
Performance & Profitability Management:
  • Monitor and influence key KPIs such as sales, margin, costs, and market share.
  • Lead cost reduction, SKU optimization, and portfolio performance initiatives.

Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
  • 5+ years of progressive product management experience, ideally within pumps, pumping systems, fluid handling, automated dispensing, industrial automation, engineered systems, or a related industrial equipment market. 
  • 3+ years of experience developing product roadmaps, managing product lifecycles, and leading new product development or stage-gate initiatives. 
  • 3+ years of experience conducting market, customer, or application discovery and converting identified needs into actionable product or system requirements. 
  • 3+ years of experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders without direct authority in a matrixed organization.

  • Market Discovery and Customer Insight: Ability to investigate new markets and applications, engage customers and industry experts, identify unmet needs, and translate insights into growth opportunities.
  • Technical-to-Commercial Translation: Ability to convert pump, fluid-handling, dispensing, and application requirements into scalable solutions, compelling value propositions, and effective sales-enablement tools.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership and Influence: Ability to align global Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, and Service teams and drive execution without direct authority.

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.


Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.

Job Summary:
We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented, and organized individual to join our team as a Laboratory Technician. The ideal candidate will play a key role in supporting both sample receipt and filter testing operations in a fast-paced, dynamic laboratory environment. This position involves performing precision work with a focus on accuracy, cleanliness, and adherence to laboratory procedures. Whether you’re experienced or seeking an entry-level opportunity, we value candidates with a passion for science and a commitment to excellence.
 

Responsibilities:
  • Aseptically handle, store, and manage agar contact plates with varying temperature requirements.
  • Execute multi-step incubation processes for colony-forming units (bacteria, yeast, mold). Perform microscopic identification of colony-forming units. 
  • Dispose of biohazardous waste safely and document procedures. 
  • Conduct 10–20 optical microscopies per day, manually counting particulates on filter membranes. Weigh 100–300 customer samples daily using an analytical balance and calculate filter weights via gravimetric analysis. Perform daily calibration of laboratory balances. Load customer samples onto GC-MS instruments and run calibration procedures. 
  • Clean and recycle laboratory media for reuse. Ensure equipment is calibrated, standardized, and functioning properly. Maintain a clean and safe working environment by following procedures, rules, and regulations. 
  • Prepare, review, and improve Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and other documentation. 
  • Produce accurate customer reports based on test findings. Field technical questions from customers and colleagues. Collaborate with team members to ensure timely and accurate results. Contribute to team success by accomplishing related task as needed.


Requirements:
  • Bachelors of Science in Microbiology High School Diploma or GED2+ years of laboratory experience
  • 3+ years of experience with Computer usage with Microsoft office platform and company applications.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing 


Key Competencies:
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to perform repetitive precision work and catch errors that may affect results. Critical Thinking:
  • Capable of identifying mistakes and providing solutions.
  • Ulti-Tasking: Skilled at prioritizing and executing simultaneous activities under pressure.
  • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written abilities to interact with customers and teammates effectively. Adaptability:
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and willing to take on tasks outside the defined scope.



Preferences: Technical Familiarity: Knowledge of microscopy, culture media, GC-MS, autoclaves, incubators, ISO 17025, and sterilization techniques is a plus.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Austin, TX no travel.

Job Title: Materials Manager            
Location:  Charlotte, NC 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Ready to lead where materials strategy directly impacts customers, operations, and results?  As Materials Manager, you will lead an experienced team of Buyer-Planners responsible for purchasing, materials planning, inventory, supplier performance, and aftermarket kit readiness within a complex manufacturing operation. Your leadership will help ensure the right materials are in the right place at the right time—supporting both legacy and next-generation compressor products.

This is more than a scheduling role. You will be the go-to leader when materials issues get difficult—supplier delays, held orders, inventory concerns, source changes, planning gaps, or cross-functional breakdowns. You will dig into root causes, drive solutions, build sustainable processes, and empower your team to prevent issues from recurring. You will also own key materials priorities including inventory performance, on-time delivery, supplier past dues, labor productivity, and continuous improvement, while partnering across Sourcing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Order Management, and Customer Service. With an Oracle-to-SAP transition ahead, you will have a meaningful opportunity to shape processes, strengthen performance, and lead the team through significant operational change.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of people leadership and hands-on materials expertise. You know how to develop talent, establish accountability, and set clear priorities—but you are equally comfortable stepping into the details when the business needs you. Most importantly, you can demonstrate where you have solved complex materials problems, identified root causes, implemented lasting improvements, and measured the results. You bring the technical credibility, analytical mindset, and leadership presence to bring clarity to complexity and turn challenges into sustainable operational improvement.

If you are ready to lead a strong team, solve meaningful operational challenges, and make a measurable impact across the business, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities: 
  • Lead all site materials management activities, including production scheduling, purchasing, inventory control, material movement, indirect materials, and supplier performance.
  • Drive end-to-end material fulfillment from production planning and procurement through warehousing and product shipment.
  • Implement, sustain, and ensure compliance with Materials and SIOP standard work, processes, and systems.
  • Manage materials, suppliers, and inventory within a Lean Six Sigma manufacturing environment, leveraging MRP to improve flow, availability, and inventory performance.
  • Monitor key materials and supplier performance, identify gaps and root causes, and implement countermeasures that deliver measurable, sustainable improvement.
  • Lead, develop, and organize a team of 12–15 Material Planners/Buyers, including performance management, workload allocation, coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sourcing, Engineering, Accounting, Marketing, Operations, Quality, and Global Procurement to support business priorities, supplier selection, and strategic goals.
  • Strengthen supplier relationships and foster a culture of problem solving, accountability, Daily Management, and continuous improvement across the materials organization.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or another relevant discipline. 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 2+ years experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • 1+ years experience with visual management systems. 

Core Competencies
Success in this role requires the following core capabilities and demonstrated strengths. 
  • Materials Systems & Manufacturing Flow – Strong knowledge of manufacturing material flow and integrated systems supporting materials management, production planning, procurement, and distribution; proficiency with MRP/ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Leadership & Change Management – Ability to motivate and develop teams, foster collaboration, and lead change while applying Lean methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
  • Problem Solving & Business Impact – Decisive, proactive problem solver who can identify issues, drive solutions, and influence bottom-line results.
  • Communication & Cross-Functional Partnership – Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across functions, support internal customers, and effectively resolve conflict.
  • Execution & Adaptability – Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure manufacturing environment.

Preferences: 
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM)

Travel and Work Arrangements  
  • This is an onsite role based from our Distribution and Logistics Center
