Job Title: Electrical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:
Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.
  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Switchgear and switchboards
    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment
    • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)
    • UPS interfaces
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
    • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection
  • Perform electrical calculations including:
    • Load flow analysis
    • Equipment sizing
    • Short-circuit studies
    • Voltage drop calculations
    • Protective device coordination
Data Center Power Solutions
  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.
  • Support integration with customer electrical infrastructure and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to evaluate custom power generation and backup power solutions.
  • Support electrical integration for modular and prefabricated power systems used in hyperscale and colocation data centers.
Product Development & Standardization
  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.
  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.
Testing, Validation & Commissioning
  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.
  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.
  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.
  • Troubleshoot electrical integration issues during manufacturing, deployment, and field operation.
Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work directly with data center customers, consultants, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide technical leadership during project execution and customer design reviews.
  • Support sales and business development teams with technical proposals and engineering evaluations.
  • Coordinate with manufacturing and sourcing teams to ensure successful product implementation.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline. 
  • 3+ years of progressive electrical design experience ideally in power generation, critical facilities, industrial systems, modular infrastructure, or related industries. 
  • 3+ years experience interpreting electrical specifications and customer technical requirements.
  • 2+ years experience designing power distribution systems and power generation equipment.
  • 2+ years of proficienct experience in AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, SolidWorks Electrical, or similar design platforms.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in: 
    • Generator systems 
    • Electrical protection and coordination 
    • Low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution 
    • Electrical codes and standards


Core Competencies:
  • Emergency and standby power systems
  • Generator controls and synchronization
  • Utility interconnection
  • Switchgear and switchboards
  • Protective relaying and system coordination
  • Medium-voltage distribution systems
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Energy storage integration
  • Mission-critical infrastructure
  • Data center electrical architecture

Preferences:

5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.
  • Experience with:
    • Data center electrical infrastructure
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Medium-voltage switchgear
    • Microgrid applications
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Knowledge of data center design practices and redundancy architectures.
  • Familiarity with PLC controls, SCADA systems, and power monitoring systems.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers such as Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta, or other colocation providers.
 
Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
  • Relocation assistance available
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Help Build What’s Next in Industrial Automation.  ARO Fluid Management, a premier global industrial brand within Ingersoll Rand, is ready to take advanced dispense to the next level—and we’re looking for the product leader who can help define where we go next.

The Global Product Manager, Advanced Dispense and Piston Pumps will lead a proven portfolio while accelerating one of the business’s biggest growth opportunities: two-component (2K) dispensing applications.  This is more than a traditional product-management role. The opportunity is to take ARO’s proven piston-pump technology and help transform it into scalable, repeatable advanced-dispense solutions that move, meter, mix and apply adhesives, sealants, foams, coatings, lubricants and other critical materials with precision. These solutions support automotive assembly, battery production, solar manufacturing, marine, coatings, lubrication and automated manufacturing—including applications that may not even be on the roadmap yet.

As Global Product Manager, you’ll define and execute the full portfolio strategy and lifecycle, with a strong focus on finding new applications, customers, markets, channels and system opportunities. Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location: Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.


Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements 
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts

    Core Competencies 
    • Power generation equipment packaging
    • Containerized power solutions
    • Structural and mechanical design
    • Thermal management systems
    • Airflow and ventilation engineering
    • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
    • Fuel system integration
    • Vibration isolation
    • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
    • Reliability and maintainability engineering
    • Data center infrastructure requirements
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

    Preferences:
    • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
    • Experience designing:
      • Generator enclosures
      • Containerized equipment packages
      • Cooling systems
      • Fuel systems
      • Acoustic attenuation solutions
    • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
    • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
    • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
    • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
    • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

    Travel & Work Arrangements
    • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
    • Relocation assistance available
    • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.


Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements 
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts

    Core Competencies 
    • Power generation equipment packaging
    • Containerized power solutions
    • Structural and mechanical design
    • Thermal management systems
    • Airflow and ventilation engineering
    • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
    • Fuel system integration
    • Vibration isolation
    • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
    • Reliability and maintainability engineering
    • Data center infrastructure requirements
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

      • Generator enclosures
      • Containerized equipment packages
      • Cooling systems
      • Fuel systems
      • Acoustic attenuation solutions
    • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.

    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems

    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment

    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)

  • Perform electrical calculations including:
    • Load flow analysis

Data Center Power Solutions
  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.

  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.
  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.

  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.
  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.
  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Ready to lead where materials strategy directly impacts customers, operations, and results?  As Materials Manager, you will lead an experienced team of Buyer-Planners responsible for purchasing, materials planning, inventory, supplier performance, and aftermarket kit readiness within a complex manufacturing operation. Your leadership will help ensure the right materials are in the right place at the right time—supporting both legacy and next-generation compressor products.

This is more than a scheduling role. You will be the go-to leader when materials issues get difficult—supplier delays, held orders, inventory concerns, source changes, planning gaps, or cross-functional breakdowns. You will dig into root causes, drive solutions, build sustainable processes, and empower your team to prevent issues from recurring. You will also own key materials priorities including inventory performance, on-time delivery, supplier past dues, labor productivity, and continuous improvement, while partnering across Sourcing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Order Management, and Customer Service. With an Oracle-to-SAP transition ahead, you will have a meaningful opportunity to shape processes, strengthen performance, and lead the team through significant operational change.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of people leadership and hands-on materials expertise. You know how to develop talent, establish accountability, and set clear priorities—but you are equally comfortable stepping into the details when the business needs you. Most importantly, you can demonstrate where you have solved complex materials problems, identified root causes, implemented lasting improvements, and measured the results. You bring the technical credibility, analytical mindset, and leadership presence to bring clarity to complexity and turn challenges into sustainable operational improvement.

If you are ready to lead a strong team, solve meaningful operational challenges, and make a measurable impact across the business, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead all site materials management activities, including production scheduling, purchasing, inventory control, material movement, indirect materials, and supplier performance.
  • Drive end-to-end material fulfillment from production planning and procurement through warehousing and product shipment.
  • Implement, sustain, and ensure compliance with Materials and SIOP standard work, processes, and systems.
  • Manage materials, suppliers, and inventory within a Lean Six Sigma manufacturing environment, leveraging MRP to improve flow, availability, and inventory performance.
  • Monitor key materials and supplier performance, identify gaps and root causes, and implement countermeasures that deliver measurable, sustainable improvement.
  • Lead, develop, and organize a team of 12–15 Material Planners/Buyers, including performance management, workload allocation, coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sourcing, Engineering, Accounting, Marketing, Operations, Quality, and Global Procurement to support business priorities, supplier selection, and strategic goals.
  • Strengthen supplier relationships and foster a culture of problem solving, accountability, Daily Management, and continuous improvement across the materials organization.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or another relevant discipline. 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 2+ years experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • 1+ years experience with visual management systems. 


Core Competencies
Success in this role requires the following core capabilities and demonstrated strengths.

  • Materials Systems & Manufacturing Flow – Strong knowledge of manufacturing material flow and integrated systems supporting materials management, production planning, procurement, and distribution; proficiency with MRP/ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Leadership & Change Management – Ability to motivate and develop teams, foster collaboration, and lead change while applying Lean methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
  • Problem Solving & Business Impact – Decisive, proactive problem solver who can identify issues, drive solutions, and influence bottom-line results.
  • Communication & Cross-Functional Partnership – Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across functions, support internal customers, and effectively resolve conflict.
  • Execution & Adaptability – Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure manufacturing environment.


Preferences:

  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM)


Travel and Work Arrangements 

  • This is an onsite role based from our Distribution and Logistics Center

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Location: Moody, AL (On-site)

Hourly Rate: $32-$35
$3.00 per hour shift differential for 2nd shift employees.
$3,500 Retention bonus, $1,000 bonus, relocation assistance available

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Are you a skilled machinist with a passion for precision and innovation? At Ingersoll Rand, we are seeking a talented and dedicated Manual Machinist to join our dynamic team. This is more than just a job — it’s an opportunity to be part of a company that values craftsmanship, excellence, safety, and collaboration. Join Ingersoll Rand and build your future with a company that recognizes your skills, experience, and contributions while providing opportunities to grow in a supportive and innovative environment.
 
 
Responsibilities:
  • Performs set ups of large Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump components and operations of large Vertical & Horizontal Lathes used to repair and overhaul Large Liquid Rind Vacuum Pumps & Compressors. 
  • Interprets blueprints/drawings to determine critical dimensions, etc. Ability to read Micrometers, Vernier Calipers, Dial Indicators & other precision measuring & test equipment as required. 
  • Able to maintain low tolerances as indicated by specifications or drawings as low as .0005” at times. 
  • Understands how to select appropriate cutting tools for various metals. Understands how to determine speeds and feeds to obtain proper surface finish.
  • Able to work overtime; typically, throughout the week and occasionally on weekends. 
  • Safe operation of Forklift within a Machine Shop environment. Safe Over Head Crane operation. Adheres to all company EH&S & QMS processes.
  • Lifting and rigging of heavy components of various configurations & weights. Assisting in the disassembly, reassembly, repair and rebuilding of Large Liquid Ring Vacuum Pumps.
  • Opportunities to cross train in different areas as necessary, such as: Fabrication, Assembly, Rotar Balancing, etc.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned
 
Requirements:
  • Applicants will be required to demonstrate knowledge of machine setup, as well as usage of machine controls and capabilities. 
  • 3+ years of experience as a machine operator/Machinist.
  • 2+ or more years of experience reading and interpreting blueprints.  
  • 1+ years of experience operating King-style boring mills and/or vertical turning lathes (VTLs).
  • Ability to effectively and safely use a variety of tools and equipment, including but not limited to depth gauges, bore gauges, height gauges, feeler gauges, micrometers, calipers, deburring tools, die grinders, drill presses, and overhead lifting equipment.
 
Core Competencies:
  • Proficiency with prioritizing and meeting multiple deadlines.
  • Ability to convert between metric and US standard units of measure.
  • Ability to deal with problems involving several variables 
  • Ability to use standard problem-solving methods (i.e. 5 Whys) as trained 
  • Ability to effectively share information about job duties in one-on-one and small group situations to supervisor, customers, clients, and other employees of the organization. 
 
Preferences: 
  • HS Diploma or GED preferred. Higher Education or certificate is a plus.
  • Experience with manual machining such as VTL/Boring Mill/ or Horizontal Lathe. Brands would include but not limited to Cincinnati and King brand.
  • Proven ability to set up and operate Manual Machines, work centers, specializing in tool changes and in-process offset adjustments. 
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • This position will be based 100% onsite at our Moody, AL facility

job.title: Maintenance Technician I
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.





Summary of Position

Lubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.  Actively involved in preventive maintenance program to achieve machine goals.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Install, troubleshoot, repair and maintain CNC machinery, electrical systems, pneumatic and hydraulic equipment
  • Reassemble machines after the completion of repair or maintenance work.
  • Start machines and observe mechanical operation to determine efficiency and to detect problems.
  • Inspect or test damaged machine parts, and mark defective areas or advise supervisors of repair needs.
  • Lubricate or apply adhesives or other materials to machines, machine parts, or other equipment, according to specified procedures.
  • Install, replace, or change machine parts and attachments, according to production specifications.
  • Dismantle machines and remove parts for repair, using hand tools, chain falls, jacks, cranes, or hoists.
  • Record production, repair, and machine maintenance information.
  • Read work orders and specifications to determine machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance.
  • Set up and operate machines, and adjust controls to regulate operations.
  • Collaborate with other workers to repair or move machines, machine parts, or equipment.
  • Inventory and requisition machine parts, equipment, and other supplies so that stock can be maintained and replenished.
  • Transport machine parts, tools, equipment, and other material between work areas and storage, using cranes, hoists, or dollies.
  • Collect and discard worn machine parts and other refuse in order to maintain machinery and work areas.
  • Clean machines and machine parts, using cleaning solvents, cloths, air guns, hoses, vacuums, or other equipment.
  • Replace or repair metal, wood, leather, glass, or other lining in machines, or in equipment compartments or containers.

Education Requirements / Certifications

 

  • Three (3) years' experience with CNC machine maintenance preferred

 

Experience / Skill Requirements         

  • Demonstrated experience in electrical and mechanical maintenance including motors, controls, power supplies, AC/DC theory, power distribution, PLC's, hydraulics/pneumatics, lubrication, power transmission and pumps
  • Demonstrated ability to follow all established safe work procedures including, but not limited to personal protection equipment, lockout/tag-out requirements and electrical safety
  • Read and interpret blueprints, technical parts manuals such as electrical and mechanical diagrams, and ability to effectively use and read gages, meters, calipers and other measuring tools
  • Effective and safe use of all required tools including, but not limited to, drills, saws, torches, welders, cranes & hoists, forklifts and other maintenance equipment
  • Ability to work other shifts, weekends and overtime as needed

 

Physical Requirements

  • Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls and reach with hands and arms
  • Occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
  • Occasionally required to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
  • Occasionally required to work near moving mechanical parts
  • Occasionally required to work in outside weather conditions and exposure to moderate cold and heat
  • Frequent exposure to various chemicals, lubricants, and grease

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. SEEPEX is a leading worldwide specialist in pump technology. SEEPEX progressive cavity pumps, pump systems, and digital solutions are used wherever low to highly viscous, aggressive, or abrasive media must be conveyed at low pulsation rates – we keep everything flowing.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (Midwest Region) is responsible for developing and implementing a strategic plan for the Environmental market (including waste water, water treatment, ENV aftermarket sales, and environmental OEM‘s), as well as growing SEEPEX Inc. sales and margins in this market.  Area included in the Western Region: Ohio, Kentucky, West Virginia, Western Pennsylvania, Michigan, Northern Illinois, Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota

Responsibilities:

  • Manage Environmental Sales Channel Partners (SCPs): Review market coverage and partner performance to increase Environmental sales revenue.
  • Drive sales opportunities: Manage Environmental projects through the full sales cycle and support SCPs in closing opportunities.
  • Use market intelligence: Leverage Dodge analytics, GovSpend, and dashboard metrics to evaluate SCP performance and guide review meetings.
  • Develop customer and OEM relationships: Conduct joint sales calls, promote Seepex products and services, and identify new Environmental OEM opportunities.
  • Educate and build relationships: Train SCPs and Environmental Engineers on Seepex products/specifications and maintain contacts with key engineering and biosolids professionals.
  • Influence specifications and applications: Review project specifications, position Seepex equipment for competitive advantage, analyze competitors, and recommend appropriate solutions to Application Engineers.
  • Manage bids and aftermarket opportunities: Coordinate SCPs and Territory Managers, hold pre-bid meetings, establish pricing strategies, track bids/results, and support plant-level aftermarket sales.
  • Monitor and counter competitors: Identify key Environmental competitors, track their activities and differences, and develop presentations highlighting Seepex’s competitive advantages.

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma 
  • 3+ years’ experience with selling Industrial Pumps or related equipment
  • Valid drivers’ licenses. Safe driving record

Core Competencies:

  • Demonstrates a service-oriented customer focus with proven experience in relationship building and providing quality customer experiences.
  • Strong closing and negotiating skills.
  • Must be an articulate and fluent communicator, written and verbal, and at ease with public speaking.
  • Demonstrated strong interpersonal and relationship-building and maintaining skills.
  • Ability to rapidly learn and retain product/service-specific information and utilize to position the features and benefits to customers.
  • Computer literate with knowledge of Microsoft Office and CRM software.
  • Superior organizational and analytical skills with keen attention to detail and quality.
  • Ability to prioritize and multi-task in a flexible, fast-paced and challenging environment.

Preferences:

  • 3+ years sales experience in the municipal or industrial water/wastewater treatment, environmental services, construction, energy or engineering industries.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business or related field.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Remote with travel up to 70%

Pay Range: The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $90,000 - $115,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Strategic Sourcing Manager, New Product Development                
Location:  Mocksville, NC 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Lead the team. Shape the products. Influence what comes next. Ingersoll Rand is evolving its compressor portfolio, and sourcing will help determine how that future takes shape. As a Sourcing Leader within the Compression Systems & Services Americas Sourcing Organization, you’ll lead the people and supplier decisions that bring new products, redesigns, and Innovate to Value (i2V) initiatives from concept through launch. Your greatest impact starts with the team. You’ll develop an established group of sourcing professionals, giving them the coaching, tools, and confidence to make sound decisions and take ownership of their work. Through clear priorities, thoughtful delegation, and meaningful accountability, you’ll strengthen the team’s capabilities while removing barriers and keeping sourcing commitments aligned with project milestones. You’ll also lead selected projects yourself, combining people leadership with hands-on sourcing execution.

Working closely with engineering, project and product management, operations, quality, finance, commodity teams, and suppliers, you’ll guide direct-material sourcing across an industrial compressor portfolio. The work spans components such as motors, drives, electronic controls, and heavy castings within a global supply base. You’ll set sourcing direction, develop supplier strategies, lead complex negotiations, and advance dual-sourcing and risk-mitigation efforts suited to a manufacturing environment with a broad product mix and lower production volumes. You’ll also help define how the team measures success: making progress visible, identifying schedule risks early, and connecting sourcing decisions to cost savings, product margins, quality, and supply assurance. As legacy products evolve and new platforms move toward production, your leadership will help turn sourcing strategy into measurable results.

For a sourcing professional who enjoys developing people, solving complex supplier challenges, and seeing decisions take shape in real products, this is an opportunity to influence both how the team performs and what Ingersoll Rand brings to market next.

Responsibilities: 
  • Sourcing Strategy and Project Leadership: Lead sourcing strategy for NPD and I2V initiatives from early concept through launch and stabilization. Align sourcing resources and deliverables with business objectives, project gates, commodity strategies, supplier rationalization, plant needs, localization objectives, and regional priorities.
  • People Leadership and Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop sourcing professionals supporting NPD, value engineering, localization, supplier transitions, and productivity projects. Set goals, prioritize assignments, balance workloads, conduct performance discussions, and support career development and succession planning. Build capability through best practices, collaboration, barrier removal, and a culture of ownership and accountability.
  • Supplier Selection and Commercial Management: Lead supplier selection, sourcing decisions, RFPs, RFQs, and negotiations, balancing cost, quality, delivery, lead time, capacity, risk, and long-term supplier capability. Oversee pricing, payment terms, tooling, inventory programs, capacity commitments, and supplier development needs.
  • Cost Management and Value Improvement: Own sourcing cost models, business case inputs, and project cost tracking for legacy-to-new product comparisons, productivity targets, and launch readiness. Drive I2V and VAVE workstreams to identify cost reduction, design-to-value, supplier optimization, localization, and specification improvement opportunities.
  • Project Governance and Performance Tracking: Establish standard work, reporting cadence, and performance measures that provide visibility to sourcing milestones, risks, savings, cost avoidance, and launch readiness. Represent Sourcing in product gate reviews, plant reviews, VAVE events, MMR events, and leadership operating reviews, ensuring actions are documented, assigned, and completed.
  • Risk Resolution and Supplier Recovery: Identify gaps to project goals and lead cross-functional countermeasures addressing cost, supplier readiness, part qualification, capacity, delivery, and quality. Manage supplier escalations and recovery plans when issues threaten launches, customer commitments, warranty performance, or project timelines.
  • Cross-Functional Partnerships and Continuous Improvement: Build strong relationships with engineering, product management, operations, quality, finance, commodity leaders, plant teams, and suppliers to align priorities, resolve conflict, and maximize value. Facilitate continuous improvement and ideation sessions to build the project pipeline and strengthen sourcing execution.
  • Special Projects and Additional Responsibilities: Lead or participate in special projects and perform additional duties as assigned.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in sourcing, supply chain, engineering, operations, or project leadership, including direct-material sourcing and support for NPD, VAVE, I2V, and / or complex cross-functional programs.
  • 3+ years of people leadership, supervisory, or team-lead experience, including assigning work, setting priorities, coaching employees, monitoring performance, and supporting employee development.
  • 3+ years of experience coordinating sourcing deliverables with engineering and project management teams through structured development processes, including tracking milestones, resolving barriers, and addressing schedule risks.
  • 3+ years of experience evaluating supplier quotations, selecting suppliers, negotiating pricing and commercial terms, and managing supplier development or performance issues; to include progressive experience preparing business cases and cost models, tracking savings, and analyzing sourcing data to identify gaps and recommend corrective actions.
  • 3+ years of advanced Microsoft Excel experience, including pivot tables and macros; experience using Word and PowerPoint to communicate business information; and general knowledge of how ERP/MRP systems support purchasing, materials planning, and manufacturing operations.

Core Competencies: 
  • Strategic Sourcing Leadership: Translates business priorities into actionable sourcing strategies with proactive planning and sound judgment.
  • People Leadership and Talent Development: Coaches and empowers employees while building trust, collaboration, and accountability.
  • NPD and I2V Execution: Aligns sourcing activities with project milestones, resolves barriers, and maintains progress from concept through launch.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Communicates clearly, aligns stakeholders, manages conflict, and drives timely decisions across organizational levels.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Builds trusted supplier partnerships, negotiates effectively, and resolves escalations while maintaining performance expectations.
  • Commercial and Business Acumen: Balances cost, quality, delivery, and risk to strengthen supplier agreements and business outcomes.
  • Project and Change Management: Prioritizes complex initiatives, meets deadlines, and adapts to changing requirements with resilience and execution discipline.
  • Data-Driven Decision Making: Uses analysis, active listening, and structured problem-solving to evaluate options and guide decisions.
  • Results Orientation: Demonstrates ownership and a bias for action, driving continuous improvement and measurable results.

Preferences: 
  • Advanced degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, or a related field.
  • Sourcing experience in industrial manufacturing, particularly high-mix, low-volume environments involving compressors, rotating equipment, or comparable industrial products.
  • Experience sourcing motors, drives, electronic controls, castings, or other heavy industrial components from global suppliers.
  • Experience developing sourcing dashboards, reporting tools, or project performance measures.
  • Hands-on experience using Oracle, SAP, or another ERP platform in a global environment.
  • Experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methods; Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.

Travel and Work Arrangements  
  • Minimal travel (less than 20%), primarily between the Mocksville and Davidson sites.
  • Occasional supplier visits may also be needed.

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Job Title: Senior Project Manager

Location: Buffalo, NY

Job Overview: 

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for leading the execution of complex engineered-to-order (ETO) centrifugal compressor and packaged equipment projects from order receipt through customer acceptance and project closeout. This role serves as the primary point of contact for customers and is accountable for project safety, quality, schedule, profitability, cash flow, contract compliance, and customer satisfaction. The Senior Project Manager leads cross-functional teams across engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, quality, document control, logistics, field service, finance, and commercial operations to ensure successful project execution and business results.

Key Responsibilities:

Project Execution:

  • Lead multiple complex ETO centrifugal compressor projects simultaneously.
  • Develop and manage project execution plans, schedules, budgets, and deliverables.
  • Drive adherence to project milestones, delivery commitments, and customer requirements.
  • Identify and mitigate project risks while leading recovery plans when required.
  • Provide accurate project forecasting, reporting, and executive-level updates.
  • Customer and Commercial Leadership
  • Serve as the primary customer interface throughout project execution.
  • Build strong customer relationships through proactive communication and issue resolution.
  • Manage contract requirements, scope changes, and project risks.
  • Lead change order identification, development, and commercialization efforts.
  • Preserve contractual entitlement related to customer-caused delays, scope growth, and schedule impacts.
  • Financial and Operational Ownership
  • Own project financial performance including revenue, margin, forecasting, and cost control.
  • Drive booked-versus-shipped margin improvement initiatives.
  • Support milestone billing, cash collection, and working capital objectives.
  • Monitor project performance metrics and implement corrective actions as needed.

 

Cross-Functional Leadership:

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

SEEPEX is a leading worldwide specialist in pump technology. SEEPEX progressive cavity pumps, pump systems, and digital solutions are used wherever low to highly viscous, aggressive, or abrasive media must be conveyed at low pulsation rates – we keep everything flowing.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (Midwest Region) is responsible for developing and implementing a strategic plan for the Environmental market (including waste water, water treatment, ENV aftermarket sales, and environmental OEM‘s), as well as growing SEEPEX Inc. sales and margins in this market.  Area included in the Western Region: Ohio, Kentucky, West Virginia, Western Pennsylvania, Michigan, Northern Illinois, Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota

Responsibilities:

  • Manage Environmental Sales Channel Partners (SCPs): Review market coverage and partner performance to increase Environmental sales revenue.
  • Drive sales opportunities: Manage Environmental projects through the full sales cycle and support SCPs in closing opportunities.
  • Use market intelligence: Leverage Dodge analytics, GovSpend, and dashboard metrics to evaluate SCP performance and guide review meetings.
  • Develop customer and OEM relationships: Conduct joint sales calls, promote Seepex products and services, and identify new Environmental OEM opportunities.
  • Educate and build relationships: Train SCPs and Environmental Engineers on Seepex products/specifications and maintain contacts with key engineering and biosolids professionals.
  • Influence specifications and applications: Review project specifications, position Seepex equipment for competitive advantage, analyze competitors, and recommend appropriate solutions to Application Engineers.
  • Manage bids and aftermarket opportunities: Coordinate SCPs and Territory Managers, hold pre-bid meetings, establish pricing strategies, track bids/results, and support plant-level aftermarket sales.
  • Monitor and counter competitors: Identify key Environmental competitors, track their activities and differences, and develop presentations highlighting Seepex’s competitive advantages.

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma 
  • 3+ years’ experience with selling Industrial Pumps or related equipment
  • Valid drivers’ licenses. Safe driving record

Core Competencies:

  • Demonstrates a service-oriented customer focus with proven experience in relationship building and providing quality customer experiences.
  • Strong closing and negotiating skills.
  • Must be an articulate and fluent communicator, written and verbal, and at ease with public speaking.
  • Demonstrated strong interpersonal and relationship-building and maintaining skills.
  • Ability to rapidly learn and retain product/service-specific information and utilize to position the features and benefits to customers.
  • Computer literate with knowledge of Microsoft Office and CRM software.
  • Superior organizational and analytical skills with keen attention to detail and quality.
  • Ability to prioritize and multi-task in a flexible, fast-paced and challenging environment.

Preferences:

  • 3+ years sales experience in the municipal or industrial water/wastewater treatment, environmental services, construction, energy or engineering industries.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business or related field.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Remote with travel up to 70%

Pay Range: The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $90,000 - $115,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Electrical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:
Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.
  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Switchgear and switchboards
    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment
    • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)
    • UPS interfaces
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
    • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection
  • Perform electrical calculations including:
    • Load flow analysis
    • Equipment sizing
    • Short-circuit studies
    • Voltage drop calculations
    • Protective device coordination
Data Center Power Solutions
  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.
  • Support integration with customer electrical infrastructure and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to evaluate custom power generation and backup power solutions.
  • Support electrical integration for modular and prefabricated power systems used in hyperscale and colocation data centers.
Product Development & Standardization
  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.
  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.
Testing, Validation & Commissioning
  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.
  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.
  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.
  • Troubleshoot electrical integration issues during manufacturing, deployment, and field operation.
Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work directly with data center customers, consultants, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide technical leadership during project execution and customer design reviews.
  • Support sales and business development teams with technical proposals and engineering evaluations.
  • Coordinate with manufacturing and sourcing teams to ensure successful product implementation.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline. 
  • 3+ years of progressive electrical design experience ideally in power generation, critical facilities, industrial systems, modular infrastructure, or related industries. 
  • 3+ years experience interpreting electrical specifications and customer technical requirements.
  • 2+ years experience designing power distribution systems and power generation equipment.
  • 2+ years of proficienct experience in AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, SolidWorks Electrical, or similar design platforms.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in: 
    • Generator systems 
    • Electrical protection and coordination 
    • Low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution 
    • Electrical codes and standards


Core Competencies:
  • Emergency and standby power systems
  • Generator controls and synchronization
  • Utility interconnection
  • Switchgear and switchboards
  • Protective relaying and system coordination
  • Medium-voltage distribution systems
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Energy storage integration
  • Mission-critical infrastructure
  • Data center electrical architecture

Preferences: 
  • 5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.
  • Experience with:
    • Data center electrical infrastructure
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Medium-voltage switchgear
    • Microgrid applications
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Knowledge of data center design practices and redundancy architectures.
  • Familiarity with PLC controls, SCADA systems, and power monitoring systems.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers such as Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta, or other colocation providers.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm
  • Open to relocation assistance

Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview: 

The Electrical Engineer is responsible for the development, optimization, troubleshooting, and long-term support of manufacturing test systems used in end-of-line (EOL) testing of pumps, compressors, motors, and related products. The position also supports laboratory instrumentation including pressure, temperature, flow, and electrical measurement systems and provides electrical and controls engineering support to plant maintenance and manufacturing teams. This role partners closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, and Operations teams to improve product validation processes, increase test system reliability, enhance data collection capabilities, and ensure products consistently meet customer and quality requirements. 

 

Responsibilities: 

  • Design, develop, implement, and maintain electrical and automated end-of-line test systems used to validate product performance, safety, and quality requirements prior to shipment.
  • Develop and support LabVIEW, National Instruments, PLC-based, and data acquisition systems used for manufacturing and laboratory testing.
  • Troubleshoot and improve electrical test equipment, instrumentation, sensors, controls, drives, and data collection systems to maximize uptime and test accuracy.
  • Support pressure, temperature, flow, electrical, vibration, and performance measurement systems used in manufacturing and product qualification testing.
  • Partner with Quality and Manufacturing teams to investigate test failures, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve product quality and first-pass yield.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on test automation, process capability, cycle-time reduction, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Support new product introductions by developing test methodologies, validation plans, fixtures, work instructions, and production support processes.
  • Provide electrical engineering support to plant operations, maintenance, and capital projects, including equipment upgrades and modernization initiatives. 
 

Requirements: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing, automation, controls, or test/industrial electrical engineering, including hands-on development, maintenance, or troubleshooting of automated test equipment and electrical measurement systems.
  • 3+ years with LabVIEW and National Instruments hardware/software platforms, with hands-on exposure to industrial instrumentation (pressure, temperature, flow, vibration, power measurement)
  • 1+ years supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment

Core Competencies:  

  • Manufacturing Test System Expertise
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Root Cause Analysis and Problem Solving
  • Data-Driven Decision Making
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Customer and Quality Focus 
 

Preferences: 

  • Experience supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, project management, and cross-functional communication skills. 
  • Knowledge of electrical controls, PLCs, VFDs, motors, sensors, industrial communications, and data acquisition systems.
  • Experience with pumps, compressors, rotating equipment, or industrial machinery.
  • Knowledge of electrical safety standards, risk assessments, system validation, and design verification testing.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is fully site-based at the Monroe, Louisiana manufacturing facility.
    • Occasional travel may be required to support equipment suppliers, training activities, customer requirements, or other business needs.
