Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) role within its Industrial Technologies and Services (ITS) Business Unit will be responsible for sales growth and business development activities for air treatment solutions, to include air dryers, process chillers, nitrogen generators, oil-water separators, both new sales and rentals in the Southwestern US. The Regional Sales Manager will utilize their technical expertise in how the equipment is utilized in the market and will work closely with channel partners to cultivate, foster, and grow the presence of our products in the marketplace. Establishing and growing the distributor and OEM business relationships, growing revenue and market share for the portfolio, and maintaining profit margins are key for this role. Join us in making the ITS division of Ingersoll Rand an outstanding place to work where both our team and our company thrive! 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand market presence and achieve sales targets in the Southwest region.
  • Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscape to identify new business opportunities and areas for growth.
  • Follow established visitation frequencies for channel partners and achieve a cadence structure for reporting new opportunities, forecasting, revenue progress, etc.
  • Regularly track sales performance and key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess progress towards targets and identify areas for improvement.
  • Identify and recruit new distribution/channel partners and acquire new distribution/channel partners to expand market reach and penetration. This includes establishing and growing synergistic channel partners throughout the region.
  • Oversee the Distribution/Channel Partner network in the Southwest territory: act as the main point of contact for distributors, including business owners, sales teams, and service leaders and guide their activities and priorities. 
  • Partner with the ITS Support teams (manufacturing, service and warranty, customer service, e-commerce, etc.) to improve collaboration, establish best practices, and grow the channel partner and organizations market share.
  • Develop, mentor and coach channel partner sales team in fostering customer relationships, train distribution personnel, and assess their proficiency in supporting products and services.
  • Establish performance benchmarks for individual product lines to gauge distributor effectiveness and drive sales outcomes.
  • Identify underserved areas and geographies, devising business plans to expand coverage.
  • Spot gaps in market/industry coverage and competition and emerging market trends and refocus existing or new channels to address these gaps.
  • Resolve conflicts within the channel and region.
  • Maintain ongoing distribution engagement that supports consistent, high-impact activities.
  • Develop and manage an active opportunity pipeline with all partner organizations, collecting regular feedback to monitor progress.
  • Actively pursue and support competitive conversion opportunities identified in the pipeline.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Enablement & Product Management to capitalize on pricing, product specifications, and new product potential.
  • Provide hands-on feedback to sales team, sharing insights on trends, competition, economics, and other factors to help identify and prioritize strategic opportunities.
  • Lead, motivate, and work with other members of the sales team and channel partners to meet revenue targets, ensure high level of new customer activity, and focus resources to achieve strategic account penetration.
  • Seek and communicate the voice of the customer (VOC) to build strong customer relationships, understand their needs, and communicate risks and opportunities to the ITS leadership team.
  • Collaborate with marketing & product management to establish market pricing and develop sales strategies to realize sales of existing and new products to meet or exceed revenue and profit targets.
  • Establish sales forecasts, plans & objectives for your region and by product line and provide weekly / monthly / yearly forecasting to update the business on short and long-term trends.
  • Track regional metrics to communicate key performance indicators relating to sales, profitability, market share and competitor activities.

Requirements:

  • High school Diploma or Equivalent 
  • 5+ years of industrial sales ideally in industrial equipment, compressed air, air treatment solutions (dryers, filtration, condensate management) or related sectors.

Core Competencies:

  • Formulate a clear and compelling regional sales strategy that aligns with the overall business objectives. This includes identifying market opportunities, defining target customer segments, and outlining a roadmap to achieve sales goals.
  • Optimizing the sales process, including following best practices, implementing sales methodologies, and continuously improving workflows through standard operating procedures. 
  • Ability to gather, interpret and effectively communicate product information in a clear, concise, way, using multiple communication channels (verbal, written, email, chat) to various internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical specifications, product technical literature, construction plans/drawings, commercial terms and conditions, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries from internal or external customers or suppliers.
  • Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of practical problems.
  • Uses technical knowledge to assess the potential application of company products, recommending solutions that meet customer needs, and advance the sales process.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology, or business
  • Experience with air compressors and/or air dryers preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience using data to drive distributors behavior and success.
  • Understanding of principles of air compression and/or air treatment, and applications.
  • Understanding of commercial terms including payment terms, receivables, shipping terms, and contract terms and conditions review.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the West region.

Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $90,000 - $110,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Location: Monroe, LA (On-site) 

 

About Us

Job Overview: 

The Electrical Engineer is responsible for the development, optimization, troubleshooting, and long-term support of manufacturing test systems used in end-of-line (EOL) testing of pumps, compressors, motors, and related products. The position also supports laboratory instrumentation including pressure, temperature, flow, and electrical measurement systems and provides electrical and controls engineering support to plant maintenance and manufacturing teams. This role partners closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, and Operations teams to improve product validation processes, increase test system reliability, enhance data collection capabilities, and ensure products consistently meet customer and quality requirements. 

 

Responsibilities: 

  • Design, develop, implement, and maintain electrical and automated end-of-line test systems used to validate product performance, safety, and quality requirements prior to shipment.
  • Develop and support LabVIEW, National Instruments, PLC-based, and data acquisition systems used for manufacturing and laboratory testing.
  • Troubleshoot and improve electrical test equipment, instrumentation, sensors, controls, drives, and data collection systems to maximize uptime and test accuracy.
  • Support pressure, temperature, flow, electrical, vibration, and performance measurement systems used in manufacturing and product qualification testing.
  • Partner with Quality and Manufacturing teams to investigate test failures, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve product quality and first-pass yield.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on test automation, process capability, cycle-time reduction, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Support new product introductions by developing test methodologies, validation plans, fixtures, work instructions, and production support processes.
  • Provide electrical engineering support to plant operations, maintenance, and capital projects, including equipment upgrades and modernization initiatives. 

 

Requirements: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing, automation, controls, or test/industrial electrical engineering, including hands-on development, maintenance, or troubleshooting of automated test equipment and electrical measurement systems.
  • 3+ years with LabVIEW and National Instruments hardware/software platforms, with hands-on exposure to industrial instrumentation (pressure, temperature, flow, vibration, power measurement)
  • 1+ years supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment


Core Competencies:  

  • Manufacturing Test System Expertise
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Root Cause Analysis and Problem Solving
  • Data-Driven Decision Making
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Customer and Quality Focus 

 

Preferences: 

  • Experience supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, project management, and cross-functional communication skills. 
  • Knowledge of electrical controls, PLCs, VFDs, motors, sensors, industrial communications, and data acquisition systems.
  • Experience with pumps, compressors, rotating equipment, or industrial machinery.
  • Knowledge of electrical safety standards, risk assessments, system validation, and design verification testing.

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is fully site-based at the Monroe, Louisiana manufacturing facility.
    • Occasional travel may be required to support equipment suppliers, training activities, customer requirements, or other business needs.

Job Overview:
The Territory Sales Manager - Responsible for sales growth and business development of Gardner Denver branded compressed air equipment and components through authorized Gardner Denver distributors in the U.S. We are seeking a motivated and results-driven professional to develop and execute business strategies aimed at increasing sales revenue and asset attachment, with a focus on key strategic initiatives. This role involves the successful implementation of commercial business programs and requires expertise in rotating equipment or air compressor products, services, and solutions. As the primary point of contact for assigned distributors, you will build strong relationships with business owners, sales teams, and service leaders to drive growth and collaboration. The role emphasizes territory management, distributor business development, and revenue growth through active customer engagement.


The ideal candidate must be willing to travel overnight as needed to achieve business objectives and foster distributor and customer relationships.


Responsibilities:

  • Manage Gardner Denver branded air compression sales and growth through the distribution channel, developing penetration plans to increase market share and increase recurring revenue through service programs at end-user accounts.
  • Build, maintain, and strengthen distributor relationships at all levels, resolving channel conflicts and ensuring high distributor capability to serve and develop customers.
  • Provide technical expertise and customer support by leveraging Gardner Denver resources to ensure consistent service quality and product knowledge.
  • Collaborate with other business units on pricing, service contract growth, strategy, and warranty concerns to align sales execution with company goals.
  • Measure distributor performance, implement improvement programs, and drive revenue growth across aftermarket parts, service offerings, and support new product sales.
  • Manage commercial programs ensuring alignment with organizational objectives while optimizing results through the distribution network.
  • Gather, analyze, and report monthly on regional activities, competitive strategies, and market trends.
  • Maintain accurate data in CRM systems (CC360 – Salesforce).
  • Pursue continuous training, while coaching and assessing distributor personnel to enhance their technical and commercial competencies in Gardner Denver products and services.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent).
  • 3+ years of experience in mechanical sales, with increasing responsibility within the sales hierarchy.

Core Competencies:

  • A wide variety of creativity and communication is required to motivate the sales force.
  • Strong interpersonal abilities along with excellent communication skills will assist the incumbent in being successful.
  • Proficient with various sales concepts, practices, and procedures.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) in Business, Engineering, Marketing, Management or related areas.
  • Experience with service contracts and aftermarket sales for mechanical equipment is highly preferred.
  • Familiarity with rotating equipment with an emphasis on after-sales services is preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite & Salesforce tracking software.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • This is a remote based position that is to be located near a major airport in the U.S.
  • Travel to distribution and customer sites expected up to 50% of the time.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations included, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, Multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $100,000-$120,000 The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

 Job Title: Area Service Leader 

Location: Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ

 

About Us  

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

 

Job Summary  

The Area Service Leader position is responsible for providing the leadership for all service activities from the installation of new equipment to the implementation of a services contract through lifetime connectivity with that customer.  Processes within that oversight include support of sales through contract pricing on parts and service, field service coordination, management of technicians and service supervisors, customer satisfaction, and responsibility for the revenue and margin of the parts and service business within the geography.  Provides strategy for connectivity and services growth within the defined region. This position is responsible for service growth for office locations within the West Region (Southern California, Arizona & Nevada).   

 

Responsibilities  

  • Accountable for full services portfolio performance.  Ensure technicians training and skill level is appropriately balanced to service customers, and leverage resources across the area.  This includes emergency repair (break/fix), regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components (parts), and long-term service agreements (Package Care).  

  • Collaborate with the Operations Leader to ensure service coordination processes/functions are aligned with service objectives. Collaborate with sales on contract pricing of parts and services to maintain and enhance profitable service operations. 

  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, and develop all service employees.  Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process and technical skills, to the highest degree possible.    

  • Proactively build the technician and service supervisor pipeline (internally and externally) and strategically manage your workforce to prevent resource gaps.  

  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team.  Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting the customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  

  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure a safe and productive work environment both in the shop and at customer sites.  

  • Visit customers on a regular basis to build relationships and provide solutions.  

 
Requirements: 

  • Bachelor’s Degree required in a related discipline; Engineering, Technical, Marketing or Business preferred. 

  • 5+ years of experience in industrial product space, preferably with a diverse product portfolio including service offerings.   


  • 3+ years management experience, preferably in a customer facing environment.

 

Key Competencies 

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. 

  • Leadership skills are essential. Individual must be able to manage an hourly technical workforce, including remote employees, as well as salaried staff.   

  • Work is completed through other employees, so this person must excel at hiring, developing, training, coaching, leading and motivating a diverse workforce for optimal results.  

  • Profit & Loss experience is critical. Individual must have experience in forecasting needs, obtaining resources, and managing budgets.

  • A strategic business mindset is important. This individual must be able to support the Regional Director in creation of a strategic business plan for growing the service business through internal process improvements and lean strategies to positively impact our market position.
     

Preferences:
Technical and/or mechanical capabilities are a plus.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

This position will be based out of one of the West region area customer centers with regional and overnight ,out of town travel required (45-70%). 

The pay range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $130,000 - $170,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.  



What We Offer: 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support needed to take charge of your health and future. 
 
Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond. 


Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.


What We Offer

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances. 

Job Title: Scheduling Coordinator
Location: Sedalia, MO onsite 

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.
 

Job Overview:

The Scheduling Coordinator supports production planning and scheduling activities for Kit Production and Paragon Whole Goods. This role ensures production orders are released, monitored, and coordinated to support customer demand, inventory targets, and on-time delivery goals. The coordinator works closely with Production, Materials, Purchasing, Engineering, Customer Service, and Supply Chain to resolve scheduling conflicts, monitor shortages, and maintain production visibility.
 

Responsibilities:

Create, maintain, and communicate production schedules for Kit Production and Paragon Whole Goods.

Release and monitor production orders in SAP or the applicable ERP/MRP system.

Monitor schedule attainment and identify risks to planned production completion.

Coordinate schedule adjustments based on material availability, capacity constraints, customer priorities, and changing production needs.

Review material shortages and partner with the Master Scheduler, Purchasing, Inventory Control, and Production to minimize disruptions.

Monitor kit availability and support actions needed to maintain production flow.

Track schedule attainment, on-time completion, backlog, and inventory levels; maintain scheduling reports and production dashboards.

Support daily production meetings with schedule status, recovery plans, and clear cross-functional communication.
 

Requirements:

High school diploma or GED required.

At least 2 years of experience using computers and Microsoft Office applications in a professional environment.

Strong Microsoft Excel proficiency; candidates should be comfortable working with data and completing everyday Excel tasks.

Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills.

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and work independently without requiring close supervision.
 

Core Competencies:

Self-motivated, driven, and accountable for results.

Collaborative and able to work effectively with cross-functional teams and different personalities.

Detail-oriented, organized, data-focused, and interested in becoming a subject matter expert.
 

Preferences:

Experience working in a database, inventory system, ERP, or MRP environment; SAP experience is preferred but not required.

Experience in manufacturing, production scheduling, planning, inventory control, supply chain, or a related operations environment is preferred but not required.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This is a fully on-site, hourly position in Sedalia, Missouri. Standard hours are Monday-Friday, 7:00 AM-3:30 PM, with some flexibility for office-hour schedules such as 8:00 AM-4:30 PM based on business needs. The position is overtime eligible, with overtime worked at the manager’s discretion, particularly during month-end and quarter-end periods. Weekend overtime is uncommon unless business needs require it. Remote or work-from-home arrangements are not available for this position.

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Overview:
The Manufacturing Technician supports daily production and fabrication operations by measuring, cutting, fitting, and assembling PVC and CPVC components according to specifications. This position uses a variety of hand tools, power tools, and fabrication equipment while following drawings and work instructions to produce quality products safely and efficiently. The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a hands-on manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Measure, cut, fit, glue, and assemble PVC and CPVC components according to specifications, shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Operate saws, drills, routers, hand tools, power tools, and other fabrication equipment used in production.
  • Assemble components manually and with semi-automatic or automatic production equipment, as required.
  • Perform basic equipment setups and routine maintenance on fabrication tools and equipment.
  • Inspect completed products and perform required quality checks to ensure workmanship and specifications meet company standards.
  • Support material handling activities, including loading/unloading shipments, inventory, picking, packing, and material movement as needed.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area while following established safety procedures and production standards.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet production schedules and adapt to changing production needs.

Requirements:

  • 1–3 years of experience in a manufacturing, fabrication, assembly, or similar hands-on production environment.
  • Ability to read and interpret basic shop drawings, blueprints, work orders, and production specifications.
  • Ability to accurately use a tape measure and basic measuring tools.
  • Basic knowledge and hands-on experience using hand tools, power tools, and production or fabrication equipment.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to follow instructions and complete hands-on assembly/fabrication tasks.
  • Strong attention to detail with a commitment to quality and safe work practices.
  • Good communication, teamwork, time-management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to lift up to 40 pounds and work overtime as needed.
Preferences:
  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Previous experience measuring, cutting, fitting, or gluing PVC/CPVC pipe.
  • Experience with pipe fabrication, plumbing, plastics manufacturing, PVC solvent welding, or mechanical fittings.
  • Previous experience performing product inspections, documenting quality checks, or completing quality forms.
  • Forklift experience or certification is a plus.

Ingersoll Rand, a company with ~$8B in annual revenue and 22,000 employees world-wide, is seeking a Product Management Excellence Leader for its Precision Technologies (PT) business unit that will be focused on designing the Product Management / NPD operating model, coaching talent & building capability, and scaling product management excellence across an entire organization.

Responsibilities:

  • Application Intelligence and Market Sizing
    • Own standard work for VOC process and host trainings, drive team adherence and create centralized customer insight database
    • Own and maintain AIM (applications, industries, markets) framework for PT overall to establish master list of target applications and total addressable market for each. Conduct periodic review to determine PT market share and identify gaps in regions/countries/markets
    • From won/lost funnel analysis, document scalable wins as references for sales and marketing and document product gaps as inputs to respective sub business unit product managers

 

  • Own Ingersoll Ran Product Excellence (IRPX) gate process and strengthen business case approval process for NPD
    • Own Stage-Gate process and deployment to drive excellence for PM and Engineering organizations, hold teams accountable to targeted toll gate dates, while establishing countermeasures to recover Engineering delays
    • Strengthen gate review process for phase gate 1, phase gate 2, create and enforce standard work for business case review at both gates, bring a neutral perspective and reduce low impact product development
    • Strengthen gate review process for phase gate 3, with standard work to translate validated business case for production inventory requirements

 

  • Drive deliverables between the Ingersoll Rand Engineering & Technology Center (IRETC) and regional business unit Engineering teams
    • Drive coordination of Engineering priorities in regions, across global business units, and with IRETC
    • Create structure to evaluate projects and deliverables that will be executed by the IRETC
    • Be the liaison with team of ~50 Engineering resources located in India, while keeping teams accountable to mutually agreed upon deliverables and timelines

 

  • IP strategy, product rationalization
    • At TG1, identify intellectual property opportunities, technology blocks, to feed patent strategy
    • Create and deploy product rationalization framework to drive simplified product portfolio with more meaning to customers

 

  • Own product related cybersecurity review process
    • Establish criteria for cyber security review process within IRPX gate process
    • For products launched, create framework together with corporate IT security resources to flag, prioritize and mitigate security risks
    • Create project plans for security mitigation and ensure on time deliverables of product security related projects 

Requirements:

  • Product Management Expertise: 8+ years of Product Management experience, with at least 3 years leading teams and building PM capability through structured mentorship 
  • Systems Thinker: Deep understanding of Agile/Scrum frameworks, product discovery techniques, and metrics-driven execution 
  • Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and develop effective solutions with a keen continuous improvement mind-set
  • Communication: Exceptional stakeholder management and executive presence to champion organizational change
  • Project / Program Management: Strong project / program management skills, including planning, execution, and monitoring
  • Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Framework Design: Created and launched original, company-wide internal training academies or product management bootcamps.
  • Agile Evolution: Managed transitions from legacy project-based delivery models to modern, outcomes-driven product operating models.

Job Summary The Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for supporting inventory accuracy, logistics operations, and supply chain execution within our third-party logistics (3PL) network. This role works closely with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and logistics providers to ensure efficient material flow, inventory integrity, and compliance with established business controls. The Supply Chain Specialist will coordinate inventory processes including cycle counting, physical inventories, inventory classification maintenance, discrepancy resolution, and inventory reporting. This position will also support continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance operational efficiency, improve inventory accuracy, reduce costs, and support customer satisfaction.
  Responsibilities
  • Monitor and support third-party logistics (3PL) provider performance by reviewing service levels, inventory accuracy metrics, and adherence to established operational requirements.
  • Analyze inventory data and prepare reports on inventory levels, inventory turns, shortages, excess inventory, and other key performance indicators.
  • Investigate and resolve inbound receiving discrepancies by working with suppliers, warehouse personnel, and internal stakeholders to ensure timely correction of errors.
  • Coordinate and support cycle count activities, including schedule adherence, variance investigation, and inventory record reconciliation and annual Physical Inventory activities to ensure accurate inventory documentation.
  • Maintain and update ABC/XYZ inventory classifications to support effective inventory planning and management strategies.
  • Partner with procurement, planning, operations, and customer service teams to optimize inventory availability while minimizing excess stock and shortages.
  • Ensure inventory transactions are processed in accordance with SOX requirements, company policies, and Accounting Limitation of Authority (LOA) guidelines.
  • Support inventory-related audits by gathering documentation, validating inventory records, and assisting with corrective action implementation.
  • Participate in continuous improvement projects focused on inventory accuracy, warehouse efficiency, material flow, and process standardization.
  • Conduct root cause analysis on inventory discrepancies and implement corrective actions to improve inventory performance.
  • Collaborate with customer service and warehouse operations to resolve inventory-related issues, including stockouts, shipping discrepancies, and material availability concerns.
  • Support Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve operational performance.
  • Assist with returns processing and inventory disposition activities, ensuring accurate inventory adjustments and proper documentation.
  • Coordinate activities associated with obsolete and excess inventory, including identification, reporting, and disposition recommendations.

Requirements:
  • 2+ years of experience in logistics, supply chain, inventory control, warehouse operations, materials planning, or related disciplines.
  • 1+ years of experience working with ERP systems, preferably Oracle R12.

Core Competencies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and follow-through skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate across functions and build productive working relationships.
  • Self-motivated and proactive with a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Knowledge of inventory management principles and supply chain processes.
  • Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience supporting process improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies preferred.
  • Ability to identify trends, analyze data, and recommend practical solutions to improve operational performance.
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to resolve supplier AP and invoicing issues
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to assist Warehouse management with priority shipments

Preference: 
 
  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and data analysis tools.
  • Experience utilizing reporting and analytics tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Alteryx, KNIME, SQL, or similar systems is preferred.
  • Knowledge of inventory control practices, cycle counting, physical inventory processes, and warehouse operations.
  • APICS CPIM, CSCP, or related certification is preferred.
  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully onsite based

Job Summary The Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for supporting inventory accuracy, logistics operations, and supply chain execution within our third-party logistics (3PL) network. This role works closely with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and logistics providers to ensure efficient material flow, inventory integrity, and compliance with established business controls. The Supply Chain Specialist will coordinate inventory processes including cycle counting, physical inventories, inventory classification maintenance, discrepancy resolution, and inventory reporting. This position will also support continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance operational efficiency, improve inventory accuracy, reduce costs, and support customer satisfaction.
  Responsibilities
  • Monitor and support third-party logistics (3PL) provider performance by reviewing service levels, inventory accuracy metrics, and adherence to established operational requirements.
  • Analyze inventory data and prepare reports on inventory levels, inventory turns, shortages, excess inventory, and other key performance indicators.
  • Investigate and resolve inbound receiving discrepancies by working with suppliers, warehouse personnel, and internal stakeholders to ensure timely correction of errors.
  • Coordinate and support cycle count activities, including schedule adherence, variance investigation, and inventory record reconciliation and annual Physical Inventory activities to ensure accurate inventory documentation.
  • Maintain and update ABC/XYZ inventory classifications to support effective inventory planning and management strategies.
  • Partner with procurement, planning, operations, and customer service teams to optimize inventory availability while minimizing excess stock and shortages.
  • Ensure inventory transactions are processed in accordance with SOX requirements, company policies, and Accounting Limitation of Authority (LOA) guidelines.
  • Support inventory-related audits by gathering documentation, validating inventory records, and assisting with corrective action implementation.
  • Participate in continuous improvement projects focused on inventory accuracy, warehouse efficiency, material flow, and process standardization.
  • Conduct root cause analysis on inventory discrepancies and implement corrective actions to improve inventory performance.
  • Collaborate with customer service and warehouse operations to resolve inventory-related issues, including stockouts, shipping discrepancies, and material availability concerns.
  • Support Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve operational performance.
  • Assist with returns processing and inventory disposition activities, ensuring accurate inventory adjustments and proper documentation.
  • Coordinate activities associated with obsolete and excess inventory, including identification, reporting, and disposition recommendations.

Requirements:
  • 2+ years of experience in logistics, supply chain, inventory control, warehouse operations, materials planning, or related disciplines.
  • 1+ years of experience working with ERP systems, preferably Oracle R12.

Core Competencies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and follow-through skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate across functions and build productive working relationships.
  • Self-motivated and proactive with a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Knowledge of inventory management principles and supply chain processes.
  • Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience supporting process improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies preferred.
  • Ability to identify trends, analyze data, and recommend practical solutions to improve operational performance.
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to resolve supplier AP and invoicing issues
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to assist Warehouse management with priority shipments

Preference: 
 
  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and data analysis tools.
  • Experience utilizing reporting and analytics tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Alteryx, KNIME, SQL, or similar systems is preferred.
  • Knowledge of inventory control practices, cycle counting, physical inventory processes, and warehouse operations.
  • APICS CPIM, CSCP, or related certification is preferred.
  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully onsite based

Job Title: Field Service Manager, Industrial Compressors & Controls              
Location: Ponoma, CA  (Hybrid, with travel)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Lead the team, solve the tough technical challenges, and keep industry moving in a highly visible service leadership role supporting some of the region’s most critical industrial operations. The Field Service Manager, is a supervisory position that is is a highly visible leadership role supporting Ingersoll Rand’s – Plant Air Centrifugal (PAC) compressed air business across California and Arizona. Working with major manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, and defense customers, this leader becomes a trusted resource when equipment reliability, uptime, and fast technical decisions matter most.

You’ll lead and develop a team of PAC Field Service Technicians responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing sophisticated centrifugal compressed air systems. Just as importantly, you’ll help build the next generation of the regional service team through recruiting, hands-on coaching, technical training, and technician development. This is not a desk-only leadership role. The right candidate brings technical credibility, strong people leadership, and confidence in front of customers. You’ll work alongside technicians, ask the right diagnostic questions, guide complex troubleshooting, and help identify safe, practical solutions when standard parts or factory support cannot meet a customer’s timeline. 

Direct centrifugal-compressor experience is preferred, but we also welcome candidates with strong backgrounds in industrial electrical systems, switchgear, automation, controls, PLCs, or microprocessor-based equipment who are ready to expand their technical expertise.  Based from Pomona, California, this hybrid position includes approximately 50% regional travel, with some overnight stays. You’ll have the backing of an established global OEM, factory training and certification opportunities, strong engineering and technical resources, and a safety-first culture—along with the opportunity to build a high-performing service team and make a direct impact on some of the region’s most demanding industrial operations.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting the customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
  • Other duties as assigned to support the service business and ensure customer satisfaction.  

Requirements
  • High School diploma or GED with relavant experience.
  • 5+ years’ experience in an industrial sales business setting. 
  • 3+ years’ experience in supervising / managing teams of people, such as a combination of relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Core Competencies 
  • Advanced operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.
  • Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Advanced customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Strong customer communication and the ability to credibly explain technical findings, action plans, timing, and alternatives to sophisticated industrial customers.
  • Resourcefulness, forward planning, safety orientation, and ability to source alternate parts, suppliers, rental equipment, and repair paths.

Preferences: 
  • Associates or Bachelors degree in engineering, engineering technology, business  
  • Management of processes and budgets
  • Spanish-English bilingual capability; helpful for Mexico coverage 
  • Direct centrifugal-compressor/PAC experience 
  • Experience with PLCs, controls, microprocessors, event-log retrieval, software revisions, switchgear, or intermediate/high-voltage environments
  • Experience supporting large automotive, aerospace/defense, or other high-value industrial facilities

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Travel up to 50% with overnight stays; Company vehicle and gas card is provided. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling. It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requiring interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to outdoor environments, mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.

Pay Range: Total pay range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $125,000 - $160000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

The Field Service Manager, is a supervisory position that is is a highly visible leadership role supporting Ingersoll Rand’s – Plant Air Centrifugal (PAC) compressed air business across California and Arizona. Working with major manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, and defense customers, this leader becomes a trusted resource when equipment reliability, uptime, and fast technical decisions matter most.

You’ll lead and develop a team of PAC Field Service Technicians responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing sophisticated centrifugal compressed air systems. Just as importantly, you’ll help build the next generation of the regional service team through recruiting, hands-on coaching, technical training, and technician development. This is not a desk-only leadership role. The right candidate brings technical credibility, strong people leadership, and confidence in front of customers. You’ll work alongside technicians, ask the right diagnostic questions, guide complex troubleshooting, and help identify safe, practical solutions when standard parts or factory support cannot meet a customer’s timeline. 

Direct centrifugal-compressor experience is preferred, but we also welcome candidates with strong backgrounds in industrial electrical systems, switchgear, automation, controls, PLCs, or microprocessor-based equipment who are ready to expand their technical expertise.  Based from Pomona, California, this hybrid position includes approximately 50% regional travel, with some overnight stays. You’ll have the backing of an established global OEM, factory training and certification opportunities, strong engineering and technical resources, and a safety-first culture—along with the opportunity to build a high-performing service team and make a direct impact on some of the region’s most demanding industrial operations.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting the customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
  • Other duties as assigned to support the service business and ensure customer satisfaction.  

Requirements
  • High School diploma or GED with relavant experience.
  • 5+ years’ experience in an industrial sales business setting. 
  • 3+ years’ experience in supervising / managing teams of people, such as a combination of relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Core Competencies 
  • Advanced operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.
  • Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Advanced customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Strong customer communication and the ability to credibly explain technical findings, action plans, timing, and alternatives to sophisticated industrial customers.
  • Resourcefulness, forward planning, safety orientation, and ability to source alternate parts, suppliers, rental equipment, and repair paths.

Preferences: 
  • Associates or Bachelors degree in engineering, engineering technology, business  
  • Management of processes and budgets
  • Spanish-English bilingual capability; helpful for Mexico coverage 
  • Direct centrifugal-compressor/PAC experience 
  • Experience with PLCs, controls, microprocessors, event-log retrieval, software revisions, switchgear, or intermediate/high-voltage environments
  • Experience supporting large automotive, aerospace/defense, or other high-value industrial facilities

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Travel up to 50% with overnight stays; Company vehicle and gas card is provided. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling. It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requiring interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to outdoor environments, mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.

Pay Range: Total pay range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $125,000 - $160000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Title: Marine Assembler

Location: Bentleyville Facility in Charleroi, PA (Gardner Denver Nash - 200 Simko Blvd. Charleroi, PA 15022) 

Pay: $25 - $27 per hour Based on Experience

Shift: 1st Shift (6:30am - 3:00pm)

 

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.   

 

Job Overview: 
This position involves building multiple new construction models along with the teardown, evaluation and repair of used equipment.  Products consist of various tank mounted systems, priming valves, and commercial pumps.  Product assembly requires the setting of heavy equipment on fabricated metal tanks to exacting tolerances.  Product assembly for some models includes making sub level components / assemblies.

 

Responsibilities: 

  •  Assemble units consisting of pumps, motors, exchangers, separators, and piping from engineering schematics, procedures, and detailed prints.
  • Conduct required acceptance testing for assembled product hydro test, vacuum test, performance test, sound test, others test as requested.
  • Assemble various products as required by the customer including pumps, compressors, exhausters, priming valves, and systems. Receive and inspect returned pumps and systems, complete a tear down and evaluation.
  •  Access computer files containing available assembly instructions follow assembly steps to build final assembly that conforms to Nash and its customers' requirements.
  • Read shop packet, pull and pick parts in SAP Warehouse Management, record required part information per job requirements and quality control documentation.  
  • Provide detailed tear down and evaluation reports; identifying the condition of each component, the recommended disposition of each component submit completed tear down reports with detailed descriptions and pictures to provide a basis for repair cost quotation to the customer.
  • Assist in receiving process as needed; measure components to affirm dimensional compliance.
  • Participate in government inspections and audit, as necessary.
  •  Complete hydro testing on incoming parts using fixtures, develop fixture when one is not available. Operate crane and fork truck in order to move equipment to specific areas. Operate machinery and hand tools per their intended purpose. Conduct Cycle Counts.
  •  Follow all safety rules, environmental regulating procedures and utilize required safety equipment when appropriate.

 

Requirements: 

  •  High School Diploma or GED 
  • Must be US Citizen and be able to obtain US Government Security clearances within 6 months of hire.  
  • 1+ years of experience in Blueprint Reading

 

Core Competencies: 

  •  Knowledge of piping systems such as threaded, flanged, socket weld and butt weld fittings.
  •  Ability to conduct visual inspection of components and systems • Ability to hear very slight noise and differentiate the source of the noise
  • Follow instructions from various sources, resolving conflicts through supervision.
  • Ability to identify when there is a need to report suspicious activity.
  • Experience with parts inspection, measuring, and machining is preferred.
  • Ability to lift and maneuverer 50 pounds.

 

Preferences: 
• US Navy or other military background 
• 3+ years experience in setting of heavy equipment, assembly and pipefitting. • Familiar with and ability to utilize all hand tools including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, and steel banding. 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Bentleyville, PA no travel. 

 

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $27.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.  

 

The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Job Overview:
The Compression Systems & Services (CSS) business unit has an opportunity for a Services Product Marketing Manager. This role will report to the Services Sales Enablement Leader and is based in Davidson, NC. The Services Product Marketing Manager will drive services growth through our Direct and Distribution channel partners by creating channel awareness and of our offerings through effective marketing strategies while providing the sales teams with the tools and capabilities to increase their effectiveness in the marketplace. This role will partner closely with two Channel Marketing managers channel while working cross-functionally to help attach to 100% of our customers for life.

 

Responsibilities:

Content Development & Sales Enablement

o Develop and deploy Services Sales Enablement tools and trainings designed to aid our sales professional’s effectiveness and capability

o Promote our array of Services programs by creating compelling content in a variety of media to provide our channels with compelling messages to deliver

o Provide daily pre-sales support to channel sales and service personnel to include product application, selling strategies and market intelligence

Pricing Strategy and Analysis

o Analyze and rationalize pricing across the product portfolios to ensure alignment with business objectives and profitability targets

o Conduct competitive pricing research to benchmark offerings against key competitors and market trends

o Evaluate pricing performance and recommend adjustments based on customer feedback, market dynamics, and product performance.

Inventory Strategy and Analysis

o Conduct inventory and sales analysis to provide monthly forecasting of aftermarket parts and system components.

o Partner with cross-functional teams to lead inventory strategy for New Product Development

o Monitor sales trends to ensure product availability and optimized stock levels.


Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience in sales of marketing, operations, industrial sales or marketing
 

Core Competencies:

  • You have the ability to articulate and define customer value.
  • You are a people leader and enjoy seeing your vision manifest itself in the collective output and growth of the team.
  • You have a natural curiosity and desire to learn.
  • You are collaborative by nature and are comfortable partnering with other functional teams to achieve a common goal.
  • You are self-motivated and accustomed working in a fast pace, self-directed work environment
 

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or engineering
  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Power Point and Office with strong analytical skills.
  • Understands the commercial aspect when interfacing with customers to deliver a solution to meet their needs.
  • Experience with B2B or channel distribution preferred
  • Experience with Sales Force and/or other online platforms
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

· This position will be based in Davidson, NC with some anticipated travel.

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.





Job Overview 

The Contract Manager, North America will support business growth by reviewing, drafting, and negotiating commercial and federal government contracts while protecting Ingersoll Rand from legal, financial, operational, and compliance risk. This role will partner closely with Sales, Customer Care, Finance, Operations, Legal, Compliance, and other stakeholders to deliver practical, timely guidance, strengthen contract governance, and improve the end-to-end contracting process. 

The successful candidate will combine sound judgment, customer focus, attention to detail, and an ownership mindset. The role will also serve as a key resource for U.S. federal contracting matters, including interpretation of applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and agency supplement requirements, management of required clauses and flow-downs, and support for audit-ready contract administration. 

Responsibilities 

•  Review, draft, revise, and negotiate a broad range of customer-facing agreements, including sales contracts, master agreements, purchase orders, non-disclosure agreements, amendments, and other commercial documents, with a focus on enabling growth while appropriately managing risk. 

•  Lead contract review for U.S. federal, state, and municipal government customers, evaluating solicitations, representations and certifications, contract terms, and applicable FAR, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and other agency-specific requirements. 

•  Identify, interpret, and coordinate required government contract clauses and subcontract flow-downs, partnering with Legal, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Finance, Supply Chain, Trade Compliance, Quality, and Operations to confirm obligations are understood and executable. 

•  Advise business partners on federal contracting risks and requirements, including compliance, records, audits, government property, intellectual property and data rights, cybersecurity, domestic sourcing, pricing, changes, claims, disputes, and closeout, as applicable to the contract. 

•  Partner directly with customers and internal stakeholders to negotiate legal terms, resolve contract issues, communicate status, and drive timely decisions and approvals in accordance with company policy and delegated authority. 

•  Maintain and continuously improve standard contract templates, playbooks, clause libraries, policies, approval workflows, and contract management materials, with clear standards for both commercial and government contracting. 

•  Develop and deliver practical training for Sales and other customer-facing teams on contract review requirements, risk identification, escalation protocols, federal contract obligations, and compliant contract administration. 

•  Use data, operating rhythms, and continuous improvement methods to strengthen cycle time, visibility, consistency, recordkeeping, and audit readiness across the contract lifecycle, while supporting disputes, investigations, and corrective actions when needed. 

Requirements 

•  Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience, with 3 or more years of experience reviewing and negotiating commercial contracts, government contracts, or related legal terms and conditions. 

•  Working knowledge of contract law and demonstrated ability to interpret complex contractual requirements, assess risk, and translate legal concepts into practical business guidance. 

•  Experience supporting U.S. federal, state, and municipal contracts or subcontracts, including familiarity with FAR requirements. 

•  Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage confidential information and multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. 

•  Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word and Excel, and experience using contract lifecycle management, ERP, or related business systems. 

Core Competencies 

Ownership Mindset: Takes accountability, anticipates risk, and follows through. 

Customer Focus: Enables timely business outcomes with clear, practical guidance. 

Integrity and Judgment: Applies policy consistently and escalates appropriately. 

Continuous Improvement: Simplifies processes and builds scalable, repeatable solutions. 

Collaboration and Influence: Builds trusted partnerships across functions and levels. 

Execution Excellence: Balances pace, detail, and quality across competing priorities. 

Preferences 

•  Experience supporting a manufacturer, industrial business, or other complex, matrixed organization. 

•  Juris Doctor, paralegal credential, contracts certification, or other relevant advanced education or certification.

This role will report to the Services Sales Enablement Leader and is based in Davidson, NC. The Services Product Marketing Manager will drive services growth through our Direct and Distribution channel partners by creating channel awareness and of our offerings through effective marketing strategies while providing the sales teams with the tools and capabilities to increase their effectiveness in the marketplace. This role will partner closely with two Channel Marketing managers channel while working cross-functionally to help attach to 100% of our customers for life.

 

Responsibilities:

Content Development & Sales Enablement

o Develop and deploy Services Sales Enablement tools and trainings designed to aid our sales professional’s effectiveness and capability

o Promote our array of Services programs by creating compelling content in a variety of media to provide our channels with compelling messages to deliver

o Provide daily pre-sales support to channel sales and service personnel to include product application, selling strategies and market intelligence

Pricing Strategy and Analysis

o Analyze and rationalize pricing across the product portfolios to ensure alignment with business objectives and profitability targets

o Conduct competitive pricing research to benchmark offerings against key competitors and market trends

o Evaluate pricing performance and recommend adjustments based on customer feedback, market dynamics, and product performance.

Inventory Strategy and Analysis

o Conduct inventory and sales analysis to provide monthly forecasting of aftermarket parts and system components.

o Partner with cross-functional teams to lead inventory strategy for New Product Development

o Monitor sales trends to ensure product availability and optimized stock levels.


Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience in sales of marketing, operations, industrial sales or marketing
 

Core Competencies:

  • You have the ability to articulate and define customer value.
  • You are a people leader and enjoy seeing your vision manifest itself in the collective output and growth of the team.
  • You have a natural curiosity and desire to learn.
  • You are collaborative by nature and are comfortable partnering with other functional teams to achieve a common goal.
  • You are self-motivated and accustomed working in a fast pace, self-directed work environment
 

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or engineering
  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Power Point and Office with strong analytical skills.
  • Understands the commercial aspect when interfacing with customers to deliver a solution to meet their needs.
  • Experience with B2B or channel distribution preferred
  • Experience with Sales Force and/or other online platforms
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

· This position will be based in Davidson, NC with some anticipated travel.

Location: Mocksville, NC
Schedule: M-F 2nd Shift 1pm-10pm

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
In this role as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of production processes. The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor
Requirements: 

  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • 1+ years of experience using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • 1+ years of experience in advanced engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.
Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Solid understanding of electro-mechanical assembly and machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.   
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering highly preferred. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.
