job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances. 

Job Title: Quality Engineer, Site Lead
Location:  Chicago, IL (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible, hands-on role with site quality lead responsibilities where your work directly impacts product integrity, customer confidence, and manufacturing performance. The Quality Site Lead is responsible for the full range of Quality Engineering support, including quality systems, process improvement, validation, CAPA, auditing, risk assessment, training, and new product introduction support across the Elastomer Chicago manufacturing site. This role has primary ownership of ISO 9001 compliance and supports ISO 13485 medical device silicone operations as needed. It is a strong opportunity for a quality leader who enjoys being close to production, solving problems at the root, partnering across Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership, and building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. The position also leads Quality Technicians and Inspectors, ensuring the team is aligned, audit-ready, and focused on consistent product quality across both industrial and medical device environments.

Responsibilities
Quality Management System / Regulatory Compliance: 
  • Develop, maintain, and execute quality procedures and work instructions to streamline processes and ensure compliance with FDA regulations, ISO standards, and other applicable regulatory requirements.

  • Oversee the development, management, maintenance, and effectiveness of the Elastomer BU Quality Management System, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 compliance.

  • Serve as Management Representative for the Elastomer BU Chicago site.

  • Ensure all SOPs and process documentation are created in accordance with the QMS and partner with departments to ensure effectiveness.

  • Ensure document control and revision control activities are maintained in compliance with QMS and regulatory requirements.

  • Responsible for ensuring all cleanroom requirements are met, as applicable.

Audits, CAPA, NCRs, and Customer Complaints:

  • Host customer and registrar audits and coordinate or perform internal quality and supplier audits as needed.

  • Lead and/or support internal and external CAPAs, NCRs, and customer complaints, including investigation, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and related documentation.

  • Change Control, Documentation, and Product Release

  • Review and assess change requests to ensure proper evaluation of impact on product quality, processes, and regulatory compliance.

  • Manage customer-submitted change requests through completion.

  • Review and approve engineering documentation, including validation protocols/reports, sample run requests, and manufacturing procedures, ensuring adherence to customer and regulatory requirements.

  • Ensure all products conform to validated processes and DMRs; perform lot release and related quality functions.

Production Quality, Process Control, and Continuous Improvement:

  • Assure reliability and consistency of production by monitoring processes and final output.

  • Implement statistical tools, including SPC, MSA, and GR&R, to ensure process control and measurement system reliability.

  • Leverage ISO 9001 continuous improvement principles to improve process efficiency and effectiveness.

  • Monitor key quality metrics and provide regular reporting to leadership.

Supplier Quality and Compliance:
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to co-manage the Approved Supplier List and evaluate suppliers to ensure product compliance.
  • Monitor supplier performance and rate suppliers through scorecard ratings.
  • Calibration, Preventive Maintenance, and Resource Planning
  • Provide oversight of the calibration and preventive maintenance programs to ensure compliance.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify equipment, testing, and resource needs for new or existing products, and communicate requirements to leadership.

Team Leadership, Training, and Talent Management:
  • Achieve quality assurance human resource objectives by recruiting, selecting, orienting, training, scheduling, coaching, counseling, and disciplining employees.
  • Communicate job expectations and lead team talent and performance management processes.
  • Conduct employee training sessions, as applicable.

Professional Development:
  • Maintain current quality management knowledge by studying industry trends, participating in educational opportunities, reading professional publications, and engaging in professional organizations and networking opportunities.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree ideally in industrial, mechanical / manufacturing engineering or similar field
  • 5+ years of significant professional experience in continuous quality improvement with progressive scope and responsibility.
  • 4+ years experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including quality procedures, documentation, audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
  • 3+ years leading teams, ideally in a quality manufacturing environment with proven experience with Good Manufacturing Practices.
  • 2+ years experience with statistical tools, data analysis, SPC, MSA, GR&R, process validation, IQ/OQ/PQ, and root cause analysis.

Core Competencies:
  • Regulatory Quality Leadership: Ability to interpret quality system requirements, maintain audit-ready processes, and guide site compliance in a regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Manufacturing Quality Problem Solving: Strong ability to investigate issues, analyze process variation, identify root cause, and drive practical corrective actions that improve product quality and process performance.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Ability to work effectively across Quality, Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and support production and NPI needs.
  • Team Leadership & Quality Culture: Ability to lead cross-functional teams, drive issue resolution, train, coach, and hold quality team members accountable while reinforcing a culture of compliance, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Quality Systems, Data & Reporting Tools: Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to use quality data, documentation, reports, metrics, and system tools to track performance, support audits, manage corrective actions, and communicate quality trends to leadership.

Preferences:
  • Advanced degree, Engineering degree, or another technical field.
  • Experience working in Master Control QMS System
  • Continuous quality improvement experience in one or more medical product environments.
  • Experience working within an ISO 13485 quality management system, including medical device documentation, audit readiness, CAPA, and regulatory compliance.
  • Experience in silicone or rubber molding, including LSR, compression, or transfer molding.
  • Experience supporting medical device OEM customers.
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR 820 and risk management, including ISO 14971.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Position based onsite in Chicago, IL
  • Work Authorization: US Citizen or Permanent Resident

Pay Range
The base pay range for this role is $80-110k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

job.description:
Job Title: Key Account & Regional Sales Manager – BioPharma Solutions (Canada)
Location: Remote – Canada (Must reside near a major airport)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Travel: Approximately 50–60% (Global Travel Required)
Reports To: Director of Sales


About Us
Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company driven by an ownership mindset and a commitment to making life better for our employees, customers, and communities. Through innovation, sustainability, and customer-focused solutions, we deliver mission-critical technologies across more than 40 trusted brands worldwide.

Job Overview
The Key Account & Regional Sales Manager is a strategic commercial leader responsible for driving profitable growth across Canada while serving as the Global Key Account Manager for one of ILC Dover's most important BioPharma customers. This role combines strategic account management, regional sales leadership, and business development within the life sciences and pharmaceutical manufacturing markets.
The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of key BioPharma accounts throughout Canada while leading the global growth strategy for Johnson & Johnson across its worldwide manufacturing network. The position requires a consultative, relationship-driven sales professional with deep BioPharma industry knowledge, experience navigating complex customer organizations, and a proven ability to influence stakeholders across multiple functions and geographies.
This is a highly visible role that works cross-functionally with sales, engineering, operations, customer service, and executive leadership to drive customer success, revenue growth, and long-term strategic partnerships.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic growth plans for assigned BioPharma customers and regional accounts.
  • Serve as the Global Key Account Manager for Johnson & Johnson, coordinating growth initiatives across approximately 34 global sites.
  • Manage and grow a Canadian territory valued at approximately $3M+ in annual revenue.
  • Establish and strengthen executive-level relationships with decision-makers and influencers at customer organizations.
  • Identify new business opportunities, drive account penetration, and expand existing customer partnerships.
  • Collaborate with Regional Sales Managers globally to implement key account strategies and accelerate growth.
  • Lead customer business reviews, strategic planning sessions, and commercial negotiations.
  • Coordinate internal resources including engineering, operations, technical support, marketing, and customer service to deliver customer solutions.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity pipelines, forecasts, account plans, and customer information within Salesforce.
  • Develop commercial programs including pricing strategies, contract renewals, incentive programs, and NDAs.
  • Resolve customer issues and drive continuous improvement initiatives that support customer operational excellence.
  • Achieve and exceed revenue, profitability, and market-share objectives.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related discipline; equivalent experience considered.
  • 5+ years of direct sales or strategic account management experience.
  • Mandatory experience within the BioPharma, pharmaceutical manufacturing, bioprocessing, or life sciences industry.
  • Proven success managing strategic accounts and driving revenue growth.
  • Experience engaging with executive-level stakeholders within complex customer organizations.
  • Strong business acumen, negotiation skills, and consultative selling capabilities.
  • Experience using Salesforce CRM or similar CRM platforms.
  • Ability to travel extensively throughout Canada, North America, and internationally.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with single-use technologies, bioprocessing solutions, or pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.
  • Global account management experience.
  • Experience managing large enterprise accounts within multi-site organizations.
  • Demonstrated success working across matrix organizations and influencing without direct authority.
  • Bilingual English/French is considered an asset.
Core Competencies
  • Strategic Account Management
  • Executive Relationship Building
  • Business Development & Hunting Mindset
  • Complex Sales & Negotiation
  • Cross-Functional Leadership
  • Customer-Centric Problem Solving
  • Forecasting & Pipeline Management
  • Influence Without Authority
  • Communication & Presentation Skills
  • Organizational & Project Management Skills
Travel & Work Arrangement
  • Home-based remote position within Canada.
  • Approximately 50–60% travel, including customer visits and strategic business meetings.
  • International travel expected 2–4 times annually, primarily throughout North America and EMEA.
  • Candidate must have access to a major airport and be able to travel globally.
What We Offer
  • Competitive Compensation
  • Management Incentive Plan (MIP) Eligibility
  • Comprehensive Benefits Package
  • Retirement Savings Programs
  • Employee Stock Programs
  • Paid Time Off
  • Career Growth Opportunities
  • Inclusive and Collaborative Environment

job.title: Thermal Application Engineer- Data Center
job.description:
Job: Thermal Application Engineer- Data Center
Location: Junction City, OR; or West Chester, PA
  Position Overview

We are seeking a skilled Data Center Thermal Application Engineer to support the design, integration, and deployment of advanced cooling solutions in modern data centers. This role will play a critical part in enabling high-density workloads (AI/ML, HPC) by working closely with Coolant Distribution Unit (CDU), Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and Fan Array/Wall system suppliers to deliver efficient, scalable, and reliable cooling architectures. This position requires strong expertise in liquid cooling systems, airflow management, and system-level thermal integration, along with the ability to collaborate with external partners and internal cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

Thermal Solution Design & Integration

  • Design and implement thermal solutions leveraging liquid cooling (CDUs, direct-to-chip) and high-performance air-cooling systems (Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler, fan walls/arrays)
  • Define system-level cooling architectures integrating CDU loops, facility water systems, and rack-level cooling solutions
  • Evaluate and optimize airflow strategies, including cold aisle/hot aisle containment and fan wall deployment
  • Perform thermal calculations, system sizing, and redundancy planning
 

Supplier Collaboration & Technical Interface

  • Act as the primary technical interface with CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and fan array/wall system suppliers
  • Review vendor designs, specifications, and performance data to ensure alignment with system requirements
  • Drive joint engineering development, validation, and issue resolution with partners
  • Coordinate integration testing, factory acceptance testing (FAT), and site acceptance testing (SAT)
 

Application Engineering & Deployment Support

  • Support site-specific solution design by assessing customer requirements, heat loads, and facility constraints
  • Provide technical guidance during installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting
  • Collaborate with field teams and customers to resolve thermal performance issues and optimize system operation
  • Develop application notes, design guides, and best practices for deployment
 

Modeling, Validation & Optimization

  • Use CFD and system modeling tools (e.g., 6SigmaDCX, ANSYS Icepak, FloTHERM) to validate thermal performance
  • Analyze liquid flow characteristics, pressure drops, and heat exchanger performance
  • Conduct lab and field validation, including thermal testing of CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and airflow systems
  • Continuously improve system efficiency, energy usage (PUE), and reliability
 

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, and data center infrastructure teams
  • Support procurement and quality teams in supplier selection and qualification
  • Contribute to product development and roadmap planning for next-generation cooling solutions
 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience in data center cooling, thermal engineering, or HVAC systems
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of the following:
    • CDUs and liquid cooling systems (direct-to-chip, liquid loops)
    • Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler
    • Fan arrays/walls or large-scale airflow systems
  • Strong understanding of heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and chilled water systems
  • Experience working with external suppliers or OEM partners in a technical capacity
  • Knowledge of ASHRAE TC9.9 guidelines and data center standards
  • Strong communication skills with ability to work across internal teams and external vendors
Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with hyperscale or colocation data center environments
  • Familiarity with AI/HPC high-density rack (>30–100kW+) cooling challenges
  • Knowledge of controls and monitoring of CDU systems (BMS/DCIM integration)
  • Experience in commissioning and field deployment of cooling systems
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or certifications in data center design (CDCDP/CDCS)
  • Proficiency in CFD and thermal simulation tools
 

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong program and project management capability
  • Leadership and influence across matrixed organizations
  • Financial and commercial acumen
  • Risk management and problem-solving
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management
  • High attention to detail and execution discipline
 

 Travel Requirements

  • 25%-40% travel (project sites, factory inspections, FAT/SAT, customer reviews)
 

Why Join Ingersoll Rand

  • Be part of a high-growth, high-impact market powering the digital economy
  • Work in a culture that values ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement
  • Collaborate with a team committed to innovation, operational excellence, and customer success
  • Play a critical role in securing strategic, multi-year platform wins that shape the future of mission-critical infrastructure
 

What We Value at Ingersoll Rand:

  • We think and act like owners. We take accountability, bounce back from setbacks, and operate with a bias for action.
  • We are bold in our aspirations. We tackle hard problems with confidence, humility, and integrity.
  • We foster inspired teams. We embrace diverse perspectives and are committed to equity and inclusion.
  • We are committed to making our customers successful. We aim to be connected for life, delivering essential and mission-critical solutions.



What We Offer

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Ingersoll Rand is committed to achieving workforce diversity reflective of our communities. We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

Title: Senior Maintenance Technician
Location: Chicago, IL (Onsite)
Shift: Day Shift, 4:00 a.m.–12:30 p.m. | Full-Time, Direct Hire
 

Job Overview:

The Senior Maintenance Technician coordinates and performs high-level mechanical, electrical, thermal, and fluid power maintenance on specialized production equipment within a rubber molding manufacturing facility. This role focuses on minimizing machine downtime, diagnosing complex system failures, ensuring compliance with strict safety standards, and mentoring junior technicians. The ideal candidate possesses robust technical knowledge of high-pressure hydraulic presses, steam or electric heating platens, automated control systems, and heavy industrial machinery.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoot, overhaul, and repair multi-stage high-pressure hydraulic molding presses, accumulators, cylinders, directional valves, and proportional pumps.
  •  Diagnose automated machinery inputs/outputs, variable frequency drives (VFDs), industrial sensors, relays, and PLC-controlled systems up to 480V.
  • Read, interpret, and troubleshoot PLC ladder logic.
  •  Inspect, maintain, and repair steam boiler lines, electric heating platens, temperature controllers, hot oil heating units, and cooling water tower circuits.
  • Lead major machinery overhauls, including replacing large bearings, gearboxes, drive shafts, and automated transport mechanisms.
  •  Safely execute heavy rigging to relocate or realign molding presses and equipment.
  •  Execute, document, and optimize preventive and predictive maintenance programs using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
  •  Audit parts inventory and maintain accurate maintenance records.
  •  Lead emergency troubleshooting during active production breakdowns.
  • Assign daily work orders, monitor progress, and mentor junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Adhere to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), NFPA 70E, OSHA, and all company safety procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  •  Perform additional duties as assigned.

Requirements:

  •  Minimum of 5 years of industrial plant maintenance experience.
  • Minimum of 2 years of maintenance experience in a rubber molding, plastic injection molding, or heavy industrial manufacturing environment.
  •  Technical trade school degree, vocational certification, or formal mechanical/electrical apprenticeship preferred.
  • Intermediate Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
  •  Experience troubleshooting Allen-Bradley and Siemens PLCs.
  • Ability to read and interpret hydraulic schematics, electrical wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and pneumatic layouts.
  •  Verified Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) training.
  • Forklift, aerial lift, and overhead crane certifications are preferred.
  •  Proficiency using digital multimeters, insulation testers, hydraulic pressure gauges, precision micrometers, welding equipment, and heavy rigging tools.
 

Core Competencies:

  •  Strong mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and PLC troubleshooting skills.
  •  Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  •  Excellent communication and leadership skills.
  •  Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  •  Commitment to workplace safety and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to mentor and train junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
 

Physical Demands & Working Environment:

  •  Routinely lift, carry, and manipulate materials weighing up to 75 pounds.
  •  Climb ladders, work at heights, crawl into confined spaces, and stand or walk on concrete floors for 8–12-hour shifts.
  • Work around elevated temperatures, steam systems, chemical odors, and high-noise manufacturing environments while wearing required PPE.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This position will be based at our Chicago, IL facility with no anticipated travel. This is a fully site-based position.

 

Pay Range:

Starting pay will range from $40.00–$45.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Title: Sourcing Engineer                
Location: Sedalia, MO 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a highly visible sourcing role where no two days are the same. The Sourcing Engineer will balance forward-looking supply chain improvement with hands-on support of the Sedalia manufacturing operation. Approximately half of the role will focus on strengthening the supply chain and supplier partnerships, while the other half will involve working closely with the materials team to address supplier escalations and help ensure the plant has the components needed to meet production and revenue commitments. The balance will shift as business priorities change, giving this individual exposure to a wide range of challenges and opportunities.

Working across Sedalia’s diverse product lines and active global supply network, the Sourcing Engineer will turn complex data into practical business strategies, build productive supplier relationships, and help navigate issues ranging from delayed materials to broader supply disruptions and resourcing needs. This is not a transactional purchasing position—the individual will serve as a trusted problem-solver who connects suppliers, materials, operations, and other internal partners to keep critical work moving forward.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys variety, thrives on solving new problems, and wants to see the direct impact of their work on both plant performance and long-term supply chain success. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful initiatives within the first few months, expand their knowledge of Sedalia’s products and operations, and grow into a fully integrated member of a collaborative, fast-moving team.

Responsibilities

Cost Reduction & Sourcing Projects
  • Identify, develop, and manage sourcing projects that reduce material costs and achieve savings goals.
  • Analyze spend, purchase price variance, materials, and other data to identify new savings opportunities.
  • Maintain sourcing/savings project tracking and lead cross-functional reviews to drive projects to completion.
  • Track sourcing activity, savings, and performance results to ensure accurate and timely reporting.
Supplier Sourcing & Commercial Negotiations
  • Identify and develop new suppliers and improve the value delivered by existing suppliers.
  • Lead RFP/RFQ activities in partnership with internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate supplier pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and other commercial terms.
  • Monitor purchase price variances and resolve discrepancies with suppliers and internal teams.
Supplier Development & Performance
  • Partner with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts and support sourcing transitions.
  • Address significant or systemic supplier performance issues involving quality, delivery, warranty, cost, or other concerns.
  • Work with suppliers to improve overall performance and support sourcing objectives.
Market Intelligence & Special Projects
  • Monitor commodity pricing, market trends, and domestic/international events that may affect supplier pricing or supply.
  • Participate in special projects and perform additional responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in sourcing, procurement, supply chain, or supplier management.
  • 2+ years of experience negotiating directly with suppliers on pricing, cost increases, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, or other commercial terms.
  • 2+ years of experience analyzing sourcing, spend, pricing, PPV, or supplier data to identify savings opportunities and support business decisions.
  • 2+ years of experience using Excel for data analysis, including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, financial or logical functions, and multiple worksheets/workbooks.
  • 1+ years of experience leading sourcing initiatives, such as RFQ/RFP activities, cost-reduction projects, supplier development, resourcing, or new supplier qualification.

Core Competencies:
  • Cost Optimization & Value Creation – Identifies and drives opportunities to reduce material costs and improve supplier value.
  • Sourcing Project Management – Organizes, tracks, and drives sourcing initiatives from identification through completion.
  • Supplier Development & Performance Management – Builds supplier capability and addresses quality, delivery, warranty, and other performance issues.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Coordinates effectively with internal stakeholders to advance sourcing initiatives, RFPs, and new-part qualification.
  • Commercial & Business Acumen – Understands the business impact of pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and sourcing decisions.
  • Market & Commodity Awareness – Monitors market conditions, commodity trends, and global events that may affect supplier cost or availability.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field
  • Manufacturing sourcing/procurement experience
  • Global and/or Low-Cost-Country sourcing experience
  • SAP or other ERP/MRP experience
  • APICS or similar certification
  • Excel macros

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Minimal travel (<10%), primarily to suppliers if needed.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better.   Job Title: Area Operations Leader

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Edmond, OK

 

About Us  

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

 

Job Summary  

Compression Technologies & Services is hiring for an Area Operations Leader to join our team. This position is responsible for providing the leadership for all activities in the value stream process from the time the customer center receives the purchase order (PO) for an equipment or services sale through PO closure. This position has responsibilities to all processes within that oversight, including service coordination, daily process management, order management, parts inventory and shipment, inside sales, invoicing and collections, and customer satisfaction for 4 customer center locations across Texas & Oklahoma.

 

Responsibilities: 

 

  • Monitor the order management process and identify process improvement opportunities to drive accuracy, efficiency, timeliness, and customer satisfaction.  
  • Collaborate with sales on contract terms and order processing to minimize errors and maximize accuracy and on time delivery.  
  • Collaborate with service to ensure optimal customer experience, parts and resource availability and technician productivity.    
  • Visit customers on a regular basis to understand process challenges and customer requirements.  
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train and develop all inside sales employees.  Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process and technical skills, to the highest degree possible.    
  • Proactively manage the workforce with cross-training and support to manage employee gaps, leveraging strengths and employee skill sets.  
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work, resolving disputes in a timely manner, managing budgets, and increasing utilization of sales support operations team. 
  • Create standard work processes where needed and ensure they are followed. Improve transactional processes impacting the customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
    Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure a safe and productive work environment.  
 

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree required in a related discipline; Engineering, Technical, Marketing or Business preferred.
  • Individual must have a minimum of 7-10 years of experience in industrial product space, preferably with a diverse product portfolio including service offerings.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:  

This position will be based out of one of the regional customer centers in Texas or Oklahoma with regional and overnight, out of town travel required (45-70%).  

 

Key Competencies: 

  • Leadership skills are essential. Individual must have a minimum of 3-5 years management experience; preferably in a customer-facing environment.
  • Work is completed through other employees, so this person must excel at hiring, developing, training, coaching, leading and motivating a diverse workforce for optimal results.
  • Profit & Loss experience is critical. Individual must have experience in forecasting needs, obtaining resources, and managing budgets.
  • A strategic business mindset is important. This individual must be able to support the Regional Director in creation of a strategic business plan to support the growth of the business through internal process improvements and lean strategies to positively impact our market position.
     
What We Offer 

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Title: Sourcing Engineer                
Location: Sedalia, MO 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a highly visible sourcing role where no two days are the same. The Sourcing Engineer will balance forward-looking supply chain improvement with hands-on support of the Sedalia manufacturing operation. Approximately half of the role will focus on strengthening the supply chain and supplier partnerships, while the other half will involve working closely with the materials team to address supplier escalations and help ensure the plant has the components needed to meet production and revenue commitments. The balance will shift as business priorities change, giving this individual exposure to a wide range of challenges and opportunities.

Working across Sedalia’s diverse product lines and active global supply network, the Sourcing Engineer will turn complex data into practical business strategies, build productive supplier relationships, and help navigate issues ranging from delayed materials to broader supply disruptions and resourcing needs. This is not a transactional purchasing position—the individual will serve as a trusted problem-solver who connects suppliers, materials, operations, and other internal partners to keep critical work moving forward.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys variety, thrives on solving new problems, and wants to see the direct impact of their work on both plant performance and long-term supply chain success. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful initiatives within the first few months, expand their knowledge of Sedalia’s products and operations, and grow into a fully integrated member of a collaborative, fast-moving team.

Responsibilities

Cost Reduction & Sourcing Projects
  • Identify, develop, and manage sourcing projects that reduce material costs and achieve savings goals.
  • Analyze spend, purchase price variance, materials, and other data to identify new savings opportunities.
  • Maintain sourcing/savings project tracking and lead cross-functional reviews to drive projects to completion.
  • Track sourcing activity, savings, and performance results to ensure accurate and timely reporting.
Supplier Sourcing & Commercial Negotiations
  • Identify and develop new suppliers and improve the value delivered by existing suppliers.
  • Lead RFP/RFQ activities in partnership with internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate supplier pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and other commercial terms.
  • Monitor purchase price variances and resolve discrepancies with suppliers and internal teams.
Supplier Development & Performance
  • Partner with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts and support sourcing transitions.
  • Address significant or systemic supplier performance issues involving quality, delivery, warranty, cost, or other concerns.
  • Work with suppliers to improve overall performance and support sourcing objectives.
Market Intelligence & Special Projects
  • Monitor commodity pricing, market trends, and domestic/international events that may affect supplier pricing or supply.
  • Participate in special projects and perform additional responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in sourcing, procurement, supply chain, or supplier management.
  • 2+ years of experience negotiating directly with suppliers on pricing, cost increases, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, or other commercial terms.
  • 2+ years of experience analyzing sourcing, spend, pricing, PPV, or supplier data to identify savings opportunities and support business decisions.
  • 2+ years of experience using Excel for data analysis, including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, financial or logical functions, and multiple worksheets/workbooks.
  • 1+ years of experience leading sourcing initiatives, such as RFQ/RFP activities, cost-reduction projects, supplier development, resourcing, or new supplier qualification.

Core Competencies:
  • Cost Optimization & Value Creation – Identifies and drives opportunities to reduce material costs and improve supplier value.
  • Sourcing Project Management – Organizes, tracks, and drives sourcing initiatives from identification through completion.
  • Supplier Development & Performance Management – Builds supplier capability and addresses quality, delivery, warranty, and other performance issues.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Coordinates effectively with internal stakeholders to advance sourcing initiatives, RFPs, and new-part qualification.
  • Commercial & Business Acumen – Understands the business impact of pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and sourcing decisions.
  • Market & Commodity Awareness – Monitors market conditions, commodity trends, and global events that may affect supplier cost or availability.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field
  • Manufacturing sourcing/procurement experience
  • Global and/or Low-Cost-Country sourcing experience
  • SAP or other ERP/MRP experience
  • APICS or similar certification
  • Excel macros

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Minimal travel (<10%), primarily to suppliers if needed.

job.description:
Job Title: Key Account & Regional Sales Manager – BioPharma Solutions (Canada)
Location: Remote – Canada (Must reside near a major airport)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Travel: Approximately 50–60% (Global Travel Required)
Reports To: Director of Sales


About Us
Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company driven by an ownership mindset and a commitment to making life better for our employees, customers, and communities. Through innovation, sustainability, and customer-focused solutions, we deliver mission-critical technologies across more than 40 trusted brands worldwide.

Job Overview
The Key Account & Regional Sales Manager is a strategic commercial leader responsible for driving profitable growth across Canada while serving as the Global Key Account Manager for one of ILC Dover's most important BioPharma customers. This role combines strategic account management, regional sales leadership, and business development within the life sciences and pharmaceutical manufacturing markets.
The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of key BioPharma accounts throughout Canada while leading the global growth strategy for Johnson & Johnson across its worldwide manufacturing network. The position requires a consultative, relationship-driven sales professional with deep BioPharma industry knowledge, experience navigating complex customer organizations, and a proven ability to influence stakeholders across multiple functions and geographies.
This is a highly visible role that works cross-functionally with sales, engineering, operations, customer service, and executive leadership to drive customer success, revenue growth, and long-term strategic partnerships.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic growth plans for assigned BioPharma customers and regional accounts.
  • Serve as the Global Key Account Manager for Johnson & Johnson, coordinating growth initiatives across approximately 34 global sites.
  • Manage and grow a Canadian territory valued at approximately $3M+ in annual revenue.
  • Establish and strengthen executive-level relationships with decision-makers and influencers at customer organizations.
  • Identify new business opportunities, drive account penetration, and expand existing customer partnerships.
  • Collaborate with Regional Sales Managers globally to implement key account strategies and accelerate growth.
  • Lead customer business reviews, strategic planning sessions, and commercial negotiations.
  • Coordinate internal resources including engineering, operations, technical support, marketing, and customer service to deliver customer solutions.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity pipelines, forecasts, account plans, and customer information within Salesforce.
  • Develop commercial programs including pricing strategies, contract renewals, incentive programs, and NDAs.
  • Resolve customer issues and drive continuous improvement initiatives that support customer operational excellence.
  • Achieve and exceed revenue, profitability, and market-share objectives.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related discipline; equivalent experience considered.
  • 5+ years of direct sales or strategic account management experience.
  • Mandatory experience within the BioPharma, pharmaceutical manufacturing, bioprocessing, or life sciences industry.
  • Proven success managing strategic accounts and driving revenue growth.
  • Experience engaging with executive-level stakeholders within complex customer organizations.
  • Strong business acumen, negotiation skills, and consultative selling capabilities.
  • Experience using Salesforce CRM or similar CRM platforms.
  • Ability to travel extensively throughout Canada, North America, and internationally.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with single-use technologies, bioprocessing solutions, or pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.
  • Global account management experience.
  • Experience managing large enterprise accounts within multi-site organizations.
  • Demonstrated success working across matrix organizations and influencing without direct authority.
  • Bilingual English/French is considered an asset.
Core Competencies
  • Strategic Account Management
  • Executive Relationship Building
  • Business Development & Hunting Mindset
  • Complex Sales & Negotiation
  • Cross-Functional Leadership
  • Customer-Centric Problem Solving
  • Forecasting & Pipeline Management
  • Influence Without Authority
  • Communication & Presentation Skills
  • Organizational & Project Management Skills
Travel & Work Arrangement
  • Home-based remote position within Canada.
  • Approximately 50–60% travel, including customer visits and strategic business meetings.
  • International travel expected 2–4 times annually, primarily throughout North America and EMEA.
  • Candidate must have access to a major airport and be able to travel globally.
What We Offer
  • Competitive Compensation
  • Management Incentive Plan (MIP) Eligibility
  • Comprehensive Benefits Package
  • Retirement Savings Programs
  • Employee Stock Programs
  • Paid Time Off
  • Career Growth Opportunities
  • Inclusive and Collaborative Environment

Job Title: Service Supervisor, PAC - Centrifugal Product
Location: Great Lakes Region
(Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend)

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes strongly preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybid / Remote US from Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Travel approximately 40 - 50% with one to two overnight stays per week. 
  • Regular daily travel to customer sites, including work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms 
  • This position will have physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Pay Range: The range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $115,000 - $140,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Job Title: Inside Sales & Service Representative – Rental Coordinator
Location: Pomona, CA

 

 

About Us

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems.

 

Job Summary

This is an Inside Sales & Service Representative – Rental Coordinator position based out of the Pomona, CA Customer Center. This role is responsible for the equipment rental business across 3 Customer Centers in California and Arizona. Responsibilities include establishing and growing rental revenue, profitability, and customer satisfaction.  This role will partner closely with Account Managers and Area Leadership on the development of actions and strategies to drive Rental Services growth and standard work across the region.

 

Responsibilities

  • Act as key customer contact to provide information to customers on rental services from order acceptance through delivery.?
  • Create and manage rental contracts to ensure paperwork is accurate and complete.
  • Accurately enter, manage and balance new equipment sales and service agreements.
  • Partner with branch offices on logistics including dispatching and return of rental assets and coordination of asset transfers between locations.
  • Develop rental business by optimizing rental fleet, building relationships with other rental companies, and partnering with Account Managers to market our fleet to Ingersoll Rand and competitive accounts.
  • Responsible for monthly and quarterly forecasting of rental revenue, rental invoicing, payables for re-rent assets, and periodic reconciliation of rental assets.
  • Develop Area network of freight carriers to reduce dispatch time of rental assets.
  • Partner with Area Service and Operations Leaders to develop standard work around after-hours customer support, quoting, & dispatch of emergency rental requests.
  • Upon return of equipment, ensure timely delivery of receiving, inspection, and servicing of equipment.
  • Achieve operational excellence to improve customer satisfaction and business performance (revenue and profitability), and develop and maintain rental assets KPIs.
  • Ensure environmental health and safety compliance.
  • Serve as a backup to Inside Sales team as needed to include handling inbound customer requests to generate sales of compressed air products, parts, and services.

Job Overview: 
We are seeking a highly skilled, motivated, and results-oriented Sourcing Engineer to support our NASH, Hibon, Fruitland, Excelsior Blower Systems, and Stamford Scientific International  Aeration. The Sourcing Engineer will be a member of our  Process Flow Technologies Sourcing Organization providing Ingersoll Rand with optimal supply assurance, pricing, flexibility, quality, and delivery performance. The Sourcing Engineer builds and leverages strong working relationships with our engineering, operations and quality teams and key suppliers to ensure achievement of cost, quality, and delivery targets, as well as work towards good supplier relationships to achieve maximum results for Ingersoll Rand and our customers.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead negotiations and supplier selection
  • Continuously looks for new savings opportunities through analysis of data (spend, purchase price variance, etc.) and hands on review of materials in the production areas.
  • Leads Request for Proposal (RFP) process with all stakeholders.
  • Works with suppliers and internal team members to qualify new parts.
  • Negotiates key items with suppliers including pricing, payment terms, lead time, and inventory programs.
  • Leads Supplier Development initiative for chronic poor performance suppliers
  • Records and tracks information as required for timely and accurate measure of performance regarding sourcing activities and savings.
  • Support the plants to help local teams efficiently resolve escalated issues.
  • Identify gaps to goals and collaboratively develop and support countermeasures and activities to close the gap and exceed targets.
  • Work to align strategies between commodity and sector localization, plant rationalization and similar
  • Works with suppliers to address significant and/or systemic issues with performance (quality, delivery, warranty, etc.) as may be required in support of plant Manufacturing, Purchasing and Quality teams
  • Responsible for coordinating with commodity teams, materials, operations, engineering, finance, quality, and field operations to complete projects and achieve expected benefits within project timeline.
  • Creates continuous improvement ideation sessions for responsible plants. Generate and evaluate new ideas and opportunities aligned with plant priorities and strategies.
  • Participate in and represent Sourcing function during plant or product Value Analysis/Value Engineering (VAVE) or Major Model Review (MMR) events. Responsible for collecting and communicating commodity actions following event.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned and participates in special projects as required


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering or equivalent.
  • 3+ years of sourcing experience.
  • 1+ years of experience using Microsoft Office, specifically Excel and Word. Proficiency using Excel at an advanced level (use financial and logical functions; work with multiple worksheets and workbooks; edit and use macros/ import and export information) is strongly preferred.


Core Competencies:

  • Incumbent must have well-developed negotiation skills and assessing vendors.
  • Ability to gather, analyze, and interpret data, confirming its accuracy and adequacy, and using it to drive decisions as well as present results and business cases to management.
  • Strategic communication with suppliers through data based decision making & strong negotiation skills.


Preferences:

  • Lean manufacturing related experience.
  • Experience using Oracle or SAP.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite in Sedalia, MO; Springfield, MO; or Bentleyville, PA.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

About ILC Dover
ILC Dover is a global leader in engineered products that protect people, products, and brands. From space exploration and defense systems to pharmaceutical and industrial applications, ILC Dover delivers mission?critical solutions where performance, reliability, and safety matter most. ILC Dover offers competitive compensation and benefits within a collaborative, engineering?driven culture that values innovation, teamwork, and technical excellence.

Job Overview: 
The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of engineering and production programs related to Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key program milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across spacesuit hardware development, integration, and production activities, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to deliver flight-critical hardware on schedule, within scope, and within budget.
This position is based at the Frederica, Delaware manufacturing facility and directly supports the development, assembly, integration, testing, and sustainment of EVA spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer plays a key role in managing the full hardware lifecycle—from design release through fabrication, production, verification, and delivery—ensuring alignment with NASA requirements and strict adherence to human spaceflight safety and quality standards.


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor EVA spacesuit hardware projects from design release through production, integration, and delivery
  • Serve as a liaison between engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment on production priorities, requirements, and schedules
  • Support execution of spacesuit assembly and integration activities at the Frederica site, ensuring readiness for build, test, and delivery
  • Ensure hardware fabrication and production efforts are completed on schedule and within budget constraints
  • Gather and manage technical, manufacturing, and program data to support requirements definition, build readiness, and production execution
  • Lead hardware failure investigations for spacesuit components and assemblies; facilitate root cause analysis (RCA) and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) across engineering and factory operations
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with program managers and stakeholders regarding risks, issues, and impacts to cost, schedule, or technical performance
  • Interface with NASA customers to communicate project status, technical progress, risks, and key milestones through formal reviews, reports, and coordination meetings
  • Support integration, test, and verification activities for EVA hardware, ensuring compliance with NASA program requirements and certification standards
  • Assist with transition of hardware from development into production, including coordination of build plans, work instructions, and configuration control
  • Support project planning activities across proposal, contract execution, and program lifecycle phases for EVA spacesuit programs
  • Conduct routine tasks as directed in support of EVA program execution


*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications:
  • Must be able to access shared government program databases (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field

Core Competencies: 
  • Experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully Site Based in Frederica, DE
  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals.  The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Overview: 

The Production Associate is responsible for performing a variety of tasks to ensure the efficient assembly, inspection, and packaging of products. This role involves working closely with the Production Department to maintain quality standards, organize the workspace, and contribute to the overall success of the manufacturing process. 

 

Responsibilities: 

  • Clean, inspect, and test parts to ensure quality standards are met during product assembly. 

  • Assemble sub-components to create final products in accordance with specifications. 

  • Perform labeling, cleaning, and packaging of assembled products. 

  • Maintain organization and cleanliness within the warehouse and work areas. 

  • Assist with keeping inventory levels of parts and supplies organized and efficiently stocked. 

  • Collaborate with team members to complete assigned tasks and support production goals. 

  • Perform other duties as required by the Production Department. 

 

Requirements 

  • High School Diploma or GED required 

  • 1-2 years of experience in manufacturing, assembly, or warehouse environments

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.
